# Doceree Product Spine Document v1

**Purpose:** Source-of-truth product reference for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center, future AI agents, crawlers, signal-mapping workflows, battlecard automation, and PMM/sales enablement systems.
**Audience:** Internal Product Marketing, Competitive Intelligence, Sales Enablement, AI orchestration, and Codex.
**Status labels used throughout:** *Confirmed* (explicit in source materials), *Inferred* (derived from materials), *Needs confirmation* (unclear or ambiguous).
**Version:** v1 — 26 April 2026.

---

## Section 1 — Executive Summary

Doceree positions itself as an AI-powered operating system for healthcare marketing that connects two sides of the same market: pharmaceutical brands and their agencies on one side, and the owners of healthcare media and clinical-workflow inventory (publishers, EHR vendors, PMS vendors, clinical-screen networks, and health systems) on the other. The platform thesis is that healthcare marketing has historically stopped at awareness, while the actual commercial value sits downstream — at prescribing, dispensing, affordability, and refills. Doceree's product portfolio is built to span the full journey from finding the right HCP to securing the refill at the pharmacy counter.

The portfolio is best understood as a connected platform with point-solution entry points. Any single product can be sold standalone, but the strategic narrative is that they compound: an audience built upstream is activatable downstream; a clinical signal captured at the point of care can fire a sequence across endemic media, virtual rep engagement, affordability surfacing, and adherence loops. The supply-side products own the inventory that the demand-side products run on, which is the mechanical basis for Doceree's "owns both sides of the marketplace" claim.

The overarching customer problem Doceree addresses is fragmentation: pharma brands are forced to stitch together five to seven vendors to cover the HCP and patient journey, and each vendor introduces probabilistic targeting, claims-based lag, walled-garden lock-in, and inconsistent compliance posture. Doceree's response is a unified architecture built on first-party clinical signals, deterministic 1:1 NPI identity, patented real-time triggers, a healthcare-specific contextual taxonomy, and a healthcare-only compliance posture (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2 Type II; HITRUST and POCMA cited in specific products).

Core audience served:
- **Demand-side** — pharmaceutical manufacturers, brand teams, market access, medical affairs, commercial leadership, and healthcare marketing agencies.
- **Supply-side** — healthcare publishers, EHR software vendors, PMS vendors, clinical-screen networks, health systems, and IDNs.

Market category: healthcare-specific marketing technology (MarTech for life sciences), spanning HCP audience intelligence, programmatic awareness, virtual sales engagement, point-of-care marketing, omnichannel orchestration, patient affordability, point-of-dispense marketing, healthcare ad-server / SSP, AI-era publisher monetization, and clinical workflow ad inventory.

What is strategically differentiated about the ecosystem:
- A two-sided platform where demand and supply are owned together rather than partnered.
- A patented, real-time clinical-trigger architecture that fires inside actual workflows (EHR, PMS, clinical screens) rather than on probabilistic exposure.
- An identity layer (ESPYIAN) and a contextual classifier (MeSH Taxonomy) that together enable NPI + context targeting that competitors typically do as either-or.
- An open, anti-walled-garden architecture (BYOP) that augments existing CRM, DSP, and ad stacks rather than replacing them.
- Compliance-from-day-one posture that is healthcare-native, not retrofitted from generic ad-tech.

## Section 4 — Product-by-Product Deep Dive

> Note: Each product card uses the structure requested. All capability claims are grounded in supplied materials. "Approved Claims" are claims that appear supported and are therefore safe to use; "Claims Needing Confirmation" are unclear or unsupported and must be validated before reuse.

### Product 1 — Marketplace

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Audience Matching.
**One-line Product Definition:** A custom-first HCP audience construction platform that builds verified, real-time segments from clinical, behavioral, prescribing, and EHR signals and activates them inside Doceree or in any external DSP.
**Plain-English Explanation:** Instead of buying an off-the-shelf HCP list from a data vendor, a brand uses Marketplace to assemble its own audience based on therapeutic area, diagnosis codes, prescribing behavior, clinical-trial involvement, treatment-line progression, and other live HCP-level signals. The audience can be previewed before commitment and then pushed into Doceree campaigns or to any DSP via LiveRamp.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Upstream definition layer for the rest of the journey. Decides who the brand will engage in Premium Programmatic, NEXT, POC, RepTwin, and POD.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Pre-packaged audience catalogues approximate the audience instead of reflecting brand-specific therapeutic and clinical criteria.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Difficulty incorporating live EHR signals into audience design.
- Limited ability to segment by treatment-line progression, switching behavior, or KOL influence.
- Vendor lock-in when audiences cannot be activated outside the data vendor's platform.

**Primary Buyer:** VP/Director of HCP Marketing, Omnichannel, or Insights & Analytics; agency planning leadership.
**Primary User:** Brand analytics and activation teams; agency planners.
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** Verified HCPs identified via NPI; segmentable by specialty, geography, prescribing pattern, and clinical-behavior signals.

**Key Use Cases:**
- High-volume prescribers within active therapeutic windows.
- Treatment switchers identified through live EHR signals.
- New therapy adopters within a related class within a defined window.
- KOLs influencing peer prescribing in academic networks.
- Adherence-risk populations identified through refill behavior and visit gaps.

**Core Capabilities:**
- Custom audience construction with 50+ HCP attributes.
- 30/60/90-day lookback windows for campaign-moment alignment.
- Real-time EHR signal ingestion across 185+ EHR and health-system integrations.
- Audience preview (size, composition) before commitment.
- Activation in Doceree or any external DSP via LiveRamp.
- Universal Doceree HCP ID for cross-platform activation.
- Privacy-by-design data masking and HIPAA / GDPR / SOC 2 / state-privacy posture.

**Workflow:** Define (clinical, behavioral, demographic, prescribing parameters) → Construct (audience assembled in real time, preview size and composition) → Activate (push to Doceree or any external DSP). *Confirmed.*

**Inputs:** Clinical parameters; HCP-level signals; lookback windows; brand criteria; campaign-moment definition.
**Outputs:** Constructed custom segment; preview metrics; activation token / LiveRamp segment.

**Key Benefits:**
- Custom-built rather than catalogue-selected audiences.
- Live EHR intelligence rather than modeled approximations.
- Build-once, activate-anywhere.
- Privacy-safe with masked HCP IDs and no PII leaving the platform.

**Customer Outcomes:**
- Reduction of audience approximation that drives spend waste.
- Faster movement from segment definition to live activation.
- Higher confidence in audience-to-campaign fit.

**Proof Points:**
- 6M+ verified HCPs available for construction.
- 185+ EHR and health-system integrations underpinning live signal ingestion.
- 50+ HCP attributes available for construction.
- Eight named external data partners on the supply side of Marketplace.

**Approved Claims:**
- Custom-first HCP audience construction platform.
- Live EHR intelligence in audience definition.
- Build once, activate anywhere through LiveRamp.
- Privacy-by-design with masked HCP IDs.

**Claims Needing Confirmation:**
- Specific audience-construction SLA.
- Specific Rx-lift outcomes attributable to Marketplace.
- Pricing model and minimum commitments.
- EU consent posture for activations via LiveRamp.

**Differentiators:**
- Custom-first vs. catalogue-first architecture.
- Live EHR intelligence including major EHR ecosystems.
- Single platform, every HCP datapoint.
- Activation in Doceree or any external DSP via LiveRamp.

**Competitor Categories:**
- HCP audience data and identity vendors.
- Healthcare DSPs that bundle audiences with their own activation only.
- Data clean rooms and audience clouds (adjacent).

**Competitive Threat Signals:**
- Competitor launches a "custom audience builder" product.
- Competitor adds live EHR data to its audience offering.
- Competitor announces a LiveRamp / cross-DSP activation partnership.
- Competitor publishes case studies built around Rx lift from custom audience design.
- Competitor hires for "HCP identity," "audience engineering," or "real-time clinical data" roles.
- Competitor adds release notes describing 30/60/90-day lookbacks.
- Competitor exec posts about "moving away from off-the-shelf segments."

**Sales Objections This Product May Face:**
- "We already buy from IQVIA / Komodo / Definitive."
- "Custom audiences take too long to build."
- "Our DSP already has its own audience builder."
- "We need Rx attribution, not just audience design."

**Battlecard Sections This Product Needs:**
- Custom vs. catalogue audience comparison.
- LiveRamp activation breadth.
- HCP identity and EHR-data freshness comparison.
- Privacy / consent posture comparison.
- Cross-product handoff narrative (Marketplace → Premium Programmatic / NEXT / POC / POD).

**Messaging Pillars:**
- From off-the-shelf to purpose-built.
- Live, not modeled.
- One platform, every datapoint.
- Build once, activate anywhere.
- Privacy at every step.

**Key Phrases / Language to Preserve:**
- Custom-First, not Catalogue-First.
- Live EHR Intelligence.
- Build Once, Activate Anywhere.

**Terms to Avoid or Validate:**
- Specific accuracy benchmarks vs. competitors.
- Rx-lift guarantees.
- "World's largest HCP marketplace."

**Dependencies / Integrations:**
- LiveRamp (external DSP activation).
- 150+ EHR integrations.
- Universal Doceree HCP ID.
- Eight named external data partners on the supply side.

**Data or Measurement Claims:**
- Audience preview metrics (size, composition).
- Downstream measurement flows through the activation product (Premium Programmatic, NEXT, POC, POD).

**Open Questions:**
- Pricing structure.
- Audience-construction SLA.
- Refresh cadence per attribute.
- Whether Marketplace and audience scoring are bundled or separately priced.

### Product 2 — ABM (Account-Based Marketing)

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Account Influence.
**One-line Product Definition:** Healthcare-purpose-built ABM that delivers hyper-personalized, intent-led messages to the multi-stakeholder buying groups inside hospitals, IDNs, academic centers, specialty pharmacies, and clinics.
**Plain-English Explanation:** Instead of marketing to individual doctors, ABM targets entire institutions — and within those institutions, the clinical, non-clinical, and value decision-makers who collectively drive adoption. It uses IP-based, contextual-keyword, geolocation, and B2B intent layers, and measures account-level lift against a pre-campaign baseline.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Adds an institutional-influence layer above HCP-level activation, particularly for specialty / hospital-administered therapies and for situations where formulary, P&T, or VAC dynamics matter.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Institutional adoption requires alignment across many stakeholders; generic B2B ABM platforms are not healthcare-native and lack endemic, EHR, or clinical-context capabilities.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Difficulty differentiating in a saturated healthcare market.
- Generic messaging that fails to resonate with role-specific stakeholders.
- Lack of healthcare-specific account-lift measurement.

**Primary Buyer:** Strategy / Engagement Strategy leadership; Digital Investment Directors; Programmatic VP/SVP/EVP; HCP Media Planning; Head of Media.
**Primary User:** Pharma campaign managers; agency planners and programmatic ops.
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** Clinical decision-makers (Medical Directors, CMOs, Department Heads, Nursing Leads), non-clinical decision-makers (Procurement, CFOs, Compliance), and value decision-makers (Pharmacy & P&T Directors, Population Health, Value & Quality), across five leadership levels (C-Suite through Staff & Specialists).

**Key Use Cases:**
- Specialty / hospital-administered launch campaigns.
- P&T committee and formulary influence campaigns.
- Multi-stakeholder cross-departmental engagement at named IDNs.
- Reaching VACs and procurement early to reduce buying delays.
- Strengthening relationships with key strategic accounts.

**Core Capabilities:**
- Four targeting layers: IP-based, MeSH keyword (7M+ medical terms), geolocation, B2B search intent.
- Role-based messaging across eight departments and five leadership levels.
- Account-lift measurement against a pre-campaign Brand.com Pixel baseline.
- DCO (dynamic creative optimization) — *Inferred as upcoming.*
- Brand.com Pixel for first-party HCP activation — *Inferred as upcoming.*

**Workflow:** Identify (account list, IP/domain, firmographic enrichment, intent analysis, role insights) → Target (programmatic activation, account-based bidding, contextual alignment, endemic and non-endemic delivery) → Measure (pre/post traffic, account lift, reach and penetration, visit frequency). *Confirmed.*

**Inputs:** Target account list (company name, domain, geography); MLR-approved creative; tracking parameters; brand objective and KPIs.
**Outputs:** Account-level traffic and engagement; account lift; penetration metrics; stakeholder engagement quality.

**Key Benefits:**
- Healthcare-native ABM rather than generic B2B ABM repurposed for healthcare.
- Combined IP + context targeting in one platform.
- Role-based at institutional scale.
- Account-lift measurement that proves business impact.

**Customer Outcomes:**
- Increase in target-account website traffic and penetration.
- Faster movement of stakeholder buying groups.
- Reduced wasted spend on generic targeting.

**Proof Points:**
- 100K+ healthcare accounts addressable.
- 100B+ monthly intent signals.
- 10K+ intent categories.
- 7M-keyword medical taxonomy.
- Documented account-traffic uplifts on launch campaigns. *Inferred from materials; outcomes are illustrative not guaranteed.*

**Approved Claims:**
- Healthcare-native ABM rather than generic B2B repurposed.
- IP and context targeting combined.
- Role-based at scale across departments and leadership levels.
- Account-lift measurement against pre-campaign baseline.

**Claims Needing Confirmation:**
- Specific outcome guarantees (account lift % cannot be guaranteed).
- "Only platform that does X" wording for ABM specifically.
- Battlecard line referencing "POC compliance" inside ABM material — likely a templating error.
- DCO and Brand.com Pixel go-live dates and feature scope.

**Differentiators:**
- Healthcare-native infrastructure (endemic publishers, EHR adjacency, MeSH).
- IP + context together rather than either-or.
- Eight departments × five leadership levels role-based targeting.
- Pre-vs-post account-lift measurement.

**Competitor Categories:**
- Generic B2B ABM platforms.
- Healthcare DSPs claiming account-level targeting.
- Healthcare data vendors that pair with separate activation platforms.

**Competitive Threat Signals:**
- B2B ABM competitor adds healthcare vertical or HIPAA module.
- Competitor announces medical-publisher integrations or endemic access.
- Competitor adds intent data sourced from medical-content sites.
- Competitor hires for "healthcare ABM," "HCP account targeting," or "P&T committee engagement."
- Competitor publishes case study with hospital / IDN account lift outcomes.
- Competitor announces partnership with KickFire / Bombora / Definitive Healthcare equivalents.
- Competitor exec posts on "B2B ABM for life sciences."
- Competitor adds release notes for IP + keyword combined targeting.

### Product 5 — Point-of-Care (POC)

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Clinical Decision.
**One-line Product Definition:** Real-time clinical-trigger messaging delivered inside the EHR at the moment of prescribing, with patented multi-condition Triggers, ESPYIAN identity, ABRB rule-building, and 86–93% NPI match by therapeutic area.
**Plain-English Explanation:** When an HCP enters a diagnosis, orders a test, or writes a prescription inside their EHR, POC fires a clinically relevant, patient-specific brand message right there in the workflow. The product owns the full tech stack (DSP + SSP + Ad Server + DMP) and integrates directly with EHR systems rather than relying on aggregated claims data.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Owns the clinical-decision moment — the point at which marketing has the highest opportunity to influence the prescription. Acts as an upstream trigger source for connected journeys to Premium Programmatic, RepTwin, co-pay.com, and POD.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Marketing must reach HCPs at the actual prescribing decision, not 30–90 days later via claims data, and not via probabilistic third-party identity.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Single-rule simplicity in legacy POC tools cannot reflect multi-condition clinical scenarios.
- Manual targeting-rule construction is slow and error-prone.
- Affordability information is typically discovered too late.
- Probabilistic targeting wastes spend on wrong HCPs.

**Primary Buyer:** Strategy / Engagement Strategy; Digital Investment Director; Programmatic VP/SVP/EVP; HCP Media Planning; Managing Director; Head of Media; Integrated Planning.
**Primary User:** Brand campaign managers; HCPs (message recipients).
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** 6M+ verified HCPs across 45+ specialties; 3M+ monthly patient decision moments.

**Key Use Cases:**
- Multi-condition oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, and rare-disease targeting (e.g., HER2+ breast cancer adjuvant; T2D HbA1c >8% on metformin monotherapy; MDS hematologists with specific IPSS-R scoring).
- Insurance-coverage-conditioned messaging across five categories and 70+ payers.
- Competitor-NDC intercepts and brand-defense plays.
- Rep-visit, sample-request, financial-assistance, clinical-trial, and DAW messaging formats.
- Connected omnichannel sequences orchestrated via NEXT.

**Core Capabilities:**
- Patented multi-condition Triggers fired on live ICD-10, CPT, NDC, clinical indicators, HCP demographics, payer/coverage events.
- ABRB (Automatic Business Rule Builder) auto-generates targeting rules and aggregates NDC variants in minutes.
- ESPYIAN identity with 86–93% NPI match by therapeutic area.
- Five messaging formats: Display, RepTwin, DAW (Dispense As Written), Co-pay coupons (auto-applied), plus Clinical/Drug-Related, Rep-Visit, Financial Assistance, Sample Request, Clinical Trial messaging.
- Real-time 24/7 dashboards and weekly Physician-Level Data; Creative Analytics post-campaign.
- Ownership of the full tech stack (DSP + SSP + Ad Server + DMP via ESPYIAN).

**Workflow:** Patient intake (demographics, vitals, insurance) → diagnostic test (HCPCS / CPT) → diagnosis entry (ICD-10) → medication review (NDC) → e-prescribing (NDC) → physician notes (DAW). *Confirmed.*

**Outputs:** In-EHR messages; weekly Physician-Level Data (NRx / TRx); Creative Analytics; ABRB optimisation recommendations.

### Product 6 — NEXT (Orchestration)

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Orchestration.
**One-line Product Definition:** AI-powered omnichannel orchestration platform that activates the right message across every channel at the moment of clinical decision, using Dynamic Audiences, Clinical Intent Triggers, Dynamic Content Selection, and BYOP.

### Product 7 — Clinical Intent Signals (CIS)

**Status:** Confirmed (with positioning ambiguity — see Open Questions).
**Journey Stage:** Orchestration / Measurement (cross-product).
**One-line Product Definition:** A unified intelligence layer that combines clinical, behavioral, and engagement signals into a per-NPI prescriber-readiness score; activatable inside NEXT or Marketplace and syndicatable to a brand's external CRM / DSP / CDP.
**Plain-English Explanation:** CIS merges three streams of HCP signal — what's happening in the EHR, what HCPs are reading and researching across publishers, and how they respond to channels — into one real-time score per physician. The score reflects how close that HCP is to prescribing, and brands can act on it inside Doceree or send it to their existing stack.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Provides the decisioning fuel that makes NEXT smart and that allows Marketplace audiences and external DSP campaigns to be prioritised on actual prescribing readiness.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Signals are siloed across EHR, CRM, and publishers; static targeting misses prescribing windows; campaigns optimise on the wrong signals.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Latency between clinical reality and marketing response.
- Cross-channel fatigue and inefficient retargeting.
- Inability to attribute movement at the decision-stage level.

**Primary Buyer:** Pharma omnichannel; brand analytics; agency strategy.
**Primary User:** Brand analytics teams; agency strategists; activation operators.
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** Verified HCPs scored at the NPI level for prescribing readiness within a brand's universe.

**Key Use Cases:**
- Real-time scoring of brand-defined NPI universes.
- Cross-channel activation prioritisation in NEXT.
- Marketplace audience scoring for activation in external DSPs.
- CRM / CDP enrichment for sales and rep prioritisation.
- Decision-stage progression measurement.

**Core Capabilities:**
- Five signal streams: Clinical & Contextual (EHR), Behavioral (publisher activity), Cross-Channel Engagement (ads, email, web, rep), Historical Performance Patterns, Brand-Owned Data.
- Real-time scoring per impression and per signal event.
- Activation paths: NEXT (native), Marketplace (data syndication), CRM / CDP (data lands in brand stack), DSPs (activate externally).
- Privacy-by-design — de-identified at NPI level; HIPAA-certified, GDPR-compliant; MLR-aware.

**Outputs:** Per-NPI prescriber-readiness score; segment movement patterns; decision-stage probability; live optimisation recommendations.

### Product 8 — co-pay.com (manufacturer-facing)

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Access and Activation.
**One-line Product Definition:** End-to-end therapy-access platform inside the EHR — Real-Time Benefit Check, automated electronic prior authorization, and AI-driven enrollment via copay twin — priced on activation and tied to confirmed therapy starts.
**Plain-English Explanation:** When the prescriber writes a script in the EHR, co-pay.com surfaces patient-specific cost and savings, automatically triggers and clears prior authorization across PBMs, and runs the patient through enrollment via an AI agent (copay twin). Manufacturers stop paying for awareness and start paying when the therapy actually starts.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Removes the cost and access barrier between the prescription and the filled script, closing the gap that downstream POD then defends. Manufacturer-funded; the same platform also surfaces to providers as co-pay.com for Health Systems.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Most co-pay program spend never converts to a filled prescription because of enrollment friction and prior-authorization delay; affordability arrives too late.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Manual hub-team workload on enrollment and PA follow-up.
- Lack of channel ROI tied to actual therapy starts.
- Patient-side abandonment due to surprise out-of-pocket cost.

**Primary Buyer:** Pharma brand teams; market access; patient services / hub.
**Primary User:** HCPs at prescribing; patients during enrollment; hub teams.
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** HCPs across 185+ EHR & health-system integrations; patients enrolled via Brand.com or co-pay.com.

**Key Use Cases:**

- copay twin AI enrollment agent (same flow on Brand.com or co-pay.com).
- Multi-channel distribution of co-pay messages (SMS, email, portal, print).
- Activation analytics dashboard (funnel, drop-off, PA-clearance, time-to-activation).

**Workflow:** Medication selected in EHR → RTBC surfaces savings and coverage → ePA triggered automatically and submitted to all PBMs → co-pay message delivered in workflow → copay twin enrolls patient → card active. *Confirmed.*

**Inputs:** EHR chart data, patient eligibility, brand co-pay program rules, PBM forms, consent capture.
**Outputs:** Activated cards, PA approvals, therapy starts, channel ROI tied to therapy starts, audit-ready consent timestamps.

### Product 9 — Point-of-Dispense (POD)

**Status:** Confirmed.

### Product 10 — Audience Quality Score (AQS)

**Status:** Confirmed.
**Journey Stage:** Cross-product (audience prioritisation; works across Marketplace, Premium Programmatic, POC, NEXT, POD).
**One-line Product Definition:** Proprietary 0–100 scoring system that predicts how likely an HCP is to prescribe a specific pharmaceutical product, with separate methodologies for current and potential prescribers and tiered budget guidance.
**Plain-English Explanation:** Instead of treating every HCP on the list as equally valuable, AQS scores each one and puts them in High, Moderate, or Low tiers — with explicit budget allocation guidance per tier and validation against actual Rx-lift outcomes.
**Strategic Role in Doceree Platform:** Cross-product capability that makes any HCP list — built in Marketplace or imported from a third-party data vendor — actionable by ranking HCPs on prescribing likelihood and recommending budget allocation accordingly.
**Primary Customer Problem:** Budget waste on low-likelihood HCPs; no consistent quality grading across vendors; brands cannot quickly distinguish high-volume prescribers from high-quality prescribers.
**Secondary Problems Solved:**
- Inability to find new prescribers efficiently.
- Difficulty quantifying the value of competitor-loyalist conversion.
- Lack of validated, predictive scoring against actual Rx outcomes.

**Primary Buyer:** Pharma brand teams; market analytics; agency planners.
**Primary User:** Audience strategists; brand analytics teams; agency planners.
**Target Audience Reached by the Product:** Verified HCPs at the NPI level; supports both current-prescriber retention and potential-prescriber acquisition.

**Key Use Cases:**
- Filter and refine an existing list to lift average AQS.
- Generate lookalike audiences seeded on top performers.
- Prioritise budget on High tier (60–70%) vs. Moderate (20–30%) vs. Low (5–10%).
- Score competitor lists (e.g., from IQVIA / Komodo) to recommend who to invest behind.
- Strategic plays: competitive switching, whitespace expansion, launch readiness, HCP reactivation, cost-per-Rx optimisation.

**Core Capabilities:**
- Dual methodology: Current Prescriber AQS (4 dimensions — Brand Affinity, Manufacturer Affinity, Competitor Affinity, Patient Reach) and Potential Prescriber AQS (5 predictive signals — clinical behavior patterns, specialty / sub-specialty, geography & practice setting, competitor prescribing activity, manufacturer relationship history).
- Tiered guidance: High (75–100), Moderate (50–74), Low (<50) with budget allocation recommendations.
- Continuous validation against Rx-lift outcomes.
- Independence — does not use Doceree ad-impression history.
- 1-click activation in Doceree platform.

**Workflow:** Upload NPI list → AQS scores returned in real time (Overall, Current, Potential, tier distribution) → optimise (filter, lookalike, add high-AQS Potentials, refine) → activate via Doceree or external DSP. *Confirmed.*

**Inputs:** NPI list; campaign objective; budget parameters; success metrics.
**Outputs:** Per-NPI AQS (Overall, Current, Potential); tier distribution; budget recommendation; lookalike seed.

**Key Benefits:**
- Vendor-agnostic — scores any HCP list.
- Validated against Rx outcomes, not just engagement.
- Actionable in 1 click.
- Privacy-first (HIPAA / SOC 2 / GDPR / CCPA).

**Customer Outcomes:**
- Improved Rx lift on High tier vs. Low tier.
- More efficient new-prescriber acquisition.
- Faster time-to-peak on launches.
- Reduced cost-per-Rx via tier-based budget reallocation.

**Proof Points:**
- Dual methodology with separate behavioral and predictive scoring.
- Validation cadence (quarterly model refinement).
- HIPAA / SOC 2 / GDPR / CCPA compliance.
- Documented common-use-case results across competitive switching, whitespace expansion, launches, reactivation, budget optimisation, and lookalike modelling.

**Approved Claims:**
- Proprietary 0–100 scoring system for HCP prescribing likelihood.
- Dual methodology for current and potential prescribers.
- Validated against real Rx-lift outcomes.
- Vendor-agnostic — scores any uploaded HCP list.

**Claims Needing Confirmation:**

**Differentiators:**
- Dual methodology (behavioral vs. predictive).
- Instant 1-click activation inside Doceree.
- Continuous Rx-lift validation.
- Vendor-agnostic scoring.

## Section 5 — Product Relationship Map

| Product A | Related Product B | Relationship Type | How They Connect | Why This Matters for PMM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marketplace | Premium Programmatic | Upstream → downstream | Audiences built in Marketplace activate inside Premium Programmatic. | Lets PMM tell a "build once, activate anywhere" narrative. |
| Marketplace | NEXT | Upstream → downstream | NEXT orchestrates campaigns against Marketplace-built audiences. | Reinforces the cross-product orchestration story. |
| Marketplace | POC | Upstream → downstream | Audiences scoped in Marketplace inform POC trigger configurations. | PMM can frame POC as the activation layer over Marketplace audiences. |
| Marketplace | POD | Upstream → downstream | Audiences and segments inform pharmacy-side targeting. | Ties demand-side audience to dispense-side action. |
| ABM | Premium Programmatic | Sequential workflow | ABM identifies institutional accounts; Premium Programmatic delivers in-account awareness on endemic publishers. | Allows agencies to bundle account influence with HCP awareness. |
| ABM | NEXT | Same campaign workflow | ABM signals can feed NEXT's orchestration logic at the institutional level. | Cross-sell narrative for institutional-grade orchestration. |
| Premium Programmatic | RepTwin | Same campaign workflow | RepTwin is an ad format inside Premium Programmatic display. | Single bundled motion lets brands buy awareness + interaction together. |
| Premium Programmatic | Content Marketing | Same product family | Content Marketing is a sub-format within Premium Programmatic. | Sales should not position them as separate products. |
| Premium Programmatic | NEXT | Sequential journey | Premium Programmatic delivers awareness; NEXT orchestrates the next-best-action. | PMM can frame NEXT as the brain over Premium Programmatic. |
| Premium Programmatic | POC | Cross-stage relationship | POC triggers can drive Premium Programmatic retargeting. | Connected-journey messaging. |
| RepTwin | POC | Same audience, different surface | RepTwin appears as a messaging format inside POC. | Sales should explain how a single brand rep can extend across endemic and EHR. |
| RepTwin | Publisher AI Suite | Cross-product reuse | RepTwin powers the Virtual Brand Rep ad format inside Publisher AI Suite. | Demonstrates platform reuse across demand and supply. |
| RepTwin | NEXT | Same orchestration layer | RepTwin sequences are orchestrated through NEXT. | Allows NEXT to be the single orchestration narrative. |
| POC | NEXT | Same orchestration layer | POC events drive NEXT's real-time decisions and downstream channel activation. | Anchors the platform-level orchestration story. |
| POC | co-pay.com | Sequential workflow | POC drives prescribing context; co-pay.com surfaces affordability inside the EHR. | Explains how Doceree closes the access gap inside the same workflow. |
| POC | POD | Sequential journey | POC influences prescribing; POD secures the dispense decision. | The full prescribe-to-fill narrative. |
| NEXT | CIS | Platform connection | NEXT activates CIS scores; CIS drives NEXT's decisions. | Enables PMM to position CIS as either standalone or NEXT-bundled. |
| CIS | Marketplace | Same audience layer | CIS scores can be syndicated into Marketplace audiences. | Reinforces the modular activation narrative. |
| CIS | POC, RepTwin, POD | Cross-product measurement | CIS unifies signals across POC, RepTwin, and POD into a single readiness score. | Lets the analytics narrative span the journey. |
| co-pay.com | POD | Sequential journey | co-pay.com clears affordability and PA before pharmacy; POD secures the fill at the counter. | The end-to-end "first fill" narrative. |
| co-pay.com (manufacturer) | co-pay.com for Health Systems | Same product, two motions | Same activation flow with two go-to-market narratives — manufacturer-funded, health-system delivered. | Sales should not present them as separate platforms. |
| co-pay.com | Spark for EHRs | Same audience / supply surface | The EHR vendor partner hosts co-pay.com modules inside its workflow. | Demonstrates supply-and-demand integration on a single inventory unit. |
| AQS | Marketplace | Cross-product capability | AQS scores any Marketplace-built audience. | Allows PMM to frame Marketplace audiences as quality-graded by default. |
| AQS | Premium Programmatic, POC, NEXT, POD | Cross-product capability | AQS scores feed activation prioritisation across the demand-side products. | Tells a budget-efficiency story across the platform. |
| Admanager | Premium Programmatic | Supply ↔ demand | Admanager is the supply for Premium Programmatic display and Content Marketing. | Anchors the two-sided platform claim. |
| Admanager | Publisher AI Suite | Same buyer, different use case | Same publisher integrates both — Admanager monetises existing inventory, Publisher AI Suite future-proofs against AI-search erosion. | Cross-sell motion for the publisher account. |
| Publisher AI Suite | RepTwin | Cross-product reuse | RepTwin is the Virtual Brand Rep ad format inside AI Ads. | Connects supply-side AI Ads to demand-side virtual rep narrative. |
| Spark for EHRs | POC | Supply ↔ demand | Spark for EHRs is the publisher-side product running on EHR inventory; POC is the demand-side product targeting it. | Two-sided platform narrative inside the EHR. |
| Spark for EHRs | co-pay.com for Health Systems | Same supply surface | Both surface inside EHR workflows; both are health-system-friendly. | Cross-sell to the same EHR-vendor / health-system buyer. |
| Spark for DOOH | Premium Programmatic | Same campaign workflow | Pharma demand bought via Premium Programmatic can run on Spark-for-DOOH inventory. | Cross-channel narrative within the awareness journey stage. |
| Spark for Pharmacy | POD | Supply ↔ demand | Spark for Pharmacy is the publisher-side product running on PMS inventory; POD is the demand-side product. | Two-sided platform narrative at the pharmacy. |
| co-pay.com for Health Systems | Spark for EHRs | Cross-sell within supply-side | Same EHR-vendor / health-system buyer. | One-account, multi-product motion. |

**Narrative — how the platform should be presented as connected**

Doceree should be presented as a connected operating system rather than a menu of point solutions. Pharma brands enter at any stage of the journey — audience matching, account influence, awareness, interaction, clinical decision, orchestration, access, or adherence — and can extend the same audience, identity, signal, and creative through every subsequent stage. Supply-side products own the inventory the demand-side products run on, which is the basis for the two-sided platform narrative. Cross-product capability layers (AQS, CIS, ESPYIAN, Triggers, MeSH, BYOP, OneHCP) act as the connective tissue: AQS prioritises any HCP list; CIS unifies signals across products; ESPYIAN provides the deterministic identity; Triggers fire across EHR, PMS, and clinical screens; MeSH gives shared contextual classification across endemic media and ABM; BYOP keeps the platform open; OneHCP handles publisher-side authentication. PMM should pitch this connected architecture rather than individual products in most enterprise contexts.

## Section 7 — Competitive Signal Mapping Rules

> Format: each rule defines a signal pattern and the Doceree product(s) the signal should map to.

**Rule 7.1 — Custom HCP audience launches**
If a competitor signal mentions launching, repositioning, or adding capability around custom HCP audience construction, live EHR audience signals, or LiveRamp-style cross-DSP audience activation, then map it to **Marketplace** and secondarily to **AQS**, because the overlap is upstream audience definition. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.2 — Healthcare ABM moves**
If a competitor signal mentions IP-based hospital / IDN targeting, healthcare-vertical ABM, P&T or VAC committee marketing, or Bombora-like healthcare-intent integration, then map it to **ABM** and secondarily to **NEXT** (when the signal involves orchestration). Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.3 — Endemic publisher / contextual targeting moves**
If a competitor signal mentions adding endemic medical publishers, healthcare contextual taxonomy, NPI + context targeting, AI virtual rep ad format, content marketing for HCPs, or keyword-level reporting, then map it to **Premium Programmatic** and (when the signal touches AI rep format) also to **RepTwin**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.4 — Pharma agentic AI moves**
If a competitor signal mentions an MLR-aware AI agent for HCPs, multimodal AI rep, video / voice / chat AI for pharma, brand-trained closed-system AI, or LOE / SMB pharma AI rep, then map it to **RepTwin**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.5 — In-EHR clinical messaging moves**
If a competitor signal mentions EHR-triggered HCP messaging, real-time ICD-10 / CPT / NDC triggers, prescribing-moment communication, multi-condition clinical scenarios, or POCMA-style certification, then map it to **POC** and secondarily to **NEXT** if orchestration is implied. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.6 — Omnichannel orchestration / clinical-intent moves**
If a competitor signal mentions HCP omnichannel orchestration, clinical intent, prescriber-readiness scoring, BYOP-style activation tags, or anti-walled-garden positioning, then map it to **NEXT** and **Clinical Intent Signals**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.7 — Patient access / ePA / RTBC moves**
If a competitor signal mentions Real-Time Benefit Check, automated electronic prior authorization, AI patient enrollment, performance-based affordability pricing, or in-workflow co-pay surfacing, then map it to **co-pay.com (manufacturer)** and **co-pay.com for Health Systems**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.8 — Pharmacy / PMS moves**
If a competitor signal mentions pharmacy management system messaging, real-time NDC trigger, native PMS embedding, auto-applied co-pay at billing, deterministic NPI-to-claim attribution, or SMS adherence loops without an app, then map it to **POD** and **Spark for Pharmacy**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.9 — Healthcare ad-server / publisher monetization moves**
If a competitor signal mentions a healthcare-exclusive ad server, HCP-identity-based publisher monetization, or healthcare publisher demand pool, then map it to **Admanager**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.10 — Publisher AI / anti-scraping moves**
If a competitor signal mentions a site-specific LLM for publishers, AI Ads inside chat, tokenised content licensing for AI developers, bot-paywall infrastructure, or HCP authentication SSO, then map it to **Publisher AI Suite**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.11 — EHR-vendor partnership moves**
If a competitor signal mentions an EHR-vendor partnership for in-workflow pharma messaging, SMART on FHIR clinical module, or co-pay / drug education / trial-recruitment modules, then map it to **Spark for EHRs**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.12 — DOOH clinical-screen moves**
If a competitor signal mentions clinical-screen DOOH targeting, real-time patient triggers from EHR check-in, no-hardware DOOH integration, or premium CPM clinical inventory, then map it to **Spark for DOOH**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.13 — Pharma demand pool moves**
If a competitor signal mentions a built-in pharma manufacturer demand pool, exclusive pharma demand for a publisher SSP, or zero-cost partner model for inventory owners, then map it to **Admanager** and **Spark for Pharmacy** (and to **Spark for EHRs** when the inventory is EHR). Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.14 — HCP scoring moves**
If a competitor signal mentions HCP scoring, prescribing-likelihood scoring, current vs potential prescriber methodology, or budget-tier guidance based on HCP grade, then map it to **AQS**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.15 — Health-system zero-cost affordability moves**
If a competitor signal mentions zero-cost-to-provider affordability tools, manufacturer-funded health-system access, trial matching at prescribing, or drug intelligence inside the EHR, then map it to **co-pay.com for Health Systems**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.16 — Identity / NPI deterministic match moves**
If a competitor signal mentions deterministic NPI matching, 1:1 HCP identity graph, or proprietary HCP identity resolution at high match rates, then map it to **Marketplace, Premium Programmatic, POC, and Admanager** (because ESPYIAN underpins all of them). Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.17 — Patented Triggers and patent-related moves**
If a competitor signal mentions patented real-time clinical-action triggers, USPTO patents in clinical messaging, or patented multi-condition clinical scenario engines, then map it to **POC, POD, NEXT, Spark for EHRs, Spark for Pharmacy, Spark for DOOH**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.18 — Compliance / certification moves**
If a competitor signal mentions HIPAA certification, SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF, GDPR Article 28, CCPA, or POCMA certification, then map it to **all relevant Doceree products in the same category** and treat as a battlecard-update trigger because certification claims affect the entire competitive set. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.19 — Generic B2B ABM platforms entering healthcare**
If a generic B2B ABM platform (Demandbase, 6sense, DemandScience, Madison Logic, etc.) launches a healthcare module, hires healthcare-specific roles, or announces medical-publisher integrations, then map it to **ABM** at Severity 4 because it indicates direct vertical entry. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.20 — Generic DSPs adding HCP capabilities**
If a generic DSP (Trade Desk, StackAdapt, etc.) announces NPI targeting, EHR adjacency, or healthcare measurement, then map it to **Premium Programmatic** and to **NEXT**, and treat at Severity 3–4 depending on integration depth. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.21 — Hospital / health-system buying-side platform moves**
If a competitor signal mentions VAC or P&T committee tools, formulary-decision platforms, or IDN engagement, then map it to **ABM**. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.22 — Job postings as leading indicators**
If competitors post jobs for clinical-trigger engineering, FHIR integration, healthcare ad-tech, MLR-aware AI, prescriber-readiness scoring, EHR-vendor BD, or PMS engineering, treat as a Severity 2–3 signal that should be mapped to the most-aligned Doceree product and queued for periodic review. Job postings are leading indicators, not proof. Confidence: Medium.

**Rule 7.23 — Partnership announcements**
If a competitor announces partnership with Epic, Cerner / Oracle Health, Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, LiveRamp, KickFire, Bombora, Definitive Healthcare, Trade Desk, or DV360, map to the most-aligned Doceree product family and treat at Severity 3–4 depending on integration depth. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.24 — Executive social posts using Doceree-category language**
If a competitor executive starts using language such as "AI-powered Operating System for healthcare marketing," "clinical intent," "Switzerland of HCP marketing," "publisher data sovereignty," or "from prescription to therapy start," treat as a Severity 3 positioning signal and map to the most-aligned product. Confidence: Medium.

**Rule 7.25 — Pricing disruption signals**
If a competitor announces pricing changes that materially undercut Doceree (e.g. removing trigger-CPM minimums, eliminating setup fees, introducing performance-based pricing), treat as Severity 4–5 depending on product, and map to the affected product or product family. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.26 — Acquisition / M&A signals**
If a competitor is acquired or acquires a player whose capability overlaps with Doceree (e.g. Lasso → IQVIA, Swoop → W2O Group), treat as Severity 5 if it materially changes the competitive set, Severity 4 otherwise, and map to all overlapping products. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.27 — Comparison page or battlecard publication**
If a competitor publishes a comparison page, review-site listing, or battlecard naming Doceree directly, treat as Severity 5 and map to the named product(s). Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.28 — Webinars and event sessions**
If a competitor sponsors or speaks at sessions on topics such as "real-time clinical context," "endemic media for HCPs," "AI in pharma marketing," "anti-AI-search tactics," "pharmacy point of decision," or "performance-based affordability," treat as Severity 2 and map to the relevant product. Confidence: Medium.

**Rule 7.29 — Documentation / release-notes changes**
If a competitor adds release notes describing real-time triggers, multi-condition logic, NPI + context targeting, MLR-cleared message libraries, or BYOP-style activation tags, treat as Severity 3 and map to the closest Doceree product. Confidence: High.

**Rule 7.30 — Negative-keyword / false-positive guardrails**
If signals appear that match Doceree keywords but are clearly outside healthcare (e.g. "ABM" in a SaaS context, "DOOH" without clinical screens, "POD" meaning podcast, "POC" meaning proof of concept), the agent should suppress mapping and log as a false positive. Confidence: High.

## Section 9 — Battlecard Intelligence Requirements

### Marketplace
**Competitor Categories:** HCP audience data and identity vendors; healthcare DSPs that bundle audiences with their own activation only; data clean rooms.
**Likely Competitors:** IQVIA / Lasso; Komodo Health; Definitive Healthcare; healthcare DSPs with self-serve audience builders.
**Where Doceree Wins:** Custom-first construction; live EHR intelligence; build-once activate-anywhere via LiveRamp; privacy-by-design with masked HCP IDs.
**Where Competitors May Claim Strength:** Larger Rx coverage (IQVIA NPA), larger patient datasets (Komodo), larger HCP profile depth (Definitive).
**Common Objections:** "We already have IQVIA / Komodo / Definitive." "Custom audiences take too long." "Our DSP has its own builder." "We need Rx attribution, not audience design."
**Recommended Responses:** Custom audiences load and preview in real time, not days; Marketplace can score competitor lists via AQS; activation extends beyond Doceree via LiveRamp; Rx attribution is supported via IQVIA / Veeva Crossix partners downstream.
**Proof Needed:** Audience-construction SLA; specific Rx-lift outcomes from Marketplace audiences vs. catalogue audiences.
**Claims to Validate:** Pricing structure; audience refresh cadence; EU consent posture for LiveRamp activations.
**Evidence Required:** Customer-validated audience-construction times; AQS-graded comparisons of Marketplace vs. catalogue lists.
**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Competitor adds custom-audience builder; Competitor announces live EHR signal ingestion; Competitor announces LiveRamp / cross-DSP activation; Competitor publishes case study with custom-audience Rx lift.

### ABM
**Competitor Categories:** Generic B2B ABM platforms; healthcare DSPs claiming account-level targeting; healthcare data vendors paired with separate activation.
**Likely Competitors:** Demandbase; 6sense; DemandScience; Madison Logic.
**Where Doceree Wins:** Healthcare-native infrastructure; IP + context together; eight departments × five leadership levels role targeting; account-lift measurement.
**Where Competitors May Claim Strength:** Cross-vertical scale; mature B2B ABM tooling; AI-driven buying-group identification.
**Common Objections:** "We already use Demandbase / 6sense." "Can you guarantee account lift?" "Our agency runs ABM." "Our budget is allocated to HCP-level media."
**Recommended Responses:** Doceree adds endemic, EHR-adjacent, MeSH-driven context; account lift is measured but not guaranteed; complement-not-replace agency motion; HCP-level media still benefits from institutional context.
**Proof Needed:** Specific account-lift case studies; healthcare-vs-generic-ABM benchmarks.
**Claims to Validate:** DCO and Brand.com Pixel launch dates; flat-rate vs CPM tier specifics; battlecard wording referencing "POC" inside ABM context (templating issue).
**Evidence Required:** Pre/post account traffic data; multi-stakeholder engagement metrics.
**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Generic ABM platform adds healthcare module; Competitor announces medical-publisher integrations; Competitor announces hospital / IDN targeting; Competitor announces VAC / P&T tools.

### Premium Programmatic (incl. Content Marketing)
**Competitor Categories:** Healthcare DSPs; IQVIA Lasso and other healthcare omnichannel platforms; cross-vertical DSPs; predictive HCP audience platforms; generic content syndication.
**Likely Competitors:** DeepIntent; PulsePoint; IQVIA Lasso; Trade Desk; StackAdapt; Swoop / Veeva Crossix.
**Where Doceree Wins:** NPI + context together; largest endemic publisher network; six ad formats including industry-first Content Marketing and AI Brand Rep; keyword-level reporting; ESPYIAN deterministic identity.
**Where Competitors May Claim Strength:** IQVIA's data scale; DeepIntent's healthcare-specific DSP and Cortex AI; PulsePoint's HCP365 measurement; Trade Desk's omnichannel scale.
**Common Objections:** "Your CPMs are higher than open exchange." "We already use a healthcare DSP." "We need Rx attribution natively." "Brand safety in programmatic." "We don't have budget for another channel."
**Recommended Responses:** Verified vs unverified audience quality; Doceree complements rather than replaces existing DSPs via NEXT BYOP; Rx attribution available via partners; brand safety is part of Doceree's pre-vetted publisher network; reallocation from non-endemic waste, not additive spend.
**Proof Needed:** Endemic-vs-non-endemic CTR benchmarks; keyword-level reporting examples; Content Marketing ROI cases.
**Claims to Validate:** Native Rx-level attribution; self-serve buying; "250+ countries" wording in any deck.
**Evidence Required:** 2-3× engagement uplift documentation; viewability and CTR benchmarks.
**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Competitor adds endemic publisher integrations; Competitor announces medical-keyword taxonomy; Competitor adds AI virtual-rep ad format; Competitor publishes keyword-level reporting; Competitor publishes case study claiming 2-3× engagement uplift.

### RepTwin
**Competitor Categories:** Pharma-specific AI rep / agent platforms; healthcare AI platforms in adjacent use cases; horizontal agentic AI platforms; traditional pharma engagement vendors.
**Likely Competitors:** Synthio Labs; Hippocratic AI (adjacent — patient care focus); Beam AI (horizontal); Veeva-based assistants; in-house pharma chatbots.
**Where Doceree Wins:** Pharma-purpose-built compliance; multimodal video / voice / chat with seamless switching; closed-system MLR-only training with sandbox testing and version locking; deployable across Brand.com, publishers, EHR widgets, messaging, internal training; embedded inside Premium Programmatic and Publisher AI Suite.
**Where Competitors May Claim Strength:** Hippocratic AI's safety architecture; horizontal agentic AI's flexibility; Veeva's CRM-native footprint.
**Common Objections:** "How do you stay compliant with MLR?" "Can it answer off-label questions?" "Do HCPs want to talk to an AI?" "Adverse-event capture liability?" "We already have a chatbot."
**Recommended Responses:** Sandbox + version-locking + MLR-only training; off-label escalates to MSL; multimodal supports HCP preference; closed system + audit trails reduce AE liability vs. open-LLM products; bundle of agencies / Brand.com / publishers / EHR widgets goes far beyond a chatbot.

**Claims to Validate:** Final 40+ language list; WhatsApp / SMS country availability; outbound automatic-call status.
**Evidence Required:** Engagement transcripts; MSL-escalation logs; LOE-brand usage data.
**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Competitor announces AI virtual rep / multimodal AI; Competitor announces MLR-aware sandbox; Competitor adds languages / voice / video; Competitor announces EHR or publisher integration for AI assistant.

### POC
**Competitor Categories:** EHR aggregators; healthcare DSPs claiming POC adjacency; agency-tech hybrids; independent EHR-resident media products; resellers and consultancies.

**Common Objections:** "We use OptimizeRx." "PulsePoint claims 95% match — yours is 86-93%." "Our agency runs all our POC." "Different from DeepIntent's POC?" "We need Rx-level attribution."
**Recommended Responses:** Direct integrations vs aggregated middleware; multi-condition vs single-variable matching; pure tech (no agency conflict); Doceree's reach 6M+ vs competitors' smaller universes; weekly Physician-Level Data plus integrations with IQVIA / Veeva Crossix for Rx attribution.
**Proof Needed:** Match-rate audits by therapeutic area; ABRB-vs-manual time savings.

**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Competitor adds direct EHR API integration; Competitor announces real-time clinical trigger product; Competitor publishes NRx / TRx lift case study; Competitor announces ABRB-equivalent automated rule builder; Competitor announces POCMA certification.

### NEXT (incl. Clinical Intent Signals)
**Competitor Categories:** Walled-garden omnichannel; healthcare DSPs; point-of-care platforms; predictive HCP audience platforms; agency-tech hybrids.
**Likely Competitors:** IQVIA Lasso; DeepIntent; PulsePoint; OptimizeRx; Swoop; Relevate Health.

**Recommended Responses:** BYOP enhances rather than replaces; multi-brand-without-conflict because Doceree is pure tech; de-identified clinical indicators only; pricing transparent and usage-based.
**Proof Needed:** BYOP-tag activation examples; CIS pilot benchmarks; multi-brand reference.
**Claims to Validate:** HITRUST scope (certified vs aligned); generalised replicability of pilot lifts.
**Evidence Required:** Decision-stage progression case studies; cost-per-incremental-Rx benchmarks.
**Battlecard Update Triggers:** Competitor adds "clinical intent" framing; Competitor announces BYOP-equivalent open architecture; Competitor announces direct EHR integration; Competitor announces partnership with Trade Desk / DV360 / Veeva / Salesforce / Adobe.

## Section 10 — Severity Scoring by Product

**General severity model:**
- **Severity 1** — Low-value mention. Archive only.
- **Severity 2** — Useful but not urgent. Include in weekly review.
- **Severity 3** — PMM should review. Potential positioning or battlecard relevance.
- **Severity 4** — Sales enablement or battlecard update likely needed.
- **Severity 5** — Executive alert. Major competitive threat, major launch, partnership, pricing disruption, acquisition, or direct attack on Doceree positioning.

## Section 11 — Confidence Scoring Guidance

| Source Type | Confidence Level | Why | How the Agent Should Phrase the Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official competitor product page | High | Owned, current, public marketing surface | "Per [competitor]'s product page (URL, date), the product is positioned as …" |
| Official press release | High | Formal, attributable announcement | "[Competitor] announced (URL, date) that …" |
| Official docs / release notes | High | Technical confirmation of capabilities | "[Competitor]'s release notes (URL, date) describe a new feature that …" |
| Official case study | High (for outcomes claimed) | Vendor-controlled but publicly attributed | "Per [competitor]'s case study (URL, date), the customer reported …" |
| Executive social post | Medium | Indicative but not authoritative | "[Executive], in a [LinkedIn / X] post (URL, date), referenced …" |
| News article | Medium | Third-party verification, but quality varies | "Per [outlet] (URL, date), [competitor] is reported to have …" |
| Job posting | Medium | Strategic indicator, not proof of product | "A [competitor] job posting (URL, date) suggests planned investment in … (treat as leading indicator, not launch)" |
| SEO / category content page | Medium | Useful for positioning, less so for capability | "[Competitor]'s category content page positions … but specific capability claims require additional verification." |
| Conference / webinar page | Medium | Often pre-launch or aspirational | "[Competitor] presented … at [event] (URL, date); product status should be verified." |
| Third-party mention | Low | Variable accuracy and recency | "A third-party mention from [source] (URL, date) describes … but should be validated against official sources." |
| Analyst report | Medium-to-High | Stronger when paywalled and attributable | "Per [analyst firm] report (date, citation), …" |
| Review site (G2, Capterra, etc.) | Low-to-Medium | User-perception bias and recency variance | "Reviews on [site] (URL, date) suggest … (user perception, not vendor claim)." |

**Important:** Severity and confidence are separate. A job posting may be strategically important (Severity 3) but should never be treated as proof of a launch (Confidence: Medium at best). The agent should never escalate based on confidence alone, and it should never anchor severity in low-confidence sources without corroboration.

## Section 14 — Final Summary for Codex

This Product Spine Document v1 is the seed asset for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center. Codex should use it as follows:

- **Seed `doceree_products` table.** Each entry under `products` in Section 13's JSON becomes one row. Use `product_name` as the canonical key and store `journey_stage`, `short_description`, `one_line_definition`, `primary_problem_solved`, and the structured arrays as columns or JSONB fields as appropriate.
- **Power product mapping.** The `keywords` block on each product becomes the basis for classifier features. Index every keyword (category, buyer, audience, workflow, competitor_signal, partnership, jobs, news, seo, case_study) with a reference back to the product. Use `negative_keywords` to suppress false positives.
- **Power classification logic.** The `competitive_signal_mapping_rules` block in Section 13 becomes the rule engine. For each new signal ingested by the agent, evaluate against rules in order; emit one or more product matches with an associated confidence.
- **Power battlecard task creation.** The `battlecard_requirements` block defines, per product, the competitor categories and update triggers. When a signal matches an `update_trigger` value, create a battlecard-update task in the workflow queue and assign it to PMM.
- **Power severity scoring.** The `severity_guidance` block defines numeric severity levels and recommended actions. Each signal receives both a severity (1–5) and a confidence (High / Medium / Low). Severity drives routing (archive / weekly review / PMM / battlecard / exec alert); confidence governs how the agent phrases the finding.
- **Power source interpretation.** The `confidence_guidance` block defines how to phrase findings depending on source type. Codex should always include the source URL and access date and never escalate severity based on confidence alone.
- **Power product-data gaps in the UI.** The `open_questions` block on each product surfaces in the UI as "Needs PMM input" tasks. When a question is resolved, write the answer back to the product record and clear the gap.
- **Use the JSON as initial backend seed data.** The JSON in Section 13 is intentionally valid and comment-free. It can be loaded directly into the backend at boot to populate the products table, the journey map, the relationship graph, the rule engine, the battlecard registry, and the severity / confidence reference tables.

Operating principles for Codex agents:
- Confirmed claims may be reused as approved messaging.
- Inferred claims may be reused only with an "Inferred" label and SME acknowledgment.
- Needs-confirmation items must never be repeated as Doceree positioning until validated.
- All competitor-related findings must cite an external source with URL and access date.
- Doceree's source-grounded positioning and external competitor descriptions must remain strictly separated in agent output.

End of Doceree Product Spine Document v1.

# Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center — Competitor & Source Registry v1

**Purpose:** Source-of-truth registry of competitors, sources, monitoring cadences, and collection methods for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.
**Status labels:** *Confirmed* (verified against the competitor's own public site), *Needs validation* (suggested but not independently verified), *Needs source discovery* (URL pattern not confirmed in this pass).
**Version:** v1 — 26 April 2026.

---

## Section 1 — Research Approach

**How competitors were identified.** The starting set was anchored to Doceree's own competitive references (Onboarding Guide, battlecards, FAQs) and the Product Spine v1 document. From that anchor, the list was widened to include category-shaping players that Doceree's own materials do not name but which credibly compete with one or more Doceree products (e.g., Hippocratic AI in adjacent agentic-AI healthcare space, TollBit in content-licensing infrastructure for AI-era publisher monetization).

**Direct vs adjacent classification.** "Direct" was reserved for vendors with explicit product-category overlap on a Doceree product (e.g., OptimizeRx and Veradigm vs POC; ConnectiveRx vs POD; CoverMyMeds vs co-pay.com). "Adjacent" was used where a vendor competes on a related buying decision but with a meaningfully different product surface (e.g., generic B2B ABM platforms — Demandbase, 6sense, Madison Logic, DemandScience — that compete with Doceree ABM only when extended into healthcare; Hippocratic AI which addresses patient-care use cases adjacent to RepTwin's pharma-rep use case).

**Mapping competitors to Doceree products.** Each competitor was mapped against Doceree's eight demand-side products from the Product Spine. Mapping rules: a "High overlap" requires the competitor to have an offering that addresses the same buyer with a comparable product motion; "Medium overlap" requires the competitor to credibly enter the territory through partnerships, repositioning, or recent product moves; "Low overlap" requires only a category adjacency.

**Public sources used.** Each competitor's own corporate website (homepages, product/solution pages, newsroom, blog, careers); investor-relations sites for public companies (e.g., GoodRx, Definitive Healthcare, OptimizeRx); PR Newswire and BusinessWire for cross-verification of dated announcements; LinkedIn company pages noted at URL level only (no scraping recommended); and Doceree's own internal materials for mapping accuracy.

**Limitations.** This pass verified URL patterns for ~15 of the most important competitors via live web searches. For the remainder, source URLs are tagged "Needs source discovery" rather than fabricated. URL patterns drift over time (especially after acquisitions and rebrands — Veradigm/Allscripts, PulsePoint/Internet Brands+WebMD, Lasso/IQVIA), so all entries below should be re-verified before being committed to the database. No paywalled or gated platforms were accessed; LinkedIn is treated as approved-API/manual-export only.

**Assumptions.** (1) The Product Spine v1 product map is canonical (eight demand-side products). (2) Doceree wants the system to monitor only public sources and approved APIs; no scraping of LinkedIn, gated webinars, paid ad libraries, or login-required portals. (3) Investor-relations sites count as official public sources for public companies. (4) Trademark / patent-office searches are out of scope for v1 (may be added later as a separate signal class).

**Areas needing human validation.** The Tier-3 list and any "Suggested / Needs validation" entries should be reviewed by Doceree PMM and Sales. Confidence on URL patterns is highest for Tier-1 competitors verified in this pass; lower for Tier-3 entries flagged "Needs source discovery."

---

## Section 2 — Competitor Tiering Framework

**Tier 1 — Direct competitors. Monitor daily.**
Companies with strong product/category overlap with one or more Doceree products. Daily monitoring on Priority-1 source types (homepage hero, product/solution pages, newsroom, blog) and weekly on the rest.
Criteria: (a) explicit head-to-head competition on at least one Doceree product, (b) named in Doceree battlecards or Onboarding Guide as a direct competitor, (c) actively shipping product or making significant news in the last 12 months.

**Tier 2 — Adjacent competitors. Monitor weekly.**
Companies that compete in related healthcare marketing, pharma media, HCP engagement, POC, access, adherence, data, AI, or orchestration categories.
Criteria: (a) overlap on a Doceree product is partial (single capability rather than full product), (b) competing primarily on adjacent buyer (e.g., generic B2B ABM platforms whose pharma practice is partial), (c) emerging or category-shaping but not yet a direct head-to-head loss source.

**Tier 3 — Emerging, indirect, or category-shaping competitors. Monitor monthly or when major news occurs.**
Companies that may not compete directly today but influence category language, buyer expectations, or future competitive direction.
Criteria: (a) early-stage but on the pharma / healthcare-marketing trajectory, (b) horizontal player whose pharma extension is plausible, (c) infrastructure-layer competitor (e.g., content licensing for AI bots) whose moves shape Doceree's supply-side strategy.

**Tiering review cadence.** Quarterly review of Tier-1 and Tier-2 by PMM; semi-annual review of Tier-3.

**Triggers to move a competitor up a tier:**
- Launches an overlapping product against a Doceree product.
- Publishes a comparison page or battlecard naming Doceree.
- Closes a major partnership with Epic, Cerner/Oracle Health, Veeva, Salesforce, or IQVIA that changes product overlap.
- Acquired by, or acquires, an incumbent in a Doceree-overlap space.
- Announces pricing parity or undercut.
- Hires for healthcare-specific roles (FHIR engineering, MLR sandbox, prescriber-readiness scientist, pharmacy-software partnership).

**Triggers to move a competitor down a tier:**
- Discontinues an overlapping product.
- Pivots away from healthcare or out of the contested category.
- Acquired by a non-strategic buyer with no plan to extend into the contested category.
- 12+ months of no new product or partnership signal in the contested space.

## Section 5 — Competitor-by-Competitor Deep Dive

> Tier-1 and Tier-2 profiles below. Tier-3 entries are summarised in Section 3 and the JSON in Section 12.

### OptimizeRx
- **Tier:** 1
- **Website:** https://www.optimizerx.com/
- **Company Description:** Public company providing omnichannel pharma-marketing solutions; 300+ EHR/ePrescribe partners; 2M+ HCPs and patients; reports script-lift averages from EHR programs.
- **Primary Category:** Point-of-care marketing
- **Secondary Categories:** Healthcare omnichannel; co-pay distribution; pharmacy adjacency
- **Doceree Products Impacted:** POC (primary), NEXT, co-pay.com, POD, Spark for EHRs
- **Why This Competitor Matters:** Most-named POC competitor in Doceree's own materials; expanding into retail / pharmacy adjacent channels (kiosks, cooler screens). DAAP platform overlaps with NEXT framing.
- **Known Products / Solutions:** DAAP (Dynamic Audience Activation Platform); Micro-Neighborhood Targeting (MNT, patented); EHR/ePrescribe placements; patient-chart messaging; NPI-level reporting and script-lift studies.
- **Target Buyers:** Pharma brands and agencies.
- **Target Audiences:** Verified HCPs and their patients via EHR/ePrescribe networks.
- **Positioning Summary:** "Dynamic, Omnichannel Solutions for Life Sciences Marketing."
- **Key Claims:** 300+ EHR/ePrescribe partners; access to 2M+ HCPs and their patients; reported 17% average script lift from EHR programs; up to 25% with AI-driven targeting. (Source: optimizerx.com, investors.optimizerx.com)
- **Proof Points:** Quarterly investor reporting; Q2 2025 revenue $29.2M (+55% YoY); recent expansion of point-of-care network with four new partner agreements increasing NPI reach by 37%.
- **Partnerships / Integrations:** EHR / ePrescribe partner network (specifics on investor pages).
- **Potential Threat to Doceree:** Direct head-to-head loss source on POC; DAAP narrative can be misread as orchestration parity with NEXT; pharmacy-adjacent moves overlap with POD.
- **Likely Sales Objections They Could Create:** "OptimizeRx already has 300+ EHR partners — why switch?" "DAAP gives us orchestration today." "Reported 17% script lift average."
- **Battlecard Relevance:** POC, NEXT, co-pay.com, POD.
- **Research Priority:** High.
- **Information Gaps:** Specific match-rate methodology vs Doceree's 86–93%; current pricing terms; specific PMS partner names for their pharmacy expansion.
- **Sources:** https://www.optimizerx.com/ ; https://investors.optimizerx.com/news-releases ; https://www.optimizerx.com/blog ; https://www.optimizerx.com/careers ; https://www.optimizerx.com/news-and-mentions

### Veradigm
- **Tier:** 1
- **Website:** https://veradigm.com/
- **Company Description:** Healthcare technology company (formerly Allscripts, founded 1986); HQ Chicago, IL. Combines platforms, data, expertise, connectivity, and scale. Owns its EHR products (Allscripts ambulatory and others).
- **Primary Category:** EHR ad media (Veradigm Digital Health Media)
- **Secondary Categories:** Healthcare data; provider-network technology
- **Doceree Products Impacted:** POC (primary), Spark for EHRs, NEXT, co-pay.com for Health Systems
- **Why This Competitor Matters:** Direct POC competitor with one of the largest US ambulatory EHR user bases. Doceree's positioning frames its EHR ownership as a conflict-of-interest for partner EHRs.
- **Known Products / Solutions:** Veradigm Digital Health Media; Veradigm Network; data and analytics products; provider-network products.
- **Target Buyers:** Pharma brands and agencies; health systems.
- **Target Audiences:** Verified HCPs in Veradigm Network EHRs.
- **Positioning Summary:** "Working together to transform health, insightfully."
- **Key Claims:** First EHR media platform validated and POCMA-certified; reported 16B+ impressions delivered for 200+ life-science brands. (Source: veradigm.com)
- **Proof Points:** POCMA certification; investor / financial milestones via Veradigm investor page.
- **Partnerships / Integrations:** EHR partner network is owned by Veradigm itself; Doceree casts this as a vulnerability for partner EHRs.
- **Potential Threat to Doceree:** Strong incumbent on POC; potentially compelling to EHR vendors who do not see the conflict-of-interest framing.
- **Likely Sales Objections They Could Create:** "Veradigm has POCMA certification and 16B+ impressions." "We're already on Veradigm's EHR — easier integration."
- **Battlecard Relevance:** POC, Spark for EHRs, NEXT.
- **Research Priority:** High.
- **Information Gaps:** Current pricing; product roadmap post-Allscripts era; relationship with non-Allscripts EHR vendors.
- **Sources:** https://veradigm.com/ ; https://veradigm.com/about-veradigm/in-the-news/ ; https://veradigm.com/about-veradigm/press-releases/ ; https://veradigm.com/careers/

## Section 7 — Source Type Taxonomy

| Source Type | What It Reveals | Example Signals | Recommended Frequency | Automation Method | Risk / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Top-level positioning, hero claim, primary buyer narrative | Hero copy change, new badge / certification, repositioned tagline | Daily (Tier 1), Weekly (Tier 2), Monthly (Tier 3) | Website crawler / DOM diff | Low risk; high signal-to-noise for repositioning |
| Product page | Specific product capability, feature claims, GA status | New feature announcement, product rename, new pricing tile, new "Coming Soon" | Daily (Tier 1), Weekly (Tier 2) | Website crawler / DOM diff | Low risk; canonical capability evidence |
| Solution page | Vertical / persona positioning, industry-specific claims | New healthcare module, new pharma vertical, new role-based positioning | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Pricing page | Commercial-model changes, pricing disruption | Price reduction, new free tier, removal of setup fee | Weekly | Website crawler / DOM diff | Low risk; may be hidden behind contact-sales |
| Blog | Thought leadership, category narratives, executive perspectives | New category language, response to industry events, customer narratives | Weekly | RSS feed where available; otherwise crawler | Low risk |
| Resource center | Whitepapers, guides, reports, e-books | New whitepaper on a clinical-intent or HCP-marketing theme | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Newsroom | Aggregated press content | New release, partnership, hire, acquisition | Daily (Tier 1), Weekly (Tier 2) | Sitemap monitor / RSS / crawler | Low risk |
| Press releases | Official company announcements | Funding, leadership change, product launch, partnership, acquisition | Daily (Tier 1), Weekly (Tier 2) | Sitemap monitor / RSS / crawler | Low risk; highest signal-to-noise on company moves |
| Case studies | Customer outcomes, named logos, claim metrics | New customer logo, new outcome metric, new vertical claim | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Customer stories | Same as case studies, often softer narrative | Same as above | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Docs / help center | Technical capability, integration depth, API specs | New API endpoint, new integration partner, new SLA | Weekly (Tier 1), Monthly (Tier 2) | Website crawler / sitemap | Low risk |
| Release notes | Granular product moves | New feature, bug fix, API change | Weekly | Website crawler / RSS where available | Low risk |
| Partner page | Integration ecosystem, channel strategy | New named partner, channel program launch | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Integration page | Technical integration list | New CRM / DSP / EHR integration | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk |
| Events / webinars | Topic and category emphasis, executive narrative | New event series, new webinar topic, conference sponsorship | Weekly | Website crawler | Low risk; gated content requires manual approval |
| Careers page | Hiring signals, capability investment | New role for FHIR engineer, MLR sandbox, prescriber-readiness scientist | Weekly | Website crawler / ATS API where available | Leading-indicator only — not proof of launch |
| LinkedIn company page | Brand voice, partnership posts, executive coverage | New post, new follower spike, new partnership post | Manual / approved access only | Approved API/vendor/manual export | NEVER scrape; LinkedIn TOS restrict automation. Use approved API or social-listening vendors only. |
| Executive LinkedIn profile | Executive narrative, hires, brand-voice direction | Executive job change, new category language post | Manual / approved access only | Approved API/vendor/manual export | NEVER scrape; consider manual review only |
| YouTube | Product demos, conference talks, launch videos | New demo video, new product walkthrough | Weekly | YouTube Data API (approved) | Low risk via API |
| Podcast | Long-form executive narrative, partnership conversations | Executive guest appearance, founder podcast launch | Monthly | RSS feed | Low risk; high context value |
| Ad library | Active campaign creative and narrative | New creative theme, new product mention in ads | Monthly | Approved ad-library API only | Many ad libraries restrict access; check TOS first |
| SEO / glossary page | Category-language plays, defensive SEO | New glossary entry, new category page targeting Doceree-coined terms | Monthly | Website crawler + SERP monitoring | Low risk |
| Comparison page | Direct competitive attack, named vs Doceree | "X vs Doceree" page, "alternatives to Doceree" page | On trigger only — Severity 5 if Doceree is named | Website crawler + SERP monitoring | Highest priority signal type when Doceree is named |
| Analyst report | Third-party validation, market sizing, competitive set framing | New Forrester / Gartner / IDC report mentioning Doceree or competitor | Monthly | Manual upload (paywalled) | Most analyst reports paywalled — manual upload only |
| Review site | Buyer perception, win/loss themes, win-rate dynamics | New review on G2 / Capterra / TrustRadius | Monthly | Approved API where available | Bias toward recent / vocal reviewers |
| Patents / trademarks | Forward-looking IP signals | New trademark filing, new patent application | Monthly (out of v1 scope; reserved for future) | USPTO PATFT, TSDR APIs | Out of scope for v1 |
