```text id="collection_methods_evidence"
manual_upload
vendor_data
human_review
not_recommended_for_automation
```

Collection method matters because it affects trust, compliance, repeatability, and confidence scoring.

---

## 9. Evidence Source Reliability Score

Each evidence record should receive a source reliability score from `0.00` to `1.00`.

### Default Reliability Scores

| Source Type                                |      Default Reliability Score | Confidence Label |
| ------------------------------------------ | -----------------------------: | ---------------- |
| Official competitor product page           |                           0.95 | High             |
| Official competitor press release          |                           0.95 | High             |
| Official docs / release notes              |                           0.90 | High             |
| Official case study                        |                           0.85 | High             |
| Official partner/integration page          |                           0.85 | High             |
| Official careers page                      |                           0.70 | Medium           |
| Executive social post from approved source |                           0.70 | Medium           |
| News article                               |                           0.65 | Medium           |
| Conference / webinar page                  |                           0.65 | Medium           |
| Analyst report                             |                           0.75 | Medium-to-High   |
| SEO / glossary page                        |                           0.55 | Medium           |
| Review site                                |                           0.45 | Low-to-Medium    |
| Third-party mention                        |                           0.40 | Low              |
| Manual upload                              | Depends on uploader and source | Variable         |

### Rule

Source reliability does not equal strategic severity.

A job posting may have medium confidence but high strategic importance.
A product page may have high confidence but low strategic importance.

---

# 10. Evidence Requirements by Source Type

## 10.1 Website Page Evidence

Website evidence includes homepages, product pages, solution pages, pricing pages, partner pages, resource pages, case studies, and similar public web pages.

### Required Fields

```text id="website_evidence_fields"
source_url
canonical_url
captured_at
source_type
collection_method
page_title
screenshot_path
raw_html_path
clean_text_path
content_hash
visual_hash
excerpt
```

### Required for Page Changes

```text id="website_change_fields"
previous_snapshot_id
current_snapshot_id
before_text
after_text
diff_text
diff_classification
change_score
```

### Website Evidence Must Show

* What the page said before
* What the page says now
* What changed
* Why the change may matter
* Whether the change is trivial or meaningful

---

## 10.2 Product Page Change Evidence

Product page changes are high-signal.

### Required Fields

```text id="product_page_change_fields"
source_url
captured_at
before_text
after_text
diff_text
screenshot_path
change_score
detected_product_keywords
detected_competitor_claims
detected_doceree_product_mapping_candidates
```

### Product Page Change Examples

Meaningful product page evidence includes:

* New product description
* New feature claim
* New buyer/persona
* New workflow language
* New integration claim
* New clinical/EHR/pharmacy/AI/co-pay language
* New customer proof
* New outcome metric
* New compliance claim

---

## 10.3 News / PR Evidence

News evidence includes external articles, competitor announcements, press releases, funding news, acquisitions, partnerships, and executive announcements.

### Required Fields

```text id="news_evidence_fields"
article_title
publisher
source_url
canonical_url
published_at
captured_at
excerpt
full_text_path, if available
is_press_release
is_syndicated
canonical_event_id, if deduped
```

### News Evidence Must Distinguish

| Type                          | Meaning                       |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Original company announcement | Highest authority             |
| Official press release        | High authority                |
| Syndicated press release      | Duplicate/supporting evidence |
| Independent article           | Medium authority              |
| Commentary / opinion          | Lower authority               |

### Rule

If the same announcement appears across multiple sources, store all useful evidence but create one canonical finding.

* Regional expansion

### Job Evidence Cannot Prove

# 11. Evidence Lifecycle

Every evidence record should move through a lifecycle.

## 11.1 Evidence Lifecycle States

```text id="evidence_lifecycle_states"
created
parsed
linked_to_candidate_finding
linked_to_final_finding
used_in_report
used_in_alert
used_in_battlecard_task
archived
expired_raw_artifact
deleted
```

---

## 11.2 Evidence Lifecycle Flow

```text id="evidence_lifecycle_flow"
1. Source is collected.
2. Snapshot or raw file is stored.
3. Evidence record is created.
4. Evidence excerpt is extracted.
5. Evidence is passed to specialist agent.
6. Agent creates candidate finding.
7. Evidence Validator checks support.
8. Orchestrator links evidence to final finding.
9. Evidence appears in Evidence Vault.
10. Evidence may be used in report, alert, or battlecard task.
11. Raw artifacts expire according to retention policy.
12. Summary evidence remains linked to findings.
```

---

## 12. Evidence Validation Rules

An evidence record is valid only if it meets the minimum evidence standard.

### Minimum Evidence Standard

| Requirement              |                Required? |
| ------------------------ | -----------------------: |
| Source URL               |                      Yes |
| Source type              |                      Yes |
| Captured timestamp       |                      Yes |
| Excerpt                  |                      Yes |
| Collection method        |                      Yes |
| Competitor mapping       | Yes, unless market-level |
| Source reliability score |                      Yes |
| Evidence type            |                      Yes |

---

## 13. Evidence Quality Levels

Each evidence record should be assigned a quality level.

| Quality Level | Criteria                                                                   | Usage                                         |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Strong        | Official source, screenshot/text captured, clear excerpt, high reliability | Can support high-confidence findings          |
| Good          | Source and excerpt clear, minor missing metadata                           | Can support normal findings                   |
| Partial       | Snippet or incomplete capture only                                         | Can support low/medium confidence with caveat |
| Weak          | Third-party or indirect evidence, limited excerpt                          | Use only as supporting evidence               |
| Invalid       | Missing source, timestamp, or excerpt                                      | Cannot support final finding                  |

---

## 14. Evidence Support Score

Each evidence-to-finding relationship should receive an evidence support score.

### Support Score Scale

|     Score | Meaning                    |
| --------: | -------------------------- |
| 0.00–0.20 | Does not support the claim |
| 0.21–0.40 | Weak support               |
| 0.41–0.60 | Partial support            |
| 0.61–0.80 | Good support               |
| 0.81–1.00 | Strong support             |

### Evidence Support Inputs

```text id="evidence_support_inputs"
source reliability
source authority
excerpt clarity
claim alignment
recency
corroboration
source type
collection completeness
screenshot availability
before/after diff availability
```

---

# 15. Evidence-to-Finding Relationship

A finding can have multiple evidence records.

An evidence record can support multiple findings.

The join table should capture the role of each evidence record.

## Evidence Roles

```text id="evidence_roles"
primary
supporting
corroborating
contradicting
background
```

### Role Definitions

| Role          | Meaning                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Primary       | Main evidence supporting the finding          |
| Supporting    | Additional evidence supporting the finding    |
| Corroborating | Independent source confirming the same signal |
| Contradicting | Evidence that weakens or disputes the finding |
| Background    | Contextual evidence, not direct support       |

---

## 16. Evidence Requirements by Finding Type

| Finding Type           | Minimum Evidence Required                            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Website change         | Screenshot + before/after text + diff                |
| Product launch         | Official page or press release; screenshot preferred |
| Feature change         | Product page/docs/release note evidence              |
| Messaging change       | Before/after website text                            |
| Partnership            | Official announcement or partner page                |
| Integration            | Official docs, partner page, or press release        |
| Case study/proof point | Official case study or customer story                |
| Pricing change         | Pricing page screenshot + before/after text          |
| Hiring signal          | Job posting excerpt                                  |
| Executive narrative    | Approved social/export/transcript evidence           |
| News/PR                | Article/press release text or excerpt                |
| Analyst mention        | Manual upload or licensed report excerpt             |
| Patent/trademark       | Public filing record                                 |
| Source failure         | Error log + source health record                     |

## 17. Screenshot Requirements

### Screenshot Required

Screenshots should be required for:

* Website changes
* Product page changes
* Pricing page changes
* Case study pages
* Partnership pages
* Integration pages
* Major homepage changes
* Comparison pages
* Evidence used in Severity 4 or 5 findings

### Screenshot Optional

Screenshots are optional for:

* RSS-only articles
* API-ingested records
* Manual PDF uploads
* Job postings where clean text is sufficient
* Source failure logs

### Screenshot Failure Handling

If screenshot capture fails but text extraction succeeds:

1. Store text evidence.
2. Mark screenshot status as failed.
3. Assign evidence quality as partial or good depending on completeness.
4. Route high-severity findings to review.
5. Do not block daily report if text evidence is strong enough.

---

# 19. Evidence Retention Policy

User preference:

```text
Raw website snapshots: 7 days
Screenshots: 7 days
Social raw data: 7 days
```

Recommended implementation:

| Evidence Artifact        |                          Retention |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------: |
| Raw HTML                 |                             7 days |
| Screenshots              |                             7 days |
| Raw social exports       |                             7 days |
| Full article text        |                30 days recommended |
| Clean extracted text     |                30 days recommended |
| Evidence excerpts        |                         Indefinite |
| Evidence metadata        |                         Indefinite |
| Diff summaries           |                         Indefinite |
| Finding records          |                         Indefinite |
| Human review records     |                         Indefinite |
| Daily/weekly/CEO reports |                         Indefinite |
| PDF exports              | Indefinite unless manually deleted |
| Source failure logs      |              12 months recommended |
| Agent run logs           |              12 months recommended |

### Important Retention Rule

Even after raw HTML and screenshots expire, the system should preserve:

* Source URL
* Captured timestamp
* Evidence excerpt
* Diff summary
* Linked finding
* Source type
* Collection method
* Review history

This ensures the finding remains auditable at a summary level.

---

## 20. Evidence Expiration Behavior

When raw artifacts expire:

```text id="expiration_behavior"
1. Do not delete the evidence record.
2. Mark raw artifact status as expired.
3. Preserve excerpt, metadata, source URL, timestamp, and linked findings.
4. Preserve PDF/report references.
5. Show UI warning that raw artifact expired.
```

UI warning:

```text
Raw screenshot/HTML artifact has expired based on the 7-day retention policy. Summary evidence, excerpt, source URL, and timestamp are preserved.
```

| Finding Evidence Appendix     | Evidence attached to one finding                       |
| Daily Brief Evidence Appendix | Evidence for all report findings                       |

## Export Must Include

```text id="evidence_export_fields"
Evidence ID
Source URL
Captured timestamp
Source type
Collection method
Excerpt
Linked finding
Source reliability
Evidence quality
Caveats
```

## Export Should Not Include by Default

* Raw HTML
* Internal prompts
* Debug logs
* API keys
* Full social exports
* Sensitive manual-upload content beyond approved excerpt

# 23. Evidence Vault Permissions

In the current MVP access model:

* Sherry can view all evidence.
* Approved readers can view evidence.
* Sherry can annotate evidence.
* No user can edit raw evidence.
* Sherry can delete or hide evidence only through an admin action.
* Raw evidence deletion must be audit logged.

### Actions by Role

| Action                 |     Sherry | Executive Reader | Sales Enablement Reader |
| ---------------------- | ---------: | ---------------: | ----------------------: |
| View evidence          |        Yes |              Yes |                     Yes |
| View linked findings   |        Yes |              Yes |                     Yes |
| Export evidence PDF    |        Yes |              Yes |                     Yes |
| Annotate evidence      |        Yes |    No by default |           No by default |
| Delete raw evidence    | Admin-only |               No |                      No |
| Edit evidence metadata | Admin-only |               No |                      No |

# 26. Evidence and Confidence Scoring

Evidence should directly influence finding confidence.

### Confidence Boosters

```text id="confidence_boosters"
official source
clear excerpt
screenshot captured
before/after diff available
multiple corroborating sources
recent capture
high source reliability
direct product claim
official docs/release notes
official case study
```

### Confidence Reducers

```text id="confidence_reducers"
third-party only
partial text only
missing screenshot
no before/after diff
job posting only
social post only
methodology missing
source inaccessible after capture
old evidence
manual upload without source context
low source reliability
```

---

# 27. Evidence and Severity Scoring

Evidence quality should influence confidence more than severity.

However, some evidence types may increase severity because they signal stronger business impact.

### Severity-Influencing Evidence Types

| Evidence Type                                      | Possible Severity Impact            |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Official product launch page                       | High                                |
| Official partnership announcement                  | High                                |
| Official docs/release notes showing new capability | Medium/High                         |
| Case study with outcome claim                      | Medium/High                         |
| Pricing page change                                | Medium/High                         |
| Jobs cluster                                       | Medium if pattern exists            |
| Executive narrative pattern                        | Medium if repeated                  |
| Third-party article                                | Depends on source and corroboration |

### Rule

Weak evidence should not prevent a finding from being high-severity, but it should keep confidence low and force review.

---

# 28. Evidence Corroboration Model

The system should identify corroborating evidence.

Example:

```text
Evidence 1:
Competitor job posting for EHR integration engineer.

Evidence 2:
Competitor webinar on clinical workflow engagement.

Evidence 3:
Competitor product page adds real-time clinical trigger language.

Finding:
Competitor appears to be moving toward POC/NEXT-adjacent positioning.
```

The system should store:

```text id="corroboration_model"
primary_evidence_id
supporting_evidence_ids
corroboration_count
corroboration_summary
confidence_boost
```

Corroboration should increase confidence only when sources are meaningfully independent.

---

# 29. Contradicting Evidence Model

The system should also support contradicting evidence.

Example:

```text
Finding:
Competitor appears to be launching an EHR workflow product.

Contradicting evidence:
Competitor clarifies in FAQ that the feature is only a content sponsorship, not EHR-integrated.
```

Contradicting evidence should:

* Lower confidence
* Trigger re-review
* Update the finding version
* Add a caveat to reports
* Notify Sherry if the original finding was Severity 4/5

---

# 35. Evidence Security and Safety

The system is intended for competitive intelligence from public, approved, or manually provided sources.

### Safety Rules

The system should:

* Avoid unnecessary personal data collection.
* Avoid extracting sensitive personal information unless directly relevant and approved.
* Avoid PHI collection.
* Avoid credential-based scraping.
* Mark restricted/gated/platform-sensitive sources as requiring review.
* Store social evidence only when obtained through approved methods.
* Audit manual uploads.
* Preserve source and access notes.

### Gated / Paid Content

Gated or paid sources should be treated as:

```text
manual_or_approved_ingest_only
```

The system should not attempt to bypass access controls.

---

# 36. Evidence Validation Checklist

Before evidence can support a final finding, the Evidence Validator should check:

```text id="evidence_validator_checklist"
Does the evidence have a source URL?
Does it have a captured timestamp?
Does it have an excerpt?
Does the excerpt support the claim?
Is the source type appropriate for the claim strength?
Is the collection method approved?
Is the source reliability score present?
Is the evidence recent enough?
Is screenshot required and present?
Is before/after text required and present?
Is this evidence direct or inferential?
Are there caveats?
```

If validation fails, the evidence may still be stored, but the finding must be:

```text
needs_more_evidence
low_confidence
rejected
archived
```

depending on the case.

---

# 37. Evidence Usage in Reports

Reports should not overwhelm readers with raw evidence.

Instead, each report item should include:

```text id="evidence_in_reports"
Evidence count
Primary evidence source
Source URL
Captured date
Short excerpt
Confidence caveat
Link to Evidence Vault
```

### Daily Brief

Show short evidence references.

### CEO Brief

Show only the most important evidence links.

### Sales Enablement Summary

Show evidence enough to support enablement claims.

### Battlecard Task

Show evidence required to justify the update.

# 38. Evidence Usage in Ask War Room

Ask War Room must cite or link to evidence for factual answers.

### Required Behavior

If the answer includes a factual claim about a competitor, Ask War Room must include:

```text id="ask_war_room_evidence_rules"
linked finding
linked evidence
source URL
captured date
confidence label
review status
```

### If No Evidence Exists

Ask War Room should say:

```text
I do not have evidence for that in the current command center database.
```

It should not guess.

# 41. Evidence Guardrails

Codex should enforce these guardrails:

1. A final finding cannot be created without evidence.
2. Evidence cannot be used without source URL, timestamp, and excerpt.
3. Raw evidence cannot be edited after capture.
4. Screenshot is required for high-impact website findings unless capture failed and text evidence is sufficient.
5. Before/after diff is required for page-change findings.
6. Job-posting evidence must carry an inference warning.
7. Social evidence must come from approved/manual/API/vendor input.
8. Third-party-only evidence must lower confidence.
9. Expired raw artifacts must remain visible as expired, not silently disappear.
10. Evidence used in reports must link back to Evidence Vault.

---

# 42. Acceptance Criteria for This Section

This section is complete when the product supports the following:

1. Every evidence record has source URL, timestamp, source type, collection method, and excerpt.
2. Every final finding links to at least one evidence record.
3. Raw evidence records are immutable after capture.
4. Website evidence supports screenshots.
5. Website-change evidence supports before/after diffs.
6. News evidence stores article metadata and excerpt.
7. Job evidence stores title, description excerpt, detected keywords, and inference warning.
8. Case study evidence extracts metrics and methodology caveats.
9. Partnership evidence captures partner type and relationship type.
10. Approved social evidence is supported only through approved/manual/API/vendor ingestion.
11. Manual uploads are stored with uploader, file, source note, and parsed excerpt.
12. Evidence quality levels are assigned.
13. Source reliability scores are assigned.
14. Evidence support scores are available for findings.
15. Evidence can be searched by competitor, product, source type, date, and keyword.
16. Evidence can be exported as PDF.
17. Evidence annotations are separate from raw evidence.
18. Raw HTML and screenshots follow the 7-day retention policy.
19. Evidence excerpts and metadata persist after raw artifacts expire.
20. Ask War Room answers factual questions with linked evidence.
21. Daily briefs, alerts, and battlecard tasks link back to evidence.
22. Source failures are stored as evidence records.
23. Evidence validation prevents unsupported findings from becoming approved intelligence.

# Section X+9 — Crawler and Diff Requirements

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines how the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center should crawl competitor sources, capture page evidence, detect changes, suppress noise, classify meaningful updates, and create evidence records for downstream AI agents.

The crawler and diff engine are the foundation of the system’s autonomy.

If the crawler is weak, the system will miss signals.  
If the diff engine is noisy, Sherry will be overwhelmed.  
If evidence capture is incomplete, findings will not be trustworthy.

The core principle is:

> The crawler captures facts.  
> The diff engine detects change.  
> Agents interpret only meaningful, evidence-backed change.

The crawler should not behave like a random web browser. It should behave like a controlled competitive intelligence collector that monitors approved competitor sources, stores snapshots, captures screenshots, detects business-relevant changes, and routes only meaningful changes to agents.

---

## 2. Crawler Operating Philosophy

The crawler should be designed for business relevance, not raw web coverage.

The goal is not to crawl the entire internet.

The goal is to monitor competitor-controlled or approved sources that are likely to reveal:

- Product launches
- Feature changes
- Messaging changes
- Positioning shifts
- Case studies
- Proof points
- Pricing or packaging signals
- Partnerships
- Integrations
- Docs/release note updates
- Jobs/hiring signals
- Event/webinar narratives
- Category language changes
- New pages related to Doceree product areas

The crawler should prioritize quality, repeatability, evidence capture, and noise reduction.

---

## 3. Crawler Scope

The system should crawl all active, approved competitor sources in the Source Registry.

### Primary Crawl Targets

```text
Competitor homepages
Product pages
Solution pages
Pricing pages
Newsroom pages
Press release pages
Blog pages
Resource centers
Case study pages
Customer story pages
Docs/help centers
Release notes
Partner pages
Integration pages
Events/webinar pages
Careers pages
Comparison pages
SEO/glossary pages, if configured
````

### Conditional Crawl Targets

```text
Paid/gated pages, only if manually approved and accessible
Analyst reports, only through manual upload or licensed access
Social sources, only through approved API/vendor/manual export
Ad libraries, only if public or approved vendor access exists
```

### Out of Scope for Automated Crawling

The crawler should not attempt to:

```text
Bypass login walls
Bypass paywalls
Bypass CAPTCHA
Use shared credentials
Scrape restricted social platforms without approved access
Collect private user data
Collect PHI
Access non-public areas
Circumvent access controls
```

---

## 4. Crawl Source Activation Rules

A URL should be crawled only if it exists in the Source Registry or is discovered through an approved discovery workflow.

### Active Crawl Conditions

A source is eligible for crawl when:

```text
source.is_active = true
competitor.is_active = true
source.health_status is not disabled
source.automation_allowed is yes or conditional
source.collection_method is supported
source.url is valid
source.requires_login is false, unless approved manual/API access exists
```

### Inactive Crawl Conditions

A source should not be crawled when:

```text
source.is_active = false
competitor.is_active = false
source.health_status = disabled
automation_allowed = no
source requires login and no approved access method exists
source is marked manual_only
source is under legal/compliance review
```

---

## 5. Approved URL vs Discovered URL Model

The system should support both:

1. **Approved URLs**
2. **Discovered URLs**

### Approved URLs

Approved URLs are manually added or approved by Sherry in the Source Registry.

These are safe for scheduled monitoring.

### Discovered URLs

Discovered URLs come from:

```text
Sitemap discovery
Internal links on approved pages
RSS feeds
Newsroom indexes
Blog indexes
Docs indexes
Case study listing pages
Events listing pages
Web Search fallback
```

Discovered URLs should not all become active automatically.

They should enter a review state:

```text
needs_review
```

unless they meet strict auto-approval rules.

### Auto-Approval Rules for Discovered URLs

A discovered URL may be auto-activated only if:

```text
It is on the same approved competitor domain
It matches an approved include pattern
It does not match any exclude pattern
It has a clearly classified source type
It does not require login
It is not social/restricted/gated content
It is not a user/account page
It is not a checkout/payment page
It is not a tracking or redirect URL
```

Otherwise, Sherry should approve it before daily monitoring.

---

## 6. URL Include and Exclude Rules

Each competitor should support URL include and exclude patterns.

### Recommended Include Patterns

```text
/product
/products
/solutions
/platform
/case-studies
/customer-stories
/resources
/blog
/news
/newsroom
/press
/press-release
/events
/webinars
/partners
/integrations
/docs
/help
/support
/release-notes
/careers
/jobs
/pricing
```

### Recommended Exclude Patterns

```text
/login
/signin
/signup
/register
/account
/cart
/checkout
/privacy
/terms
/cookie
/legal
/contact
/demo
/thank-you
/subscribe
/unsubscribe
/tag/
?page=
?utm_
/author/
/search
```

### Notes

Exclude rules should be configurable.

Some URLs like `/legal` or `/terms` may matter if compliance claims are being monitored, but they should not be part of the default crawl set unless explicitly configured.

---

## 7. Crawl Frequency Rules

The user preference is to monitor all configured channels daily.

The system should support daily checks across all active sources, while applying source priority to control depth and alerting.

| Source Priority |              Collection Frequency |              Deep Diff Frequency | Agent Analysis             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------: | -------------------------------: | -------------------------- |
| Priority 1      |                             Daily |                            Daily | If changed or high-signal  |
| Priority 2      |           Daily lightweight check | Daily if changed; weekly summary | If meaningful change       |
| Priority 3      |          Daily availability check |              Weekly or triggered | If significant change      |
| Priority 4      | Optional daily availability check |                   Triggered only | Usually archive/background |

### Practical Rule

All active sources may be checked daily, but not every unchanged page should be sent to AI agents.

Agents should analyze only:

```text
new pages
changed pages
new articles
new jobs
new docs
new case studies
new event pages
high-priority pages with meaningful diffs
low-confidence recheck targets
manual recheck targets
```

---

## 8. Crawl Depth Rules

The crawler should support three crawl modes.

### Mode 1 — Single URL Crawl

Used for:

```text
Approved product pages
Approved homepage
Approved case study page
Approved pricing page
Manual source recheck
```

Crawl only the configured URL.

### Mode 2 — Listing Page Crawl

Used for:

```text
Blogs
Newsroom
Resources
Case studies
Events
Careers
Release notes
```

Crawl the listing page and discover new child URLs.

Default depth:

```text
Depth 1–2
```

### Mode 3 — Sitemap Discovery Crawl

Used for:

```text
New competitor onboarding
Source discovery
Broken source fallback
Periodic source refresh
```

Default behavior:

```text
Discover URLs
Classify likely source types
Mark new URLs needs_review unless auto-approved
```

---

## 9. Rate Limiting and Crawl Politeness

The crawler should be conservative and reliable.

### Default Rate Limits

Recommended defaults per competitor domain:

```text
Max concurrent pages per domain: 2
Delay between requests: 2–5 seconds
Daily max pages per competitor: configurable
Timeout per page: 30 seconds static / 45 seconds rendered
Retry count: based on failure type
```

### Notes

The system should avoid aggressive crawling.

The goal is to monitor known competitive sources, not stress external websites.

---

## 10. Source Policy and Access Controls

The crawler must respect the configured source policy.

Every source should have:

```text
automation_allowed
requires_login
collection_method
source_type
source_confidence
notes
```

### Collection Policy Outcomes

```text
allowed
conditional_allowed
manual_only
blocked
needs_review
```

If a source is marked `manual_only`, the crawler should not attempt automated collection.

If a source is blocked or requires credentials, the crawler should log it and notify Sherry if it is Priority 1.

---

## 11. Crawler User Agent and Identification

The crawler should use a configurable user agent.

Recommended:

```text
DocereeCompetitiveIntelligenceBot/1.0
```

The exact user agent can be configured in system settings.

The crawler should not impersonate a human user or a browser in a deceptive way.

Browser rendering through Playwright is allowed for technical rendering of public pages, but not for bypassing access controls.

---

## 12. Static vs Browser-Rendered Crawling

The system should support both static and browser-rendered crawling.

### Static Crawl

Use for:

```text
Simple HTML pages
RSS pages
Blogs
Newsrooms
Docs
Press releases
Case studies
```

Recommended tools:

```text
fetch
Cheerio
Readability extractor
```

### Browser-Rendered Crawl

Use for:

```text
JavaScript-heavy pages
Pages where content is not visible in static HTML
Pages requiring screenshot capture
Pages where static extraction fails
```

Recommended tool:

```text
Playwright
```

### Rendering Rules

Browser-rendered crawler should:

```text
wait for network idle
capture full-page screenshot where useful
extract visible text
remove hidden content
avoid interacting with forms
avoid logging in
avoid accepting restricted prompts beyond normal cookie dismissal
```

---

## 13. Cookie Banner Handling

The crawler should suppress cookie banner noise when possible.

Allowed behavior:

```text
Detect common cookie banners
Avoid treating cookie banner text as page content
Optionally dismiss banners if a simple public-page accept/close button is visible
Record that cookie banner was handled
```

The crawler should not use cookie interactions to access restricted content.

Cookie banners should not trigger findings.

---

## 14. Text Extraction Requirements

The crawler should extract clean, business-relevant page text.

### Text Extraction Should Remove

```text
Navigation
Footer
Cookie banner text
Legal boilerplate
Repeated menus
Tracking text
Hidden scripts
CSS/JS
Social sharing widgets
Newsletter signup boilerplate
Related posts boilerplate
Pagination boilerplate
```

### Text Extraction Should Preserve

```text
Page title
Headings
Product descriptions
Feature descriptions
Customer proof
Metrics
Case study summaries
Partner/integration language
Pricing/packaging language
CTA language when meaningful
Docs/release-note body text
Job title and description
Event/webinar abstract
```

---

## 15. Boilerplate Removal

Boilerplate removal is critical for reducing false positives.

The diff engine should maintain a boilerplate profile for each domain.

### Boilerplate Examples

```text
Header navigation
Footer links
Cookie notices
Newsletter CTAs
Social links
Repeated sidebar content
Generic “contact us” blocks
Legal disclaimers
Copyright years
Tracking parameters
```

### Domain-Level Boilerplate Memory

The system should learn repeated blocks per competitor domain.

If the same block appears on many pages, it should be treated as likely boilerplate unless it appears in the main content area.

---

## 16. Snapshot Requirements

Every successful crawl should create a snapshot.

### Snapshot Fields

```text
snapshot_id
source_id
competitor_id
url
canonical_url
source_type
captured_at
http_status
page_title
raw_html_path
clean_text_path
screenshot_path
content_hash
visual_hash
text_length
language
collection_method
previous_snapshot_id
change_detected
change_score
created_at
```

### Snapshot Creation Rule

Create a snapshot for every successful crawl, even if no change is detected.

This allows the system to prove the source was checked.

---

## 17. First-Day Baseline Behavior

On the first day a source is crawled, there is no previous snapshot.

The system should create a baseline.

### Baseline Output

For first-time crawl, the system should:

```text
Create source snapshot
Create evidence record
Mark snapshot as baseline
Generate competitor/source baseline summary
Do not classify as “changed”
Optionally create baseline product summary for Tier 1 competitors
```

### Baseline Summary

For Tier 1 competitors, baseline should summarize:

```text
Products listed
Positioning
Target audiences
Core claims
Key use cases
Proof points
Partnerships/integrations
Doceree product overlap
Open questions
```

This baseline becomes the comparison point for future changes.

---

## 18. Change Detection Overview

The diff engine should compare the current snapshot to the previous snapshot.

It should answer:

```text
Did anything change?
Was the change meaningful?
What exactly changed?
Is the change business-relevant?
Which signal type does the change suggest?
Should an agent analyze it?
```

---

## 19. Change Detection Layers

The system should use multiple layers of change detection.

### Layer 1 — Hash Change

Compare content hashes.

```text
If hash unchanged → no text change
If hash changed → inspect diff
```

### Layer 2 — Structural Diff

Compare headings, sections, and visible content blocks.

### Layer 3 — Text Diff

Compare clean extracted text.

### Layer 4 — Semantic Diff

Use LLM or embedding-assisted comparison only for candidate meaningful changes.

### Layer 5 — Business-Relevance Diff

Check whether the change affects product, positioning, proof, partnerships, jobs, docs, or Doceree-relevant themes.

---

## 20. Trivial Change Suppression

The diff engine should suppress non-business changes.

### Ignore by Default

```text
Cookie banner changes
Navigation text changes
Footer text changes
Copyright year updates
Social widget changes
Date/time refreshes
Tracking parameter changes
Whitespace changes
Formatting changes
CSS/JS changes
Minor image alt text changes
Newsletter block changes
Related article list changes
Pagination updates
“Read more” link order changes
Ad slot changes
```

### Do Not Ignore

```text
New product page
New product name
New feature claim
New category language
New buyer/persona language
New integration claim
New partner logo/name
New customer logo/name
New proof point or metric
New case study
New pricing/packaging language
New clinical/EHR/pharmacy/co-pay/adherence/AI language
New comparison page
New docs/release-note capability
```

---

## 21. Business-Relevant Change Categories

The diff engine should classify changes into categories.

```text
product_launch
feature_change
messaging_change
positioning_change

new_persona

new_case_study
new_customer_logo

new_integration
```

---

## 23. Change Score Model

Every detected change should receive a change score from 0 to 100.

### Change Score Inputs

```text
text_diff_size
semantic_change_score
source_priority
competitor_tier
Doceree keyword match
product keyword match
signal type match
new page detection
new metric/proof point
new product/feature language
new partner/integration language
new pricing language
new clinical/EHR/pharmacy/AI language
new customer/case study language
change location on page
corroborating source exists
```

### Suggested Scoring Bands

| Change Score | Meaning            | Action                                    |
| -----------: | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
|         0–20 | Trivial/noise      | Archive                                   |
|        21–40 | Minor change       | Store only                                |
|        41–60 | Moderate change    | Agent analysis if source/product relevant |
|        61–80 | Significant change | Agent analysis + daily brief candidate    |
|       81–100 | Major change       | Agent analysis + alert candidate review   |

---

## 24. Change Location Weighting

Where the change appears matters.

### Higher Weight

```text
Hero section
Product description
Feature section
Use case section
Customer proof section
Integration section
Pricing section
Case study body
Docs/release note body
Job description responsibilities
Partner announcement body
```

### Lower Weight

```text
Footer
Navigation
Sidebar
Related content
Author bio
Social links
Generic CTA
Newsletter signup
```

---

## 25. Semantic Diff Requirements

For business-relevant candidate changes, the system should generate a semantic diff.

The semantic diff should answer:

```text
What is the meaning of the change?
Did positioning change?
Did product capability change?
Did the target audience change?
Did the competitor add a new proof point?
Did the competitor move closer to a Doceree product area?
```

### Semantic Diff Output

```json
{
  "semantic_change_summary": "",
  "business_relevance": "",
  "possible_signal_types": [],
  "doceree_product_candidates": [],
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "requires_agent_analysis": true
}
```

---

## 26. Diff Object Schema

Every meaningful diff should create a structured diff object.

```json
{
  "diff_id": "",
  "source_id": "",
  "competitor_id": "",
  "previous_snapshot_id": "",
  "current_snapshot_id": "",
  "url": "",
  "source_type": "",
  "captured_at": "",
  "change_detected": true,
  "change_score": 0,
  "diff_classification": "",
  "before_text": "",
  "after_text": "",
  "added_text": [],
  "removed_text": [],
  "diff_text": "",
  "semantic_change_summary": "",
  "detected_keywords": [],
  "doceree_product_candidates": [],
  "is_trivial": false,
  "requires_agent_analysis": true,
  "created_at": ""
}
```

---

## 27. Evidence Creation From Diff

A diff should create evidence when:

```text
change_score >= 41
OR diff_classification is high-signal
OR source is Priority 1 and product-relevant
OR competitor is Tier 1 and source is product/news/docs/case study/pricing
OR the change contains Doceree-relevant keywords
OR the change may affect battlecards
```

Evidence should include:

```text
source URL
captured timestamp
before text
after text
diff text
screenshot path
change score
diff classification
excerpt
```

---

## 28. Agent Analysis Trigger Rules

A changed source should be sent to agents when:

```text
change_score >= 41
diff_classification is not trivial_change
source priority is Priority 1 and change_score >= 30
new page discovered in approved source area
new product/case study/news/job/docs/event item found
detected keywords match Doceree product spine
source type is high-signal
manual rerun requested
low-confidence recheck requested
```

High-signal source types:

```text
product_page
solution_page
pricing_page
docs_help_center
release_notes
case_study
customer_story
newsroom
press_release_page
partner_page
integration_page
careers_page
events_webinars
```

---

## 29. New Page Detection

The crawler should detect newly discovered pages.

### New Page Sources

```text
Sitemap
Listing pages
RSS feed
Internal links on approved pages
Newsroom indexes
Blog indexes
Case study indexes
Docs indexes
Careers indexes
```

### New Page Workflow

```text
1. Discover new URL.
2. Classify likely source type.
3. Check against include/exclude rules.
4. Check automation policy.
5. Create source candidate.
6. If auto-approved, crawl and create baseline.
7. If not auto-approved, route to Source Registry review.
```

### New Page Evidence

If a new page is auto-approved and product-relevant, create evidence and route to the appropriate agent.

---

## 31. Docs and Help Center Crawling

Docs/help centers are high-value sources.

Docs changes can be high-severity if they indicate actual product capability.

## 32. Newsroom and Press Crawling

The crawler should monitor competitor newsrooms and press release pages.

### Newsroom Behavior

```text
Check listing page
Detect new article URLs
Fetch article pages
Extract title, published date, body excerpt
Create evidence
Deduplicate against Web Search/news results
```

### Press Release Rule

Official press releases should be treated as high-confidence evidence.

Syndicated copies should be linked as corroborating evidence, not separate findings.

---

## 33. Blog and Resource Center Crawling

Blogs and resources are useful for category narrative, but can be noisy.

### Blog Analysis Should Focus On

```text
new category language
new buyer/persona focus
new product education
new comparison content
new solution themes
new executive POV
new market narrative
```

### Blog Analysis Should Avoid Overweighting

```text
generic thought leadership
SEO filler content
general healthcare commentary
repeat content
minor updates
```

---

## 34. Case Study Crawling

Case studies are high-value for Sales Enablement and battlecards.

The crawler should detect:

```text
new case study
new customer story
new customer logo
new metric claim
new outcome claim
new vertical/therapy area
new product usage claim
```

Case studies should create evidence even if they do not immediately create high-severity findings.

---

## 35. Partner and Integration Page Crawling

Partner/integration pages are high-value.

The crawler should detect:

```text
new partner
removed partner
new integration
new ecosystem category
new marketplace listing
new technical connector
new health-system/EHR/pharmacy/publisher relationship
```

If a partner type overlaps with Doceree strategic areas, route to Partnership / Integration Agent.

---

## 36. Pricing Page Crawling

Pricing changes can be strategically important.

The crawler should detect:

```text
new pricing page
removed pricing page
new package
new plan name
new pricing model
free trial
enterprise plan
usage-based pricing
outcome-based pricing
new packaging language
```

Pricing evidence should always include screenshot and before/after text when possible.

---

## 37. Screenshot Requirements

The crawler should capture screenshots for:

```text
homepage
product pages
solution pages
pricing pages
case studies
partner pages
integration pages
comparison pages
major findings
Severity 4/5 evidence
```

### Screenshot Configuration

Recommended defaults:

```text
Viewport: 1440x1200
Full-page screenshot: true for high-priority pages
Image format: PNG or WebP
File naming: competitor_source_date_snapshot.png
```

### Screenshot Failure

If screenshot fails:

```text
Store text evidence
Flag missing_screenshot
Retry once
Lower evidence quality if screenshot required
Notify Sherry if Priority 1 and repeated
```

---

## 38. Content Hashing Requirements

The crawler should compute hashes.

### Required Hashes

```text
raw_html_hash
clean_text_hash
main_content_hash
visual_hash, if screenshot exists
```

### Use Cases

Hashes are used to:

```text
detect changes
avoid duplicate evidence
identify unchanged pages
dedupe similar pages
detect repeated boilerplate
track source stability
```

---

## 39. Canonical URL Handling

The crawler should normalize and store canonical URLs.

### Canonicalization Rules

```text
remove UTM parameters
normalize trailing slashes
resolve redirects
use canonical link tag if present
lowercase domain
preserve meaningful path case if needed
remove fragment identifiers unless meaningful
```

### Store Both

The system should store:

```text
requested_url
final_url
canonical_url
```

This helps debug redirects and deduplication.

---

## 40. Redirect Handling

Redirects should be tracked.

### Redirect Cases

| Redirect Type                        | Action                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 301/302 to new page                  | Update final URL; flag for source review          |
| Redirect to homepage                 | Mark possible source moved                        |
| Redirect to login                    | Mark blocked / requires review                    |
| Redirect loop                        | Mark failed                                       |
| Redirect to country/language variant | Store final URL; watch for localization duplicate |

---

## 41. HTTP Status Handling

| HTTP Status | Action                             |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 200         | Process normally                   |
| 301/302     | Follow; log redirect               |
| 304         | Treat as no change if supported    |
| 403         | Mark blocked; notify if Priority 1 |
| 404         | Mark source failed/not found       |
| 429         | Retry later; reduce crawl rate     |
| 500/502/503 | Retry                              |
| Timeout     | Retry                              |
| DNS failure | Retry once; mark degraded          |

---

## 42. Source Health Integration

Every crawl should update source health.

### Source Health Fields

```text
last_checked_at
last_successful_check_at
last_failure_at
consecutive_failure_count
health_status
failure_reason
fallback_attempted
fallback_successful
```

### Health Status Rules

```text
healthy: latest crawl succeeded
degraded: latest crawl partially succeeded
failed: latest crawl failed
needs_review: repeated failure or source moved
disabled: manually disabled
```

---

## 43. Retry Rules

| Failure Type            | Retry Count | Fallback                    |
| ----------------------- | ----------: | --------------------------- |
| Timeout                 |           2 | Browser-rendered crawl      |
| HTTP 5xx                |           2 | Retry later                 |
| HTTP 429                |           1 | Backoff                     |
| Screenshot failure      |           1 | Text-only evidence          |
| Text extraction failure |           1 | Browser-rendered extraction |
| DNS failure             |           1 | Mark degraded               |
| 404                     |           0 | Mark failed                 |
| Login wall              |           0 | Mark needs review           |
| CAPTCHA/block           |           0 | Mark blocked                |
| Policy restricted       |           0 | Skip                        |

---

## 44. Fallback Rules

Fallback methods should be used when appropriate.

### Fallback Options

```text
browser-rendered crawl
sitemap discovery
RSS feed check
Web Search fallback
competitor newsroom check
previous snapshot comparison
manual review request
```

### Fallback Example

If a newsroom page fails:

```text
1. Retry static crawl.
2. Try browser-rendered crawl.
3. Check RSS feed.
4. Use Web Search for competitor news in last 24 hours.
5. Mark source degraded if fallback succeeds.
6. Notify Sherry if all fail and source is Priority 1.
```

---

## 45. PDF and File Crawling

Some competitor sources may link to PDFs.

The system should support PDF detection and optional extraction.

### PDF Handling

```text
Detect PDF links
Download only if source policy allows
Store file path
Extract text if possible
Create manual/document evidence
Route to relevant agent
```

### PDF Use Cases

```text
case study PDFs
whitepapers
webinar decks
analyst excerpts
product brochures
event materials
```

If a PDF is gated, it should not be fetched automatically unless manually uploaded or approved.

---

## 46. Language and Localization Handling

Competitor pages may have localized variants.

The crawler should:

```text
Detect language
Store language code
Avoid duplicate localized pages unless region is relevant
Group localized duplicates
Allow region-specific monitoring if configured
```

Localization should not create duplicate findings unless the content is materially different.

---

## 49. Crawler Logging Requirements

Every crawl attempt must be logged.

### Required Logs

```text
run_id
source_id
competitor_id
requested_url
final_url
start_time
end_time
duration_ms
status
http_status
retry_count
fallback_used
error_type
error_message
snapshot_id
evidence_id
```

Logs should support:

```text
source health dashboard
agent run logs
debugging
coverage reports
failure notifications
quality review
```

---

## 50. Crawler Performance Requirements

The local MVP should be able to handle:

```text
All configured competitors
All active approved URLs
Daily 6:00 AM run
Screenshots for high-priority pages
Diffing against previous snapshots
PDF report generation
Email delivery
```

Performance should be optimized by:

```text
skipping agent analysis for unchanged pages
using hashes before semantic diff
batching crawls by domain
limiting concurrency per domain
storing artifacts on local filesystem
running expensive analysis only on candidate changes
```

---

## 51. Crawler Safety Guardrails

The crawler must follow these guardrails:

1. Do not bypass access controls.
2. Do not use unauthorized social scraping.
3. Do not collect private user data intentionally.
4. Do not collect PHI.
5. Do not crawl login/account/payment areas.
6. Do not generate findings from failed crawls.
7. Do not treat cookie/navigation/footer changes as meaningful.
8. Do not silently ignore repeated source failures.
9. Do not auto-activate restricted discovered URLs.
10. Do not send unchanged pages to agents unnecessarily.

---


### Source Health Dashboard

Show:

```text

failed sources
needs review sources
disabled sources
```

# Section X+10 — Alert Routing Rules and Notification System

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines how the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center routes findings, notifications, alerts, briefs, failures, and review items to the right user at the right time.

The system should not simply generate findings and leave users to discover them manually.

The notification system must ensure that:

- Sherry receives the daily competitive intelligence report automatically.
- Urgent competitor moves are surfaced immediately.
- Severity 4 and Severity 5 findings are routed for approval.
- CEO and Sales alerts are created as candidates, not auto-sent.
- Failed sources and failed runs are visible.
- Low-confidence high-impact findings are clearly marked.
- Battlecard update candidates are routed to Sherry.
- Alert fatigue is controlled.
- Every notification is logged.
- Every sent message can be traced back to evidence.

The core principle is:

> The system should notify Sherry automatically, but it should not distribute high-risk intelligence broadly without Sherry’s approval.

---

## 2. Notification Philosophy

The notification system should balance autonomy with governance.

The system should be autonomous for:

- Daily report generation
- Daily report email to Sherry
- Source failure notifications to Sherry
- Urgent alert candidate creation
- Review queue creation
- Battlecard task candidate creation
- Low-confidence flagging
- Dashboard updates

The system should require Sherry’s approval for:

- CEO alerts
- Sales alerts
- Severity 4/5 broad distribution
- Battlecard copy going live
- Sensitive competitor interpretations
- High-impact findings based on low-confidence evidence
- Findings based on jobs, social, or other inferential sources when used for leadership or Sales

The correct routing model is:

```text
Autonomous detection.
Autonomous draft.
Human approval for high-impact distribution.
````

---

## 3. Primary Notification Recipient

The MVP notification system should send all system-generated intelligence first to:

```text
Sherry George
sherry.george@doceree.com
```

Sherry is the primary owner, reviewer, approver, and operator of the command center.

### Default MVP Rule

```text
All alerts, reports, failures, review queues, and candidates route to Sherry first.
```

This includes:

* Daily reports
* Urgent alerts
* CEO alert candidates
* Sales alert candidates
* Battlecard candidates
* Source failure alerts
* Agent failure alerts
* Low-confidence high-severity findings
* Weekly quality summaries

---

## 4. Notification Channels

## 4.1 MVP Channels

The MVP should support:

```text
Email
UI notifications
Dashboard alert badges
PDF attachments
```

### Required MVP Delivery

| Output                    | Channel                              | Recipient |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------- |
| Daily brief               | Email + PDF + dashboard              | Sherry    |
| Urgent alert candidate    | Email + dashboard                    | Sherry    |
| Source failure            | Email + dashboard                    | Sherry    |
| Agent/run failure         | Email + dashboard                    | Sherry    |
| CEO alert candidate       | Dashboard + optional email to Sherry | Sherry    |
| Sales alert candidate     | Dashboard + optional email to Sherry | Sherry    |
| Battlecard task candidate | Dashboard + daily/weekly summary     | Sherry    |
| Weekly quality report     | Email + dashboard                    | Sherry    |

## 4.2 Later Channels

The following can be added later:

```text
Slack
Microsoft Teams
Gmail API
Microsoft Graph
CRM task creation
Notion / Google Docs export
PPT export
```

MVP should not depend on Slack.

---

## 5. Alert Types

The system should support these alert types.

| Alert Type                                | Purpose                               | Default Recipient |             Auto-Send? |              Approval Required? |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------: | ------------------------------: |
| Daily Competitive Intelligence Brief      | Daily report summary                  | Sherry            |                    Yes |                              No |
| Urgent Competitor Alert Candidate         | High-severity competitor movement     | Sherry            |          Yes to Sherry | Yes before broader distribution |
| CEO Alert Candidate                       | Executive-level strategic finding     | Sherry first      |        No broader send |                             Yes |
| Sales Alert Candidate                     | Sales-relevant competitive finding    | Sherry first      |        No broader send |                             Yes |
| Battlecard Update Alert                   | Finding may require battlecard update | Sherry            |       Dashboard/digest |              Yes before publish |
| Source Failure Alert                      | Source failed or degraded             | Sherry            | Yes when threshold met |                              No |
| Agent Failure Alert                       | Agent/run failed                      | Sherry            |      Yes when critical |                              No |
| Low-Confidence High-Severity Alert        | Important but uncertain finding       | Sherry            |                    Yes |                  Yes before use |
| Product Mapping Review Alert              | Finding cannot map confidently        | Sherry            |       Dashboard/digest |                 Review required |
| Weekly Sales Enablement Summary Candidate | Weekly sales-facing summary           | Sherry first      |        No broader send |                             Yes |
| Weekly Quality Review                     | Agent/source quality summary          | Sherry            |                    Yes |                              No |

---

## 6. Severity-Based Routing Rules

Severity should drive routing.

| Severity | Meaning                        | Default Route                              | Notification Behavior                     |
| -------: | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
|        1 | Low-value mention              | Auto-archive                               | No notification                           |
|        2 | Useful but not urgent          | Weekly summary                             | No immediate notification                 |
|        3 | PMM should review              | Daily brief + optional review queue        | Include in daily report                   |
|        4 | Sales/battlecard update likely | Sherry review queue + battlecard candidate | Email Sherry if high-confidence or urgent |
|        5 | Executive alert candidate      | Urgent alert queue + CEO alert candidate   | Immediate email to Sherry                 |

---

## 7. Confidence-Based Routing Rules

Confidence should control language, caveats, and review routing.

| Confidence       | Routing Behavior                               | Notification Behavior         |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| High             | Can appear in daily brief and alert candidates | Notify based on severity      |
| Medium           | Can appear in daily brief with caveat          | Notify if Severity 4/5        |
| Low              | Route to low-confidence review if Severity 3+  | Notify Sherry if Severity 4/5 |
| Needs validation | Do not distribute beyond Sherry                | Review queue only             |

### Critical Rule

```text
Severity and confidence are separate.
```

A finding can be strategically important but uncertain.

Example:

```text
Competitor hires for multiple EHR integration roles.

Severity:
4

Confidence:
Low/Medium

Routing:
Send to Sherry as a low-confidence high-severity finding. Do not send to CEO or Sales until reviewed.
```

---

## 8. Alert Routing Matrix

| Finding Condition           | Route                               |            Email Sherry? | UI Badge? |             Approval Needed? |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -----------------------: | --------: | ---------------------------: |
| Severity 1                  | Auto-archive                        |                       No |        No |                           No |
| Severity 2                  | Weekly summary                      |                       No |  Optional |                           No |
| Severity 3, high confidence | Daily brief                         |        No separate alert |       Yes |                     Optional |
| Severity 3, low confidence  | Low-confidence review queue         | Included in daily report |       Yes |                  If actioned |
| Severity 4, high confidence | Review queue + battlecard candidate |                      Yes |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Severity 4, low confidence  | Low-confidence high-severity queue  |                      Yes |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Severity 5                  | Urgent alert candidate              |          Yes immediately |       Yes |                          Yes |
| CEO relevance true          | CEO alert candidate                 |           To Sherry only |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Sales relevance true        | Sales alert candidate               |           To Sherry only |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Battlecard relevance true   | Battlecard queue                    |      Daily/weekly digest |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Product mapping uncertain   | Product mapping review queue        |             Daily digest |       Yes |                          Yes |
| Source Priority 1 failed    | Source failure alert                |                      Yes |       Yes |              Review required |
| Agent critical failure      | Agent failure alert                 |                      Yes |       Yes | No approval; action required |
| Daily run completed         | Daily brief                         |                      Yes |       Yes |                           No |
| Daily run failed            | Failure alert                       |                      Yes |       Yes |                           No |

---

## 9. Daily Brief Delivery Rules

The daily brief is the only report that should auto-send without human approval in the MVP.

### Schedule

```text
Every day
6:00 AM America/New_York run
Send after run completion
Weekend runs enabled
```

### Recipient

```text
sherry.george@doceree.com
```

### Delivery Package

The daily brief email should include:

* Email body summary
* Attached PDF
* Dashboard link
* Warning section if failures occurred
* Review queue counts
* Top findings
* Product impact summary

### Daily Brief Auto-Send Rule

```text
The daily brief should auto-send to Sherry even if it contains draft, low-confidence, or needs-review items, as long as they are clearly labeled.
```

### Daily Brief Should Not Auto-Send To

* CEO
* Sales Enablement
* Broader teams
* External users

unless Sherry approves broader distribution.

---

## 10. Daily Brief Email Template

```text

Hi Sherry,

Your daily competitive intelligence brief is ready.

Today’s strategic read:
[2–4 sentence summary]

Top findings:
1. [Competitor] — [Finding title] — Severity [X] — Confidence [Y]
2. [Competitor] — [Finding title] — Severity [X] — Confidence [Y]
3. [Competitor] — [Finding title] — Severity [X] — Confidence [Y]

Doceree products most impacted:
- [Product]
- [Product]
- [Product]

Needs your review:
- [X] Severity 4/5 findings
- [X] low-confidence findings
- [X] battlecard candidates
- [X] CEO alert candidates
- [X] Sales alert candidates
- [X] source failures

Attached:
Daily Competitive Intelligence Brief PDF

Dashboard:
```

---

## 11. Daily Brief Warning Section

If there are warnings, the email must include:

```text
Warnings:
- [X] Priority 1 sources failed
- [X] agent steps failed
- [X] findings remain low-confidence
- [X] findings need product mapping review
- [X] screenshots failed but text evidence was captured
```

### Rule

Warnings should never be hidden.

A daily brief with warnings is still useful, but Sherry must know where coverage or confidence was limited.

---

## 12. Urgent Alert Candidate Rules

An urgent alert candidate should be created when the system detects a major competitor event.

### Trigger Conditions

Create an urgent alert candidate when:

```text
Severity = 5
OR Severity = 4 and source reliability is high
OR competitor tier = 1 and signal type is major product launch
OR competitor announces major partnership/integration
OR competitor publishes strong proof point
OR competitor directly attacks or compares against Doceree
OR competitor enters a Doceree product area
OR multiple related Severity 3/4 findings form a strategic pattern
```

### Urgent Alert Recipient

Urgent alert candidates go to Sherry first.

### Auto-Send Rule

```text
Urgent alerts may be auto-sent to Sherry.
Urgent alerts may not be auto-sent to CEO or Sales without Sherry approval.
```

---

## 13. Urgent Alert Email Template

```text
Subject: Urgent Competitive Alert Candidate — [Competitor] — Severity [X]

Hi Sherry,

The command center detected a high-priority competitor signal.

Competitor:
[Name]

Signal:
[Finding title]

Severity:
[X]

Confidence:
[Y]

Doceree products impacted:
[Products]

Evidence:

[Evidence excerpt]

Dashboard:
[Finding link]
```

---

## 14. CEO Alert Candidate Rules

CEO alerts should be rare.

The system should create a CEO alert candidate only when a finding has leadership-level importance.

### CEO Alert Candidate Triggers

Create CEO alert candidate when:

```text
Severity = 5
OR competitor launches direct Doceree alternative
OR competitor announces major acquisition/funding
OR competitor announces major EHR/PMS/pharmacy/publisher partnership
OR competitor makes direct attack/comparison against Doceree
OR finding affects multiple Doceree products
OR finding threatens Doceree platform narrative
OR strategic pattern emerges across multiple competitors
```

### CEO Alert Approval Rule

```text
CEO alert candidates must not be sent to Harshit Jain until Sherry approves them.
```

### CEO Alert Content Requirements

CEO alert must include:

* Strategic read
* Why it matters
* Product areas affected
* Evidence
* Recommended leadership attention
* Caveats
* Whether action is needed now or just monitoring

---

## 15. CEO Alert Candidate Template

```text
Subject: CEO Competitive Alert Candidate — [Competitor / Theme]

Strategic read:
[One concise paragraph]

What happened:
[Competitor action]

Why it matters for Doceree:

[X]

[Y]
```

## 16. Sales Alert Candidate Rules

Sales alerts should be useful, accurate, and approved before distribution.

### Sales Alert Candidate Triggers

Create Sales alert candidate when:

```text
Finding creates likely sales objection
Finding affects active battlecard
Competitor publishes comparison page
Competitor publishes strong proof point
Competitor claims capability overlap with Doceree
Competitor launches product in Doceree area
Competitor announces partnership likely to be used in sales cycles
```

### Sales Alert Approval Rule

```text
Sales alert candidates must not be sent broadly until Sherry approves them.
```

### Sales Alert Should Include

* What changed
* What Sales may hear
* Recommended response
* Evidence
* Confidence caveat
* Battlecard link, if available

---

```text
Subject: Sales Alert Candidate — [Competitor] — [Doceree Product]

What changed:
[Short finding summary]

Why Sales may hear about this:
[Likely objection or competitor claim]

Doceree product impacted:
[Product]

Status:
```

## 18. Battlecard Notification Rules

Battlecard update candidates should appear in:

* Battlecard Queue
* Daily brief
* Weekly summary
* UI badge

### When to Notify Sherry Immediately

Notify Sherry immediately when:

```text
Battlecard candidate is linked to Severity 4 or 5 finding
Competitor publishes direct comparison page
Competitor claims measurable outcome that Sales may repeat
Competitor announces direct feature overlap
Competitor makes a claim that could create immediate sales objection
```

### When to Include in Digest Only

Include in digest when:

```text
Severity 2 or 3
No immediate Sales risk
Low-confidence
Needs product mapping review
Minor messaging change
```

---

## 19. Source Failure Alert Rules

Source failures must be visible because they create coverage gaps.

### Notify Sherry Immediately When

```text
Priority 1 source fails
Tier 1 competitor homepage fails
Tier 1 competitor product page fails
Tier 1 competitor newsroom/press source fails
A source fails two runs in a row
Crawler is blocked
Source redirects to login
Source returns 404
Screenshot and text extraction both fail
All fallback methods fail
```

### Do Not Notify Immediately When

```text
Priority 3 source fails once
Optional source fails but fallback succeeds
Screenshot fails but text is captured and source is low priority
Source is paused intentionally
Source is manual-only
```

### Source Failure Email Template

```text
Subject: Source Failure — [Competitor] — [Source Type]

Source:
[URL]

Competitor:
[Name]

Priority:
[Priority level]

Failure type:
[Timeout / 404 / blocked / extraction failure / screenshot failure / login wall / redirect]

Fallback attempted:
[Yes/No]

Fallback result:
[Successful / Failed / Not applicable]

Current source status:
[Degraded / Failed / Needs Review]

Recommended action:
[Update URL / Pause source / Manual check / Retry later]

Dashboard:
[Source health link]
```

---

## 20. Agent Failure Alert Rules

Agent failures should be routed based on criticality.

### Critical Agent Failures

Notify Sherry immediately when these fail:

```text
Market Intelligence Orchestrator
Evidence Validator
Product Mapper
Daily Brief Agent
PDF Generation
Email Delivery
Database Write
Evidence Storage
```

### Non-Critical Agent Failures

Include in daily warning section when these fail but the run can continue:

```text
Events Agent
Podcast/Video Agent
Patent/Trademark Agent
Paid Campaign Agent
Analyst Report Agent
Optional social ingest
```

### Critical Failure Rule

If the Orchestrator fails, the daily report should not be marked complete.

---

## 21. Low-Confidence Alert Rules

Low-confidence findings should not be hidden.

### Notify Sherry When

```text
Severity 4 or 5 and confidence is low
Severity 3+ and product mapping is uncertain
Finding is low-confidence but competitor is Tier 1
Finding is low-confidence but signal affects POC, NEXT, RepTwin, co-pay.com, POD, or supply-side inventory
Finding is low-confidence but repeated across multiple weak sources
```

### Low-Confidence Alert Label

```text
Low-confidence high-severity finding — evidence exists, but interpretation remains uncertain. Review before using in Sales, PMM, or leadership messaging.
```

---

## 22. Product Mapping Alert Rules

A finding should generate product-mapping review notification when:

```text
No Doceree product maps confidently
Multiple products are plausible
Demand-side and supply-side products are both implicated
Finding maps only to cross-product capability
Competitor overlap matrix conflicts with agent mapping
Signal appears category-level but strategically important
```

These alerts should usually stay in the dashboard and daily brief, unless Severity is 4 or 5.

---

## 23. Alert Approval Workflow

All high-impact alert candidates should follow this workflow.

```text
1. System creates alert candidate.
2. Alert appears in Alerts Center.
3. Sherry receives email if high priority.
4. Sherry opens alert.
5. Sherry reviews evidence.
6. Sherry edits if needed.
7. Sherry approves, rejects, archives, or requests more evidence.
8. If approved, system sends or exports alert.
9. Notification event is logged.
```

---

## 24. Alert Status Model

Every alert should have a status.

```text
draft
needs_approval
approved
rejected
sent
archived
failed_to_send
cancelled
```

### Status Definitions

| Status         | Meaning                             |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| draft          | Created by system, not yet reviewed |
| needs_approval | Requires Sherry review              |
| approved       | Approved but not yet sent           |
| rejected       | Rejected by Sherry                  |
| sent           | Delivered successfully              |
| archived       | Stored but not sent                 |
| failed_to_send | Delivery failed                     |
| cancelled      | Send cancelled before delivery      |

## 27. Alert Fatigue Controls

The system must avoid overwhelming Sherry.

### Daily Alert Limits

Recommended MVP defaults:

```text
Maximum immediate competitor alerts per day: 5
Maximum source failure emails per day: 5
Maximum agent failure emails per day: 3
Daily brief always sends regardless of count
```

If more alerts are created, they should be grouped.

### Grouping Rules

Group alerts by:

```text
competitor
Doceree product
source failure type
agent failure type
signal type
```

### Alert Digesting

If more than 5 non-urgent alerts exist, send a grouped digest:

```text
5 competitor alerts require review.
3 source failures require attention.
2 battlecard candidates were created.
```

Urgent Severity 5 alerts should not be suppressed by the cap.

```text
Severity 4 alerts can be included in the daily brief unless urgent.
Source/agent failures send immediately only if critical.
```

Future versions may add configurable quiet hours.

## 32. Alert Language Rules

Alert language must match evidence strength.

### Strong Source Language

For official product pages, docs, or press releases:

```text
Competitor announced...
Competitor now claims...
Competitor documentation indicates...
```

### Medium Source Language

For news articles, conference pages, or executive posts:

```text
A source reports...
Competitor leadership is emphasizing...
Competitor appears to be positioning around...
```

### Inferential Source Language

For jobs, social, patents, or weak signals:

```text
This may suggest...
This could indicate...
This is a potential signal of...
```

### Forbidden Alert Language

Do not use:

```text
definitely launching
proves
guaranteed
dominates
copied
will replace
is better than
has already built
```

unless directly supported by high-confidence official evidence.
