# 10. Crawl Plan

Before crawling begins, the system should build a crawl plan.

The crawl plan defines:

* Which competitors are in scope
* Which sources are in scope
* Which sources are blocked
* Which sources are manual-only
* Which sources are skipped
* Which sources require fallback
* Which crawl method to use
* Expected priority
* Expected timeout
* Expected artifact capture

---

## 10.1 Crawl Plan Object

```json id="crawl_plan_object"
{
  "run_id": "",
  "created_at": "",
  "competitors_in_scope": 0,
  "sources_total": 0,
  "sources_approved": 0,
  "sources_skipped": 0,
  "sources_blocked": 0,
  "sources_manual_only": 0,
  "sources_needing_review": 0,
  "source_items": [
    {
      "source_id": "",
      "competitor_id": "",
      "source_url": "",
      "source_type": "",
      "priority": "priority_1",
      "collection_method": "website_crawler",
      "crawl_mode": "static | browser | rss | sitemap | news_search | api | manual_skip",
      "automation_allowed": true,
      "source_compliance_status": "compliant",
      "skip_reason": "",
      "expected_artifacts": ["raw_html", "clean_text", "screenshot"],
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "retry_policy": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 10.2 Source Selection Rules

Include a source in the daily run when:

```text id="daily_source_include_rules"
source.is_active = true
competitor.is_active = true
source.approval_status = approved or conditional_approved
source.automation_allowed = true
source.collection_method is supported
source.requires_login = false
source.source_risk_level is not blocked
source is not manual_only
```

Skip source when:

```text id="daily_source_skip_rules"
source.is_active = false
competitor.is_active = false
source.approval_status = blocked
source.approval_status = manual_only
source.approval_status = needs_review
source.requires_login = true and no approved API/manual method exists
source.collection_method is unsupported
source.source_risk_level = blocked
```

---

# 11. Source Collection Batch Strategy

The crawler should avoid overloading competitor domains.

## 11.1 Batch Grouping

Group source collection by:

```text id="source_collection_batch_grouping"
competitor
domain
source priority
collection method
source type
```

## 11.2 Concurrency Defaults

```json id="source_collection_concurrency_defaults"
{
  "max_global_concurrent_sources": 10,
  "max_concurrent_per_domain": 2,
  "default_delay_between_domain_requests_ms": 2500,
  "default_static_timeout_ms": 30000,
  "default_browser_timeout_ms": 45000
}
```

## 11.3 Priority Ordering

Crawl in this order:

```text id="crawl_priority_order"
1. Priority 1 sources
2. Priority 2 sources
3. Priority 3 sources
4. Optional or low-priority sources
```

Within each priority:

```text id="crawl_priority_internal_order"
homepage
product pages
solution pages
pricing pages
newsroom / press
docs / release notes
case studies
partner / integration pages
careers / jobs
events / webinars
blogs / resources
```

---

# 12. Evidence Queue

After evidence is created, it should enter an evidence analysis queue.

## 12.1 Evidence Queue Purpose

The evidence queue prevents agents from running on every raw source.

Agents should run only on:

```text id="agent_evidence_queue_conditions"
new evidence
meaningful changes
new pages
new news articles
new jobs or job clusters
new docs/release notes
new case studies
new partnerships
high-priority baselines
manual recheck evidence
low-confidence recheck evidence
```

---

## 12.2 Evidence Queue Item

```json id="evidence_queue_item"
{
  "queue_item_id": "",
  "run_id": "",
  "evidence_id": "",
  "competitor_id": "",
  "source_id": "",
  "evidence_type": "",
  "source_type": "",
  "priority": "normal",
  "recommended_agent": "",
  "secondary_agents": [],
  "status": "queued",
  "attempt_count": 0,
  "last_error": "",
  "created_at": ""
}
```

---

## 12.3 Evidence Queue Statuses

```text id="evidence_queue_statuses"
queued
running
completed
failed
skipped
needs_review
```

---

# 13. Agent Analysis Batch Strategy

Agent analysis should be grouped and controlled.

## 13.1 Batch Grouping

Group agent analysis by:

```text id="agent_batch_grouping"
agent type
competitor
source type
evidence type
priority
```

## 13.2 Agent Concurrency Defaults

```json id="agent_concurrency_defaults"
{
  "max_global_concurrent_agent_tasks": 5,
  "max_concurrent_per_agent": 2,
  "max_retries_per_agent_task": 1,
  "agent_timeout_ms": 90000
}
```

---

## 13.3 High-Priority Evidence

High-priority evidence should be processed first.

High-priority conditions:

```text id="high_priority_evidence_conditions"
competitor tier = 1
source priority = priority_1
evidence type = product_page_change
evidence type = press_release
evidence type = partnership_page_change
evidence type = pricing_page_change
evidence type = case_study
evidence has change_score >= 80
evidence mentions Doceree-relevant keywords
evidence may map to POC, NEXT, RepTwin, co-pay.com, POD, or supply-side products
```

# 16. Retry Strategy

Retries should be controlled and transparent.

## 16.1 Retryable Operations

```text id="retryable_operations"
static crawl timeout
browser crawl timeout
temporary HTTP 5xx
HTTP 429 with backoff
screenshot failure
text extraction failure
OpenAI temporary API error
invalid JSON repair
email send failure
PDF render temporary failure
database deadlock or transient connection error
```

---

## 16.2 Non-Retryable Operations

```text id="nonretryable_operations"
blocked source
manual-only source
login wall
paywall
CAPTCHA
source compliance failure
missing evidence
unknown access basis for restricted source
possible PHI
permission denied
approval missing
invalid schema after repair attempt
```

---

## 16.3 Retry Policy Defaults

```json id="retry_policy_defaults"
{
  "static_crawl": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 3000
  },
  "browser_crawl": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 5000
  },
  "screenshot": {
    "max_attempts": 1,
    "fallback": "text_only_evidence"
  },
  "agent_task": {
    "max_attempts": 1,
    "fallback": "mark_agent_step_failed"
  },
  "json_repair": {
    "max_attempts": 1,
    "fallback": "mark_output_invalid"
  },
  "pdf_generation": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "fallback": "dashboard_report_only"
  },
  "email_delivery": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "fallback": "dashboard_notification_and_email_failed_status"
  }
}
```

---

# 17. Fallback Strategy

Fallbacks should preserve the run when safe.

## 17.1 Source Collection Fallbacks

| Failure                 | Fallback                                        |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Static crawl timeout    | Browser-rendered crawl                          |
| Browser crawl timeout   | Mark source degraded                            |
| Newsroom page fails     | RSS feed or web/news search                     |
| Screenshot fails        | Text-only evidence with missing_screenshot flag |
| Text extraction fails   | Browser extraction                              |
| Sitemap fails           | Listing page crawl                              |
| Listing page fails      | Existing approved URLs only                     |
| One article fetch fails | Continue with other articles                    |
| Jobs ATS parse fails    | Store source failure and continue               |

---

## 17.2 Agent Fallbacks

| Failure                                      | Fallback                                         |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Specialist agent fails for one evidence item | Mark item failed; continue others                |
| Product Mapper fails                         | Route finding to product mapping review          |
| Severity Scorer fails                        | Route to review with severity needs_validation   |
| Confidence Scorer fails                      | Route to review with confidence needs_validation |
| Overclaiming Guardrail fails                 | Block high-risk output until review              |
| Duplicate Detector fails                     | Continue with duplicate_warning flag             |
| Orchestrator fails                           | Stop finalization and notify Sherry              |
| Daily Brief Agent fails                      | Mark run partially_failed and notify Sherry      |

---

# 18. Scheduler Architecture

## 18.1 Local MVP Scheduler

For local MVP, use a simple scheduler.

Recommended:

```text id="local_scheduler_recommendation"
node-cron or equivalent Node scheduler
```

The scheduler should run inside:

```text id="scheduler_runtime_location"
worker process
```

not only inside a Next.js request handler.

---

## 18.2 Scheduler Responsibilities

```text id="scheduler_responsibilities"
load schedule settings
start daily run
prevent duplicate concurrent daily runs
create scheduled run record
log scheduler trigger
handle missed runs
support manual trigger
support pause/resume
```

---

## 18.3 Prevent Duplicate Runs

The system should prevent two full daily runs from running at the same time.

## Locking Rule

```text id="run_locking_rule"
Only one scheduled_daily or manual_daily run may be active at a time.
```

If a run is already active:

```text id="duplicate_run_behavior"
Do not start another full daily run.
Create skipped scheduler event.
Notify Sherry only if repeated.
```

---

## 18.4 Run Lock Object

```json id="run_lock_object"
{
  "lock_id": "",
  "lock_type": "daily_run",
  "run_id": "",
  "acquired_at": "",
  "expires_at": "",
  "status": "active"
}
```

---

## 18.5 Missed Run Handling

If the app was offline at 6:00 AM:

```text id="missed_run_handling"
1. Detect missed run on startup.
2. Check whether catch-up runs are enabled.
3. If enabled, start catch-up run.
4. Mark run_type as catch_up_daily.
5. Notify Sherry in UI that run was delayed.
```

Recommended default:

```json id="missed_run_settings"
{
  "catch_up_missed_daily_run": true,
  "maximum_catch_up_delay_hours": 6
}
```

---

# 19. Worker Architecture

The daily run should not depend on a single HTTP request.

## 19.1 Recommended MVP Worker

Create a worker process:

```text id="daily_worker_file"
src/workers/daily-run-worker.ts
```

The worker should:

```text id="daily_worker_responsibilities"
start scheduler
listen for manual run requests
execute DailyRunService
write run state updates
handle graceful shutdown
```

---

## 19.2 Worker Commands

```json id="worker_package_scripts"
{
  "worker:daily": "tsx src/workers/daily-run-worker.ts",
  "worker:retention": "tsx src/workers/retention-worker.ts",
  "worker:eval": "tsx src/workers/eval-worker.ts"
}
```

---

## 19.3 Future Worker Upgrade

If needed later, migrate to:

```text id="future_worker_options"
BullMQ
Redis-backed queues
Temporal
Cloud scheduler
Vercel cron
AWS EventBridge
Google Cloud Scheduler
```

MVP should not require this complexity unless local scheduler becomes unreliable.

---

# 20. Run Cancellation

Sherry should be able to cancel a running manual run.

Scheduled daily runs should also be cancellable by Admin if needed.

## 20.1 Cancellation Rules

Cancellation should:

```text id="run_cancellation_rules"
set cancellation_requested = true
stop scheduling new work
allow in-flight safe tasks to finish or timeout
avoid corrupting partial records
mark incomplete items skipped or cancelled
preserve logs
finalize run as cancelled or partially_failed
```

Do not cancel in a way that leaves:

* partially written evidence with missing required fields
* final findings without evidence
* notification status incorrect
* locks unreleased

---

# 21. Run Pause / Resume

MVP does not require pause/resume.

Future version may support:

```text id="future_pause_resume"
pause after source collection
resume agent analysis
pause before email send
resume daily brief generation
```

For MVP, use cancellation and rerun instead.

---

# 24. Notification Behavior for Run Outcomes

## 24.1 Successful Run

When run completes successfully:

```text id="successful_run_notification_behavior"
Send daily brief email with PDF to Sherry.
Update dashboard.
Log notification event.
```

---

## 24.2 Completed With Warnings

When run completes with warnings:

```text id="completed_with_warnings_notification_behavior"
Send daily brief email with PDF to Sherry.
Include warning section in email and PDF.
Update dashboard warning badge.
Create warning notification in UI.
```

---

## 24.3 Partially Failed

When run partially fails:

```text id="partially_failed_notification_behavior"
Notify Sherry by email if email service works.
Show dashboard alert.
Do not claim daily brief was successfully delivered if it was not.
Preserve partial outputs.
Recommend rerun or review.
```

---

## 24.4 Failed Run

When run fails:

```text id="failed_run_notification_behavior"
Notify Sherry immediately if possible.
Show dashboard critical alert.
Create failed run record.
Preserve logs.
Create recommended action.
Do not create false daily brief delivery status.
```

---

## 25.2 Rerun Rules

```text id="rerun_rules"

preserve original run logs
not overwrite original evidence
not duplicate final findings
deduplicate outputs
show parent-child relationship
```

```text id="idempotency_key_targets"
alert candidate creation
battlecard task creation
```

For email:


# Section X+21 — Report Generation, PDF Design, and Email Delivery Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines how the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center should generate reports, design PDFs, structure daily briefs, create evidence appendices, deliver emails, handle failures, store report history, and support future report formats.

The command center is not complete until it can deliver a polished, useful, evidence-backed report to Sherry automatically every morning.

The daily report is the primary user-facing output of the system.

The report must be:

- Useful
- Prioritized
- Evidence-backed
- Product-mapped
- Actionable
- Easy to read
- Easy to trust
- Easy to forward after approval
- Clear about confidence and caveats
- Clear about failures and coverage gaps

The core principle is:

> The report is not a summary of everything the system saw.  
> The report is a decision document that tells Sherry what changed, why it matters, what evidence supports it, which Doceree products are affected, and what action should happen next.

---

## 2. Report Philosophy

The report should behave like a senior competitive intelligence analyst writing for a busy PMM.

It should not behave like:

```text
A raw crawl dump.
A long AI-generated essay.
A list of every changed webpage.
A generic news digest.
A collection of unsorted findings.
A dashboard screenshot.
````

It should behave like:

```text id="report_should_behave_like"
A prioritized competitive intelligence brief.
A product impact memo.
A review queue summary.
A Sales and battlecard trigger detector.
An evidence-backed morning operating report.
```

The daily report should help Sherry answer:

```text id="daily_report_questions"
What changed?
Who changed?
Why does it matter?
Which Doceree product is affected?
How strong is the evidence?
How urgent is this?
What should I do?
What needs review?
What failed?
What should I not trust yet?
```

---

# 3. Report Types

The system should support multiple report types.

## 3.1 MVP Report Types

| Report Type                          | Purpose                                               |          Frequency | Auto-Generated |                                     Auto-Sent |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | -----------------: | -------------: | --------------------------------------------: |
| Daily Competitive Intelligence Brief | Morning summary of all meaningful competitor movement |              Daily |            Yes |                                Yes, to Sherry |
| Source Failure Report                | Coverage gaps and failed source checks                |  Daily / triggered |            Yes | Included in daily brief; urgent if Priority 1 |
| Urgent Alert Candidate PDF           | One high-severity finding for review                  |          Triggered |            Yes |              No broader send without approval |
| Weekly Agent Quality Report          | Eval and quality summary                              |             Weekly |            Yes |                                Yes, to Sherry |
| Weekly Success Scorecard             | KPIs and ROI progress                                 |             Weekly |            Yes |                                Yes, to Sherry |
| Battlecard Update Pack               | Draft battlecard changes                              | Weekly / on demand |            Yes |                No broad send without approval |
| Competitor Profile Report            | One competitor snapshot                               |          On demand |            Yes |                                            No |
| Product Impact Report                | All findings mapped to one Doceree product            |          On demand |            Yes |                                            No |
| Ask War Room Export                  | Exported answer from Ask War Room                     |          On demand |            Yes |                                            No |

---

## 3.2 Future Report Types

Future versions may support:

```text id="future_report_types"
Monthly executive competitive landscape report
Quarterly competitor strategy review
Sales enablement digest
CEO board-ready competitive summary
Product-specific battlecard delta report
Competitor launch dossier
Competitor source coverage audit
Market narrative trend report
```

---

# 4. Daily Competitive Intelligence Brief

## 4.1 Purpose

The Daily Competitive Intelligence Brief is the core morning report.

It should be generated after the daily autonomous run completes.

It should summarize:

* Meaningful findings
* High-severity changes
* Product impact
* Competitor movement
* Evidence
* Review needs
* Battlecard candidates
* CEO alert candidates
* Sales alert candidates
* Source failures
* Agent failures
* Coverage warnings

---

## 4.2 Recipient

The MVP default recipient is:

```text id="daily_brief_recipient"
Sherry George
sherry.george@doceree.com
```

The daily brief should not auto-send to CEO, Sales Enablement, or broader teams in MVP.

---

## 4.3 Delivery Timing

Default delivery:

```text id="daily_brief_delivery_timing"
After the 6:00 AM America/New_York daily run completes.
```

The system should send as soon as:

```text id="daily_brief_send_conditions"
daily brief content is generated
PDF is generated
email service is available
daily report recipient is configured
```

If the run completes with warnings, send the report with warnings clearly shown.

---

# 5. Daily Brief Structure

The daily brief should use the following structure.

```text id="daily_brief_structure"
1. Cover / Header
2. Executive Summary
3. Strategic Read
4. Top Findings
5. Product Impact Summary
6. Competitor Movement Summary
7. Severity 4/5 Review Queue
8. Low-Confidence Findings
9. Battlecard Candidates
10. CEO Alert Candidates
11. Sales Alert Candidates
12. Source and Agent Warnings
13. Evidence Appendix
14. Run Metadata
```

---

## 5.1 Cover / Header

The top of the report should include:

```text id="daily_brief_header_fields"
Report title
Report date
Generated timestamp
Run ID
Run status
Coverage summary
Report owner
Confidentiality label
```

Recommended title:

```text id="daily_brief_title"
Doceree Competitive Intelligence Brief
```

Recommended subtitle:

```text id="daily_brief_subtitle"
Daily competitor movement, product impact, and review priorities
```

Confidentiality label:

```text id="daily_brief_confidentiality"
Internal Doceree Use Only
```

---

## 5.2 Executive Summary

The Executive Summary should be short.

Recommended length:

```text id="executive_summary_length"
3–6 bullets or one short paragraph
```

It should answer:

```text id="executive_summary_answers"
What matters most today?
Which competitors moved?
Which Doceree products are affected?
Were there any Severity 4/5 items?
Were there any failures that limit coverage?
```

---

## 5.3 Strategic Read

The Strategic Read should synthesize the day’s signals.

It should not repeat every finding.

It should explain:

```text id="strategic_read_purpose"
whether a competitor appears to be moving closer to a Doceree product area
whether a pattern is emerging across competitors
whether Sales or leadership should care
whether this is a one-off signal or part of a trend
```

Example structure:

```text id="strategic_read_example_structure"
Today’s strongest signal is [theme].
The most affected Doceree product area is [product].
The evidence is [high/medium/low] confidence because [source type].
Recommended PMM action: [action].
```

---

## 5.4 Top Findings

Top Findings should be ordered by:

```text id="top_findings_order"
1. Severity
2. Confidence
3. Competitor tier
4. Doceree product impact
5. Sales / battlecard relevance
6. Recency
```

Each top finding should show:

```text id="top_finding_fields"
Finding title
Competitor
Signal type
Severity
Confidence
Doceree products impacted
Why it matters
Recommended action
Evidence summary
Review status
```

Recommended maximum:

```text id="top_findings_max"
5–7 top findings
```

If there are more than 7 important findings, the report should group them by product or competitor.

---

## 5.5 Product Impact Summary

This section should group findings by Doceree product.

```text id="product_impact_examples"
ABM

Content Marketing
RepTwin
Point-of-Care
NEXT
Clinical Intent Signals
co-pay.com
Point-of-Dispense
Admanager
Publisher AI Suite
Spark for EHRs
Spark for DOOH
Spark for Pharmacy
co-pay.com for Health Systems
```

Each product block should include:

```text id="product_impact_fields"

Number of findings
Highest severity
Affected competitors
Summary of change
Recommended PMM action
Battlecard impact
```

---

## 5.6 Competitor Movement Summary

This section should group findings by competitor.

Each competitor block should include:

```text id="competitor_summary_fields"
Competitor name
Tier
Number of sources checked
Number of findings
Highest severity
Main signal type
Products impacted
Notable source failures
```

This section should help Sherry quickly see which competitors moved today.

---

## 5.7 Severity 4/5 Review Queue

This section must be prominent.

It should list every Severity 4 and Severity 5 finding requiring Sherry review.

```text id="severity_45_review_fields"

Competitor
Severity
Confidence
Reason for severity
Evidence source
Recommended decision
Review link
```

Severity 5 findings should be visually separated.

---

```text id="low_confidence_fields"
Evidence source
Recommended next step
```

```text id="low_confidence_label"
Low-confidence finding — evidence exists, but interpretation requires review before use in Sales, PMM, or leadership messaging.
```

# 6. Daily Brief Content Rules

## 6.1 What the Report Must Include

Every daily brief must include:

```text id="daily_brief_must_include"
Executive summary
Top findings, if any
Product impact summary
Review queue counts
Source failure warnings, if any
Evidence appendix
Run metadata
PDF generation timestamp
Confidence labels
Severity labels
Draft/approved labels
```

---

## 6.2 What the Report Must Not Do

The report must not:

```text id="daily_brief_must_not"
Hide source failures
Hide low-confidence labels
Treat draft findings as approved
Treat job postings as product launches
Treat social posts as product proof
Overstate competitor claims
Use non-compliant evidence
Mix Doceree approved claims with competitor claims without distinction
Invent competitor facts
Include secrets or API keys
Include raw prompts
Include full raw HTML
Include private debug stack traces
```

---

# 7. PDF Design Principles

The PDF should be designed for reading, not decoration.

The PDF should feel like:

```text id="pdf_design_feel"
A board-ready internal intelligence brief
A PMM operating document
A clean analytics-style report
A command center export
```

It should not feel like:

```text id="pdf_should_not_feel_like"
A raw database export
A 50-page crawl log
A visually heavy slide deck
A cluttered dashboard screenshot
A generic ChatGPT answer
```

---

## 7.1 PDF Visual Style

Recommended design:

```text id="pdf_visual_style"
Light background
Doceree-style purple accent
Clean typography
Clear section hierarchy
Compact cards
Tables for evidence
Badges for severity/confidence
Minimal icons
No dark mode
No unnecessary decorative graphics
```

---

## 7.2 PDF Layout

Recommended page flow:

```text id="pdf_page_flow"
Page 1: Cover + Executive Summary
Page 2: Strategic Read + Top Findings
Page 3: Product Impact Summary
Page 4: Competitor Movement Summary
Page 5+: Finding Detail Cards
Later pages: Review Queues, Warnings, Evidence Appendix, Run Metadata
```

If there are no meaningful findings, the PDF should still generate and show:

```text id="no_findings_pdf"
No meaningful competitor movement detected today.
Sources checked: [X]
Warnings: [Y]
Review items pending: [Z]
```

---

## 7.3 PDF Length Guidelines

| Report Type                    | Recommended Length |
| ------------------------------ | -----------------: |
| Daily Brief                    |         5–12 pages |
| Daily Brief with many findings |        12–20 pages |
| Urgent Alert Candidate         |          1–3 pages |
| Weekly Quality Report          |         5–10 pages |
| Weekly KPI Scorecard           |          4–8 pages |
| Competitor Profile             |         5–15 pages |
| Product Impact Report          |         5–15 pages |
| Battlecard Update Pack         |         5–12 pages |

The system should prioritize clarity over fixed length.

# 9. PDF Generation Architecture

## 9.1 Recommended Technical Approach

Use HTML-to-PDF rendering.

Recommended local MVP:

```text id="pdf_generation_recommended_stack"
React report template
Server-side HTML render
Playwright PDF generation
Local filesystem storage
```

Why:

```text id="pdf_generation_why"
Same design system as UI
Better control over layout
Easy preview in browser
Works locally
Can later migrate to cloud rendering
```

---

## 9.2 PDF Generation Flow

```text id="pdf_generation_flow"
1. DailyBriefService creates structured report data.
2. ReportTemplateService selects template.
3. ReportRenderService renders HTML.
4. PdfGenerationService opens rendered HTML in Playwright.
5. Playwright generates PDF.
6. PdfExportService stores PDF file.
7. pdf_exports record is created.
8. PDF is attached to email.
9. PDF is linked in dashboard.
```

---

## 9.3 PDF File Naming

Use deterministic file names.

```text id="pdf_file_naming"
doceree-ci-daily-brief-YYYY-MM-DD-run-{runId}.pdf
doceree-ci-urgent-alert-{competitor}-{YYYY-MM-DD}-{alertId}.pdf
doceree-ci-weekly-quality-{YYYY-MM-DD}.pdf
doceree-ci-kpi-scorecard-week-{YYYY-MM-DD}.pdf
```

Example:

```text id="pdf_filename_example"
doceree-ci-daily-brief-2026-04-25-run-8f13.pdf
```

---

## 9.4 PDF Storage Path

Local MVP path:

```text id="pdf_storage_path"
storage/pdf_reports/
```

Suggested subfolders:

```text id="pdf_storage_subfolders"
storage/pdf_reports/daily/
storage/pdf_reports/alerts/
storage/pdf_reports/weekly/
storage/pdf_reports/on_demand/
```

---

## 9.5 PDF Export Object

```json id="pdf_export_object"
{
  "pdf_export_id": "",
  "report_type": "daily_brief",
  "related_entity_type": "daily_brief",
  "related_entity_id": "",
  "run_id": "",
  "file_name": "",
  "file_path": "",
  "file_size_bytes": 0,
  "generated_at": "",
  "generated_by": "system",
  "status": "generated",
  "error_message": "",
  "version": 1
}
```

---

# 10. PDF Generation Failure Handling

## 10.1 Retry Rules

PDF generation should retry:

```text id="pdf_retry_rules"
maximum attempts: 2
retry delay: 5 seconds
```

Retryable failures:

```text id="pdf_retryable_failures"
temporary browser crash
temporary template render error
temporary missing asset
timeout
file write transient failure
```

Non-retryable failures:

```text id="pdf_nonretryable_failures"
missing required report data
invalid report schema
storage permission failure
template not found
```

---

## 10.2 Failure Behavior

If PDF generation fails:

```text id="pdf_failure_behavior"
1. Log pdf_export status as failed.
2. Create run warning or run error.
3. Keep dashboard report available as HTML.
4. Attempt email without attachment only if configured.
5. Default MVP behavior: notify Sherry that PDF failed and dashboard version is available.
6. Do not claim PDF was attached if it was not.
```

---

## 10.3 PDF Failure Email Subject

```text id="pdf_failure_email_subject"
Doceree CI Brief Generated — PDF Failed
```

Email body should say:

```text id="pdf_failure_email_body"
The daily brief was generated, but PDF rendering failed. Please view the dashboard report while the PDF issue is resolved.
```

---

# 11. Email Delivery Specification

## 11.1 Email Purpose

Email delivery ensures Sherry receives the report without opening the dashboard.

The email should be useful even before opening the PDF.

The email body should include:

```text id="email_body_should_include"
Short strategic summary
Top 3 findings
Review queue counts
Source failure warnings
PDF attachment
Dashboard link
Delivery timestamp
```

---

## 11.2 MVP Email Provider

The MVP should support configurable SMTP.

Environment variables:

```text id="email_env_vars"
SMTP_HOST=
SMTP_PORT=
SMTP_USER=
SMTP_PASS=
SMTP_FROM=
DAILY_REPORT_RECIPIENT=sherry.george@doceree.com
```

Future providers:

```text id="future_email_providers"
SendGrid
AWS SES
Postmark
Google Workspace SMTP
Microsoft Graph
```

---

## 11.3 Email Delivery Flow

```text id="email_delivery_flow"
1. Daily brief record exists.
2. PDF export exists or PDF failure is documented.
3. Email template is selected.
4. Email body is rendered.
5. PDF is attached if available.
6. Email is sent to Sherry.
7. notification_event record is created or updated.
8. Delivery status is stored.
9. Dashboard reflects email status.
```

---

### Successful Daily Brief

```text id="daily_email_subject"
Doceree Competitive Intelligence Brief — [Date]
```

### Daily Brief With Warnings

```text id="daily_email_subject_warnings"
Doceree Competitive Intelligence Brief — [Date] — Warnings
```

### Failed Daily Run

```text id="failed_run_email_subject"
Doceree CI Daily Run Failed — [Date]
```

### Urgent Alert Candidate

```text id="urgent_alert_subject"
Urgent Competitive Alert Candidate — [Competitor] — Severity [X]
```

### Weekly Quality Report


# 16. Email Delivery Failure Handling

## 16.1 Retry Rules

Email delivery should retry:

```text id="email_retry_rules"
maximum attempts: 2
retry delay: 10 seconds
```

Retryable failures:

```text id="email_retryable_failures"
temporary SMTP connection failure
temporary provider timeout
rate limit
temporary authentication timeout
```

Non-retryable failures:

```text id="email_nonretryable_failures"
missing recipient
invalid recipient email
missing SMTP configuration
authentication rejected
attachment file missing
attachment too large, if provider rejects
```

---

## 16.2 Email Failure Behavior

If email fails:

```text id="email_failure_behavior"
1. Mark notification_event as failed.
2. Log run error or warning depending on report importance.
3. Show failure in dashboard.
4. Keep PDF available in UI.
5. Notify Sherry in UI.
6. Allow Sherry to resend manually.
7. Do not mark daily brief as delivered.
```

---

## 16.3 Manual Resend

Sherry should be able to resend the report.

Resend rules:

```text id="manual_resend_rules"
use same daily brief record
use same or regenerated PDF
create new notification_event
preserve original failed event
audit log resend action
do not duplicate findings
```

# Section X+22 — Dashboard UI, Command Center UX, and Page-by-Page Product Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the full product UI, command center UX, navigation model, dashboard structure, page-by-page requirements, component system, interaction rules, filters, empty states, permissions, and implementation requirements for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The command center should not feel like a generic AI chat product.

It should feel like:

```text
A live competitive intelligence operating room.
A PMM decision dashboard.
A product impact map.
A source-health command center.
An evidence-backed research system.
A review and approval workflow.
A daily reporting cockpit.
````

The core principle is:

> Sherry should be able to open the dashboard every morning and immediately understand what changed, what matters, what needs review, what failed, and what action to take.

---

## 2. UX Philosophy

The UI should be dashboard-first, not chat-first.

Ask War Room is important, but it should not be the main interface.

The main product experience should prioritize:

```text
visibility
trust
speed
reviewability
evidence
actionability
source health
auditability
```

The system should help Sherry answer:

```text
What happened today?
Which competitors moved?
Which Doceree products are affected?
Which findings are high severity?
Which findings are low confidence?
Which sources failed?
What needs my approval?
What should become a battlecard update?
What should Sales know?
What should the CEO know?
Can I trust this finding?
Where is the evidence?
```

---

# 3. UX Principles

## 3.1 Evidence Always Visible

Every finding, alert, battlecard task, daily brief section, and Ask War Room answer should have a visible evidence path.

The user should never wonder:

```text
Where did this come from?
```

Every intelligence object should show:

```text
evidence count
source type
source URL
captured timestamp
confidence label
raw artifact status
```

---

## 3.2 Severity and Confidence Must Be Visually Separate

Severity and confidence should never be merged into one score.

Severity answers:

```text
How important is this?
```

Confidence answers:

```text
How strongly does the evidence support this?
```

The UI should show both badges side by side.

Example:

```text
Severity 4 — Battlecard / Sales Impact
Confidence: Medium
```

---

## 3.3 Draft vs Approved Must Be Obvious

The UI must clearly distinguish:

```text
Draft
Needs Review
Approved
Rejected
Archived
Low Confidence
CEO Candidate
Sales Candidate
Battlecard Candidate
```

No reader should mistake a draft AI-generated finding for approved Doceree intelligence.

---

## 3.4 Warnings Must Not Be Hidden

The UI should surface warnings on:

* Home dashboard
* Run detail page
* Daily brief
* Source Registry
* Evidence Vault
* Alerts Center

Warnings include:

```text
source failure
agent failure
PDF failure
email failure
missing screenshot
low confidence
product mapping uncertainty
source compliance issue
raw artifact expired
```

---

## 3.5 Action Queues Over Raw Lists

The UI should avoid overwhelming Sherry with raw records.

Instead of showing only long lists, the UI should present work queues:

```text
Needs Review
Urgent
Low Confidence
Battlecard Candidates
CEO Candidates
Sales Candidates
Source Failures
Product Mapping Review
Prompt / Eval Failures
```

---

## 3.6 One Click to Evidence

From any finding, Sherry should be able to reach:

```text
finding detail
evidence detail
source page
screenshot
before/after diff
agent run
human review history
```

---

## 3.7 Command Center First, Analytics Second

The UI should prioritize operational clarity.

Analytics charts are useful, but only after the core questions are answered.

Top-level UI order should be:

```text
today's status
urgent review
product impact
competitor movement
source health
daily brief
quality metrics
```

---

# 4. Visual Design Direction

## 4.1 Overall Style

The UI should look like:

```text
Command center + analytics dashboard
```

Not:

```text
CRM
spreadsheet-only Airtable clone
generic admin panel
chatbot product
dark cyber dashboard
```

---

## 4.2 Theme

MVP theme:

```text
Light mode only
Doceree-style purple accent
Clean white background
Soft cards
Clear badges
Strong table readability
Minimal but useful charts
```

Dark mode is not required for MVP.

---

## 4.3 Density

The UI should support medium-high information density.

Competitive intelligence users need to scan many records quickly.

Recommended approach:

```text
card summaries for top-level dashboard
tables for source/finding/evidence registries
side panels for detail previews
full pages for deep review
```

---

## 4.4 Visual Hierarchy

Use clear hierarchy:

```text
Page title
Status summary
Primary action queue
Key metrics
Detailed tables
Evidence drill-down
Audit / metadata
```

---

# 39. UI Acceptance Criteria

This section is complete when the product supports the following:

1. Dashboard-first UI exists.
2. Sidebar navigation includes all core modules.
3. Top bar shows today’s run status.
4. Command Center Home shows daily status, findings, review queues, source failures, and report status.
5. Product Impact Map shows products, journey stages, findings, and open questions.
6. Competitor Radar shows competitor cards, tiers, overlaps, and source health.
7. Source Registry shows source priority, cadence, collection method, approval status, and source confidence.
8. Source Registry blocks unsupported source configurations.
9. Evidence Vault shows source URL, timestamp, excerpt, artifact status, and compliance status.
10. Findings page shows severity, confidence, product mapping, evidence count, and review status.
11. Human Review queue allows Sherry to approve, reject, edit, archive, and request more evidence.
12. Battlecards page shows draft battlecard task candidates.
13. Alerts page enforces CEO/Sales approval gates.
14. Daily Briefs page shows PDF and email status.
15. Agent Runs page shows timeline, warnings, errors, and outputs.
16. Ask War Room answers from evidence and labels low-confidence/draft findings.
17. Evals page shows agent quality and failures.
18. KPIs page shows success metrics and drill-downs.
19. Compliance page shows source and evidence compliance flags.
20. Retention page shows raw artifact expiration and retention jobs.
21. Settings page is admin-only.
22. Notification Center shows run, alert, source, email, PDF, and eval notifications.
23. Severity and confidence are visually separate everywhere.
24. Draft/approved/low-confidence states are always visible.
25. Source failures and warnings are never hidden.
26. Reader users cannot edit, approve, send, rerun, or configure.
27. Sherry/Admin can perform all owner actions.
28. Empty states are useful and do not imply false success.
29. UI does not expose secrets, raw prompts, or unsupported evidence.
30. All major UI actions are audit logged.

# Section X+23 — Database Schema Finalization and Prisma Model Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the final database schema and Prisma model specification for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The database is the command center’s source of truth.

It must store:

- Doceree products
- Product Spine claims
- Competitors
- Competitor product overlaps
- Source registry
- Source compliance policies
- Source snapshots
- Evidence
- Findings
- Product mappings
- Human review decisions
- Battlecard tasks
- Alerts
- Daily briefs
- PDF exports
- Email delivery events
- Agent runs
- Agent tool calls
- Prompt versions
- Eval examples
- Eval runs
- KPI snapshots
- Retention jobs
- Audit logs
- Users and permissions

The core principle is:

> The database must make every competitive intelligence claim traceable, reviewable, versioned, evidence-backed, and auditable.

If the database is weak, the agents will hallucinate, the UI will be inconsistent, and Sherry will not be able to trust the command center.

---

## 2. Database Philosophy

The schema should be relational-first.

Use strong relational models for:

```text
products
competitors
sources
evidence
findings
reviews
alerts
battlecards
reports
runs
users
audit logs
````

Use JSONB only where flexibility is necessary:

```text id="d4ek8r"
agent outputs
tool-call metadata
run summaries
report content snapshots
eval inputs/outputs
crawler metadata
model configuration
```

Do not hide critical business objects inside JSONB.

For example:

```text id="t2ttdd"
Bad:
Store all finding data inside one JSONB column.

Good:
Store title, severity, confidence, status, competitor_id, product mappings, and evidence links as relational fields.
Use JSONB only for supplementary structured agent metadata.
```

---

## 3. Recommended Database

Use:

```text id="db_recommendation"
PostgreSQL
+
Prisma ORM
```

Local MVP:

```text id="local_db"
PostgreSQL through Docker Compose
```

Future hosted options:

```text id="future_db_options"
Supabase Postgres
Neon
Railway Postgres
Render Postgres
AWS RDS
Google Cloud SQL
```

Recommended MVP approach:

```text id="recommended_mvp_db"
Local PostgreSQL first.
Cloud Postgres later when deployment is needed.
```

---

# 4. Schema Design Principles

## 4.1 Use UUID Primary Keys

Every major table should use:

```text id="uuid_primary_key"
id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
```

In Prisma:

```prisma id="prisma_uuid_id"
id String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
```

---

## 4.2 Use `created_at` and `updated_at`

Every mutable table should include:

```prisma id="timestamps_prisma"
createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
```

Immutable event tables may include only `createdAt`.

---

## 4.3 Use Soft Disable Before Delete

Most business records should not be deleted.

Use:

```text id="soft_disable_fields"
is_active
disabled_at
disabled_reason
archived_at
status
```

Hard delete should be reserved for:

```text id="hard_delete_allowed"
expired raw artifacts
test data
incorrect manual uploads
security-sensitive files
possible PHI
```

---

## 4.4 Preserve Version History

Version history is required for:

```text id="versioned_objects"
findings
alerts
daily briefs
prompts
reports
battlecard tasks
product mapping corrections
```

Agents must not overwrite important human-reviewed records.

---

## 4.5 Keep Evidence Immutable

Evidence is the trust layer.

Once created, raw evidence fields should not be edited through normal UI/API.

Immutable fields include:

```text id="immutable_evidence_fields"
source_url
captured_at
source_type
collection_method
excerpt
raw_html_path
clean_text_path
screenshot_path
before_text
after_text
diff_text
content_hash
visual_hash
compliance metadata
```

Corrections should be stored as:

```text id="evidence_corrections"
evidence_annotations
new evidence records
audit logs
review notes
```

---

## 4.6 Use Explicit Status Fields

Avoid ambiguous booleans when lifecycle matters.

Example:

```text id="status_examples"
review_status
alert_status
brief_status
run_status
source_approval_status
source_health_status
artifact_status
compliance_status
```

Use enums where possible.

---

# 5. Naming Conventions

## 5.1 Database Table Names

Use snake_case plural table names:

```text id="table_naming"
doceree_products
competitor_sources
finding_product_mappings
daily_briefs
agent_run_steps
```

## 5.2 Prisma Model Names

Use PascalCase singular names:

```text id="prisma_model_naming"
DocereeProduct
CompetitorSource
FindingProductMapping
DailyBrief
AgentRunStep
```

## 5.3 Field Names

In Prisma, use camelCase and map to snake_case:

```prisma id="field_mapping_example"
createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
sourceUrl String @map("source_url")
```

---

# 7. Domain 1 — Users, Permissions, Sessions

## 7.1 Purpose

This domain controls authentication, authorization, owner access, reader access, and admin actions.

## 7.2 Tables

```text id="identity_tables"
users
user_permissions
sessions
audit_logs
```

---

## 7.3 `users`


# 8. Domain 2 — Product Spine

## 8.1 Purpose

This domain stores Doceree product truth.

It must separate:

```text id="product_truth_separation"
confirmed claims
inferred claims
needs-confirmation claims
deprecated claims
```

This is critical because agents must not reuse inferred or needs-confirmation claims as approved messaging.

## 8.2 Tables

```text id="product_spine_tables"
doceree_products
product_claims
product_keywords
product_negative_keywords
product_relationships
product_signal_rules
product_open_questions
product_journey_stages
```

---

## 8.3 `doceree_products`

```prisma id="model_doceree_products"
model DocereeProduct {
  id                    String       @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name                  String       @unique
  slug                  String       @unique
  productGroup          String?      @map("product_group")
  journeyStage          String?      @map("journey_stage")
  shortDescription      String?      @map("short_description")
  plainEnglish          String?      @map("plain_english")
  strategicRole         String?      @map("strategic_role")
  primaryBuyer          String?      @map("primary_buyer")
  primaryUser           String?      @map("primary_user")
  mainProblemSolved     String?      @map("main_problem_solved")
  coreValueProposition  String?      @map("core_value_proposition")
  closestCompetitorCategory String?  @map("closest_competitor_category")
  claimStatus           ClaimStatus  @default(confirmed) @map("claim_status")
  isActive              Boolean      @default(true) @map("is_active")

  claims                ProductClaim[]
  keywords              ProductKeyword[]
  negativeKeywords      ProductNegativeKeyword[]
  signalRules           ProductSignalRule[]
  openQuestions         ProductOpenQuestion[]
  primaryMappings       FindingProductMapping[]

  createdAt             DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt             DateTime     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  @@index([journeyStage])
  @@index([claimStatus])
  @@map("doceree_products")
}
```

---

```prisma id="model_product_claims"
}
```

```prisma id="model_source_snapshots"
model SourceSnapshot {
  id                 String            @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  sourceId           String            @map("source_id") @db.Uuid

  screenshotPath     String?           @map("screenshot_path")

  rawHtmlStatus      ArtifactStatus    @default(available) @map("raw_html_status")

  previousSnapshotId String?           @map("previous_snapshot_id") @db.Uuid

  createdAt          DateTime          @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  @@index([capturedAt])

  @@map("source_snapshots")
}
```

## 11.3 `evidence`

```prisma id="model_evidence"
model Evidence {
  id                       String                  @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid

  competitorId              String?                 @map("competitor_id") @db.Uuid
  competitor                Competitor?             @relation(fields: [competitorId], references: [id])

  sourceId                  String?                 @map("source_id") @db.Uuid
  source                    CompetitorSource?       @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id])

  snapshotId                String?                 @map("snapshot_id") @db.Uuid

  evidenceType              EvidenceType            @map("evidence_type")

  canonicalUrl              String?                 @map("canonical_url")
  capturedAt                DateTime                @map("captured_at")

  sourceReliabilityScore    Float                   @default(0.5) @map("source_reliability_score")
  evidenceQualityScore      Float?                  @map("evidence_quality_score")

  excerpt                   String
  beforeText                String?                 @map("before_text")
  afterText                 String?                 @map("after_text")
  diffText                  String?                 @map("diff_text")

  rawHtmlPath               String?                 @map("raw_html_path")
  cleanTextPath             String?                 @map("clean_text_path")
  screenshotPath            String?                 @map("screenshot_path")

  rawArtifactStatus         ArtifactStatus          @default(available) @map("raw_artifact_status")
  screenshotStatus          ArtifactStatus          @default(available) @map("screenshot_status")
  rawArtifactExpiresAt      DateTime?               @map("raw_artifact_expires_at")

  sourceComplianceStatus    SourceComplianceStatus  @default(unknown) @map("source_compliance_status")

  contentHash               String?                 @map("content_hash")
  visualHash                String?                 @map("visual_hash")

  metadataJson              Json                    @default("{}") @map("metadata_json")

  findingLinks              FindingEvidence[]
  annotations               EvidenceAnnotation[]
  complianceFlags           EvidenceComplianceFlag[]

  createdAt                 DateTime                @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt                 DateTime                @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  @@index([competitorId])

  @@index([snapshotId])
  @@index([evidenceType])
  @@index([sourceType])
  @@index([capturedAt])
```

# 12. Domain 6 — Findings and Product Mappings

## 12.1 Purpose

Findings are the core intelligence objects.

A finding must be:

```text id="finding_requirements"
evidence-backed
competitor-linked
severity-scored
confidence-scored
product-mapped or explicitly unmapped
reviewable
versioned
auditable
```

## 12.2 Tables

```text id="finding_tables"
findings
finding_versions
finding_product_mappings
finding_duplicates
finding_comments
```

---

## 12.3 `findings`

```prisma id="model_findings"
model Finding {
  id                       String          @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid

  competitorId              String?         @map("competitor_id") @db.Uuid
  competitor                Competitor?     @relation(fields: [competitorId], references: [id])

  runId                     String?         @map("run_id") @db.Uuid

  title                     String
  summary                   String
  whyItMatters              String?         @map("why_it_matters")
  recommendedPmmAction      String?         @map("recommended_pmm_action")
  recommendedSalesAction    String?         @map("recommended_sales_action")

  signalType                String          @map("signal_type")
  sourceType                String?         @map("source_type")

  severity                  Int
  confidenceScore           Float           @map("confidence_score")
  confidenceLabel           ConfidenceLabel @map("confidence_label")

  status                    FindingStatus   @default(candidate)
  reviewStatus              ReviewStatus    @default(not_required) @map("review_status")

  isLowConfidence           Boolean         @default(false) @map("is_low_confidence")
  isCeoRelevant             Boolean         @default(false) @map("is_ceo_relevant")
  isSalesRelevant           Boolean         @default(false) @map("is_sales_relevant")
  isBattlecardRelevant      Boolean         @default(false) @map("is_battlecard_relevant")
  humanReviewRequired       Boolean         @default(false) @map("human_review_required")

  severityRationale         String?         @map("severity_rationale")
  confidenceRationale       String?         @map("confidence_rationale")
  productMappingRationale   String?         @map("product_mapping_rationale")
  caveats                   String[]        @default([])

  idempotencyKey            String?         @unique @map("idempotency_key")

  evidenceLinks             FindingEvidence[]
  productMappings           FindingProductMapping[]
  versions                  FindingVersion[]
  reviews                   HumanReview[]
  battlecardTasks           BattlecardTask[]
  alerts                    Alert[]

  createdAt                 DateTime        @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt                 DateTime        @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  @@index([competitorId])
  @@index([runId])
  @@index([severity])
  @@index([confidenceLabel])
  @@index([status])
  @@index([reviewStatus])
  @@index([signalType])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("findings")
}
```

## 13.3 `human_reviews`

```prisma id="model_human_reviews"
model HumanReview {
```

```prisma id="model_audit_logs"
  @@index([entityType, entityId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("audit_logs")
}
```

# 24. Required Database Constraints

## 24.1 Final Finding Must Have Evidence

This is partly application-enforced, but Codex should also enforce via service-level transaction.

Rule:

```text id="final_finding_evidence_constraint"
A finding cannot move to status = final or approved unless at least one finding_evidence record exists.
```

Implementation:

```text id="final_finding_evidence_implementation"
FindingService.finalizeFinding()
- check evidence count
- check evidence compliance
- check evidence excerpt exists
- transactionally update finding
```

---

## 24.2 CEO/Sales Alerts Require Approval

Rule:

```text id="alert_approval_constraint"
Alerts of type ceo_alert_candidate or sales_alert_candidate cannot move to sent unless approved_by_user_id and approved_at exist.
```

---

## 24.3 Raw Evidence Must Not Be Edited

Application-level enforcement:

```text id="evidence_immutability_enforcement"
EvidenceService.updateEvidence()
- block raw field changes
- allow annotations only
```

Optional DB trigger later.

---

## 24.4 Manual-Only Sources Cannot Be Crawled

Rule:

```text id="manual_only_crawl_constraint"
SourcePolicyResolver must reject crawl plan items where approval_status = manual_only.
```

# Section X+24 — Backend Services, API Routes, and Business Logic Contracts

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the backend service architecture, API route structure, business logic contracts, permission enforcement, transaction rules, validation requirements, error-handling behavior, and service-level guardrails for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The backend is the control layer of the product.

It must ensure that agents, crawlers, UI actions, scheduled jobs, report generation, alerts, battlecard updates, and human review all operate safely and consistently.

The backend must enforce rules that the UI and agents cannot be trusted to enforce alone.

The core principle is:

> The backend is the authority.  
> Agents recommend.  
> UI requests.  
> Services validate.  
> Business rules decide.  
> Database transactions preserve truth.

---

## 2. Backend Philosophy

The backend should be built as a set of clear domain services.

It should not be:

```text
A collection of random API handlers.
A frontend-driven data layer.
A direct Prisma-access free-for-all.
An agent-controlled database writer.
A brittle script that only works for the happy path.
````

It should be:

```text id="backend_should_be"
service-oriented
transaction-safe
permission-aware
evidence-first
auditable
idempotent where needed
testable
typed
modular
clear about failure states
```

Every important action should pass through a service.

Example:

```text id="service_flow_example"
UI button / scheduled job / agent runtime
  ↓
API route or worker
  ↓
Auth and permission middleware
  ↓
Domain service
  ↓
Business rule validation
  ↓
Prisma transaction
  ↓
Audit log
  ↓
Structured response
```

---

# 3. Backend Architecture Layers

The backend should use these layers:

```text id="backend_layers"
1. API Route Layer
2. Auth and Permission Middleware Layer
3. Request Validation Layer
4. Service Layer
5. Business Rule / Policy Layer
6. Data Access Layer
7. Audit / Event Layer
8. Notification / Reporting Layer
```

---

## 3.1 API Route Layer

Responsibilities:

```text id="api_route_layer_responsibilities"
receive HTTP request
authenticate user
authorize action
validate input
call service method
return structured response
handle errors consistently
```

API routes should not contain business logic beyond request orchestration.

---

## 3.2 Middleware Layer

Responsibilities:

```text id="middleware_layer_responsibilities"
require authentication
require active user
require permission
require admin for sensitive settings
apply rate limits later if needed
ensure API key is never exposed
```

---

## 3.3 Request Validation Layer

Use Zod schemas for all request bodies, query params, and service inputs.

Every API should validate:

```text id="request_validation_requirements"
required fields
UUID format
enum values
string length
array shape
date ranges
URL format
permission-sensitive action types
```

---

## 3.4 Service Layer

The service layer owns business behavior.

Services should:

```text id="service_layer_requirements"
enforce business rules
use Prisma transactions
write audit logs
call policy services
handle idempotency
return typed outputs
avoid leaking internal errors
```

---

## 3.5 Policy Layer

Policy services decide whether an action is allowed.

Examples:

```text id="policy_services_examples"
SourcePolicyResolver
ApprovalGateService
EvidenceComplianceService
EvidenceImmutabilityService
ToolPermissionService
ReportAccessPolicy
AlertRoutingPolicy
RetentionPolicyService
```

---

## 3.6 Data Access Layer

Use Prisma only inside:

```text id="prisma_allowed_locations"
services
repositories, if introduced
seed scripts
migration utilities
test setup
```

Do not use Prisma directly inside React components.

---

# 4. Required Backend Principles

## 4.1 No Final Finding Without Evidence

The backend must block final finding creation unless:

```text id="final_finding_backend_rules"
at least one evidence record exists
evidence has source URL
evidence has captured timestamp
evidence has excerpt
evidence compliance status allows use
evidence is not blocked
evidence does not contain possible PHI
```

This rule must be enforced in `FindingService.finalizeFinding()`.

---

## 4.2 No CEO or Sales Alert Without Sherry Approval

The backend must block alert sending unless:

```text id="alert_approval_backend_rules"
alert exists
alert has evidence
alert approval status is approved
approved_by_user_id exists
approved_at exists
recipient is configured
sender has permission
```

CEO and Sales alerts must never be sent directly by agents.

---

## 4.3 No Manual-Only or Blocked Source Crawl

The backend must block crawling when:

```text id="source_crawl_block_backend_rules"
source approval status is manual_only
source approval status is blocked
source approval status is needs_review
source requires login and has no approved method
source collection method is unsupported
source compliance status is non_compliant
source is LinkedIn/social and method is normal crawler
```

This rule must be enforced in `SourcePolicyResolver` and `CrawlerService`.

---

## 4.4 Raw Evidence Is Immutable

The backend must block updates to raw evidence fields.

Mutable evidence actions:

```text id="mutable_evidence_actions"
add annotation
resolve compliance flag
mark raw artifact expired
mark screenshot expired
retain artifact by exception
hide artifact through admin workflow
```

Immutable evidence fields:

```text id="immutable_evidence_backend_fields"
source_url
captured_at
collection_method
source_type
excerpt
before_text
after_text
diff_text
raw_html_path
clean_text_path
screenshot_path
content_hash
visual_hash
```

---

## 4.5 Agents Cannot Bypass Services

Agents must call tools that wrap service methods.

Agents must not write directly to database tables.

Allowed:

```text id="agent_service_allowed"
agent -> tool wrapper -> service -> policy checks -> transaction
```

Forbidden:

```text id="agent_direct_db_forbidden"
agent -> raw Prisma write
agent -> direct email send
agent -> direct alert send
agent -> direct source disable
agent -> direct permission change
```

---

# 7. Auth and Permission Middleware Contracts

## 7.1 `requireAuth()`

Purpose:

```text id="require_auth_purpose"
Ensure request has authenticated active user.
```

Behavior:

```text id="require_auth_behavior"
If no session: return AUTH_REQUIRED.
If user inactive: return PERMISSION_DENIED.
Attach user context to request.
```

---

## 7.2 `requirePermission(permissionName)`

Purpose:

```text id="require_permission_purpose"
Ensure authenticated user has required permission flag.
```

Example:

```typescript id="require_permission_example"
await requirePermission(user, "canApproveFindings")
```

Behavior:

```text id="require_permission_behavior"
If permission false: return PERMISSION_DENIED.
Write denied event to audit log for sensitive actions.
```

---

## 7.3 `requireAdmin()`

Purpose:

```text id="require_admin_purpose"
Restrict system settings, source policy, users, prompts, scheduler, and secrets metadata.
```

Allowed:

```text id="require_admin_allowed"
owner_admin
users with canAccessSettings and relevant permission
```

---

# 8. Core Service Contract Pattern

Every service method should follow this structure.

```typescript id="service_method_contract_pattern"
async function serviceMethod(input: Input, context: ServiceContext): Promise<Output> {
  validateInput(input)
  await assertPermission(context.user, "requiredPermission")
  await assertBusinessRules(input, context)

  return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    const result = await performDatabaseWork(tx, input, context)
    await auditLogService.record(tx, {
      actorUserId: context.user?.id,
      actorType: context.actorType,
      action: "action_name",
      entityType: "entity_type",
      entityId: result.id,
      metadata: {}
    })
    return result
  })
}
```

---

## 8.1 Standard `ServiceContext`

```typescript id="service_context_contract"
export type ServiceContext = {
  user?: {
    id: string
    email: string
    roleLabel: string
    permissions: Record<string, boolean>
  }
  actorType: "user" | "system" | "agent" | "scheduler"
  runId?: string
  agentName?: string
  requestId?: string
  dryRun?: boolean
  environment: "local_dev" | "test" | "dry_run" | "production"
}
```

# 10. Product Services

## 10.1 `ProductService`

Purpose:

```text id="product_service_purpose"
Manage Doceree product records used by agents, UI, and product mapping.
```

Methods:

```typescript id="product_service_methods"
getProducts(filters)
getProductById(productId)
getProductBySlug(slug)
updateProduct(productId, input, context)
getProductSpineContext()
getProductMappingContext()
```

Business rules:

```text id="product_service_business_rules"
Only Sherry/Admin can edit product records.
Confirmed, inferred, and needs-confirmation claims must remain separated.
Needs-confirmation claims cannot be marked approved without review.
Product edits must be audit logged.
Product updates should create version history if messaging-impacting fields change.
```

API routes:

```text id="product_api_routes"
GET /api/products
GET /api/products/:productId
```

# 12. Source Registry and Policy Services

## 12.1 `SourceRegistryService`

Purpose:

```text id="source_registry_service_purpose"
Manage competitor sources and source configuration.
```

Methods:

```typescript id="source_registry_methods"

updateSource(sourceId, input, context)

approveSource(sourceId, input, context)
markManualOnly(sourceId, reason, context)
markBlocked(sourceId, reason, context)
testCrawlSource(sourceId, context)
```

Business rules:

```text id="source_registry_rules"
Only Sherry/Admin can create or edit sources.
Source URL must be valid.
Collection method must be supported.
LinkedIn/social cannot use website_crawler or browser_rendered_crawler.
Manual-only source cannot be test crawled.
Blocked source cannot be test crawled.
Gated/paid sources cannot have automation_allowed=true unless approved API/vendor path exists.
Source policy changes are audit logged.
```

API routes:

```text id="source_registry_api_routes"
GET /api/sources
GET /api/sources/:sourceId
POST /api/sources
PUT /api/sources/:sourceId

GET /api/sources/:sourceId/snapshots
```

## 12.2 `SourcePolicyResolver`

Purpose:

```text id="source_policy_resolver_purpose"
Determine whether a source can be crawled, skipped, manually ingested, or blocked.
```

Input:

```typescript id="source_policy_input"
type SourcePolicyInput = {
  sourceId: string
  sourceType: string
  url: string
  collectionMethod: CollectionMethod
  automationAllowed: boolean
  requiresLogin: boolean
  approvalStatus: SourceApprovalStatus
  complianceStatus: SourceComplianceStatus
  sourceRiskLevel: SourceRiskLevel
  accessBasis: string
}
```

Output:

```typescript id="source_policy_output"
type SourcePolicyDecision = {
  allowed: boolean
  decision: "allow" | "skip" | "manual_only" | "blocked" | "needs_review"
  reason: string
  requiredAction?: string
  canCreateEvidence: boolean
  canSupportFinalFinding: boolean
}
```

Blocking rules:

```text id="source_policy_blocking_rules"
approval_status = blocked -> block
approval_status = manual_only -> manual_only
approval_status = needs_review -> needs_review
requires_login = true and no approved API/manual path -> block
source_type includes LinkedIn/social and collection method is crawler -> block
access_basis unknown for paid/gated source -> block
compliance_status non_compliant -> block
```

---

# 13. Crawler, Snapshot, and Diff Services

## 13.1 `CrawlerService`

Purpose:

```text id="crawler_service_purpose"
Fetch approved public sources and create raw artifacts for snapshotting.
```

Methods:

```typescript id="crawler_service_methods"
crawlSource(sourceId, context)
crawlCompetitor(competitorId, context)
testCrawlSource(sourceId, context)
```

Business rules:

```text id="crawler_service_rules"
Call SourcePolicyResolver before every crawl.
Never crawl blocked or manual-only sources.
Never crawl unsupported social sources through browser automation.
Record source health whether crawl succeeds or fails.
Do not create findings directly.
Only create snapshots and evidence candidates.
```

---

## 13.2 `SnapshotService`

Purpose:

```text id="snapshot_service_purpose"
Store raw crawl artifacts and compare current source state to prior state.
```

Methods:

```typescript id="snapshot_service_methods"
createSnapshot(input, context)
getPreviousSnapshot(sourceId)
linkSnapshotToPrevious(snapshotId, previousSnapshotId)
markBaseline(snapshotId)
expireSnapshotArtifacts(snapshotId)
```

Business rules:

```text id="snapshot_service_rules"
First crawl creates baseline.
Baseline does not create change finding.
Raw HTML and screenshots follow retention policy.
Snapshot creation must be idempotent by run_id + source_id + content_hash.
```

---

## 13.3 `DiffService`

Purpose:

```text id="diff_service_purpose"
Compare source snapshots and classify changes.
```

Methods:

```typescript id="diff_service_methods"
computeTextDiff(previousSnapshotId, currentSnapshotId)
computeChangeScore(diff)
suppressBoilerplate(diff)
classifyChange(diff)
```

Business rules:

```text id="diff_service_rules"
Ignore footer, nav, cookie banner, copyright year, tracking script, and cosmetic changes.
Meaningful changes create evidence.
Trivial changes may be logged but should not create candidate findings.
```

---

# 28. Idempotency Contracts

```text id="idempotent_operations_backend"
alert candidate creation

```

---

## 28.2 Idempotency Service

Methods:

```typescript id="idempotency_service_methods"
createKey(scope, parts)
checkExisting(key)
recordResult(key, entityType, entityId)
assertNoConflict(key, requestHash)
```

Behavior:

```text id="idempotency_behavior_backend"
Same request with same key returns existing result.
Same key with different payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
Retries do not duplicate findings, emails, PDFs, or evidence.
```

# 29. Transaction Contracts

Use Prisma transactions for multi-step business changes.

## 29.1 Required Transactions

```text id="required_transactions_backend"
finalize finding
approve finding
edit and approve finding
reject finding
create alert candidate
approve alert
send alert
create battlecard task
publish battlecard task
generate daily brief
generate PDF export record
send email notification event
run retention cleanup
resolve compliance flag
update source policy
change user permissions
activate prompt version
```

---

## 29.2 Transaction Example — Approve Finding

```typescript id="approve_finding_transaction_example"
await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  const current = await tx.finding.findUnique({ where: { id: findingId } })

  await tx.findingVersion.create({
    data: {
      findingId,
      versionNumber: nextVersion,
      changeReason: "approved_by_sherry",
      title: current.title,
      summary: current.summary,
      contentSnapshot: current
    }
  })

  const finding = await tx.finding.update({
    where: { id: findingId },
    data: {
      status: "approved",
      reviewStatus: "approved"
    }
  })

  await tx.humanReview.create({
    data: {
      findingId,
      reviewerUserId: context.user.id,
      decision: "approved"
    }
  })

  await tx.auditLog.create({
    data: {
      actorUserId: context.user.id,
      actorType: "user",
      action: "finding_approved",
      entityType: "finding",
      entityId: findingId
    }
  })

  return finding
})
```

# Section X+25 — Crawler, Diff Engine, and Source Collection Implementation Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the source collection layer for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The crawler and diff engine are the evidence factory of the product.

They are responsible for turning approved competitor sources into durable, timestamped, structured evidence that agents can safely analyze.

The crawler must not behave like a generic scraper.

It must behave like a disciplined competitive intelligence collection system that knows:

- Which sources are approved.
- Which sources are manual-only.
- Which sources are blocked.
- Which collection method is allowed.
- Which pages are high-value.
- Which changes are meaningful.
- Which changes are noise.
- Which artifacts need to be stored.
- Which evidence is strong enough for agent interpretation.
- Which collection failures should be surfaced to Sherry.

The core principle is:

> The crawler collects proof.  
> The diff engine detects meaningful change.  
> The Evidence Vault stores the record.  
> Agents interpret only after evidence exists.

---

## 2. Crawler Philosophy

The crawler should prioritize reliability, traceability, and source compliance over brute-force coverage.

It should not try to scrape everything on the internet.

It should collect from:

```text
approved competitor sources
approved public pages
approved RSS/news feeds
approved sitemaps
approved docs/release pages
approved public careers pages
approved public case studies
approved manual uploads
approved API/vendor/manual social inputs
````

It should not collect from:

```text
blocked sources
manual-only sources through automation
login walls
paywalls without approved access basis
CAPTCHA-gated pages
unauthorized LinkedIn/social pages
private groups
restricted portals
unknown-access gated reports
```

The crawler’s job is not to create final intelligence.

The crawler’s job is to produce:

```text
snapshots
clean text
screenshots
content hashes
diffs
change classifications
evidence records
source health records
crawl errors
```

---

# 3. Source Collection Architecture

## 3.1 High-Level Flow

```text id="source_collection_high_level_flow"
1. DailyRunService creates a crawl plan.
2. SourcePolicyResolver checks every source.
3. Approved sources are queued for collection.
4. CrawlerService selects collection method.
5. Source page is fetched or rendered.
6. Raw HTML is stored.
7. Main content is extracted.
8. Boilerplate is removed.
9. Screenshot is captured where required.
10. Content hashes are calculated.
11. SourceSnapshot is created.
12. Previous snapshot is loaded.
13. DiffService compares previous vs current.
14. ChangeClassifierService classifies change.
15. Trivial changes are suppressed.
16. Meaningful changes create evidence.
17. SourceHealthService records success or failure.
18. EvidenceQueueService queues meaningful evidence for agents.
```

---

## 3.2 Collection Services

Codex should implement these services:

```text id="crawler_collection_services"
CrawlerService
StaticCrawlerService
BrowserCrawlerService
SitemapDiscoveryService
RssFeedService
NewsSearchIngestionService
CareersPageCollector
DocsReleaseNotesCollector
CaseStudyCollector
PartnerIntegrationCollector
ManualUploadCollector
ApprovedSocialIngestionService
TextExtractionService
BoilerplateRemovalService
ScreenshotService
SnapshotService
DiffService
SemanticDiffService
ChangeClassifierService
SourceHealthService
CrawlerRetryService
CrawlPlanService
ArtifactStorageService
EvidenceCreationService
```

---

## 3.3 Collection Method Ownership

Each source type should have an explicit collection method.

The system should not guess silently.

If method is unknown:

```text id="unknown_collection_method_behavior"
mark source as needs_review
do not crawl
create source compliance warning
surface in Source Registry
```

| Newsroom              | rss_feed, sitemap_monitor, crawler   |   Optional |  Yes |               Yes | Prefer RSS/sitemap if available |
| Press release         | rss_feed, news_search, crawler       |   Optional |  Yes |               Yes | High-confidence official source |
| Blog                  | rss_feed, sitemap_monitor, crawler   |   Optional |  Yes |   Yes if relevant | Often noisy                     |
| Resource center       | sitemap_monitor, crawler             |   Optional |  Yes |   Yes if relevant | Whitepapers/guides              |
| Case study            | crawler                              |        Yes |  Yes |               Yes | Battlecard/proof-point signal   |
| Docs/help center      | sitemap_monitor, crawler             |   Optional |  Yes |               Yes | Product truth signal            |
| Release notes         | rss_feed, sitemap_monitor, crawler   |   Optional |  Yes |               Yes | Product change signal           |
| Partner page          | crawler                              |        Yes |  Yes |               Yes | Integration/partnership signal  |
| Integration page      | crawler                              |        Yes |  Yes |               Yes | Technical depth signal          |
| Event/webinar page    | crawler                              |   Optional |  Yes |   Yes if relevant | Narrative signal                |
| Careers page          | crawler / ATS parser                 |         No |  Yes | Yes if meaningful | Directional only                |
| Job posting           | crawler / ATS parser                 |         No |  Yes |               Yes | Not launch proof                |
| Investor relations    | rss_feed / crawler                   |   Optional |  Yes |               Yes | Public-co strategic signal      |
| Manual upload         | manual_upload                        |         No |   No |  Yes after review | Requires access basis           |
| Approved social input | approved_social_tool / manual_export |         No |   No |               Yes | No unauthorized scraping        |
