# 6. Source Policy Enforcement

## 6.1 SourcePolicyResolver Must Run Before Every Collection

No source should be collected until this function returns `allowed = true`.

```typescript id="source_policy_resolver_contract"
type SourcePolicyDecision = {
  sourceId: string
  allowed: boolean
  decision: "allow" | "skip" | "manual_only" | "blocked" | "needs_review"
  reason: string
  collectionMethod: string
  canCreateEvidence: boolean
  canSupportFinalFinding: boolean
  requiredAction?: string
}
```

---

## 6.2 Blocking Rules

The crawler must block:

```text id="crawler_blocking_rules"
approval_status = blocked
approval_status = manual_only
approval_status = needs_review
approval_status = disabled
source_compliance_status = non_compliant
source_risk_level = blocked
requires_login = true and no approved API/manual method exists
collection_method = blocked
source_type = LinkedIn company page with crawler method
source_type = executive LinkedIn profile with crawler method
source_type = analyst report with automation allowed
source_type = gated webinar with automation allowed
access_basis = unknown for paid/gated source
possible PHI detected
```

---

## 6.3 Skip Behavior

When a source is skipped, the system should:

```text id="crawler_skip_behavior"
create crawl_plan_item with skipped status
record skip_reason
create run warning if priority_1
show skipped source in run detail
do not create snapshot
do not create evidence
do not run agents
```

---

## 6.4 Manual-Only Behavior

Manual-only sources should be visible but not crawled.

UI should show:

```text id="manual_only_ui_warning"
Manual-only source — upload approved excerpts or files. Automated crawling is disabled.
```

---

# 7. Crawl Plan Specification

## 7.1 Crawl Plan Purpose

The crawl plan is the source collection blueprint for a run.

It should be created before any collection begins.

It answers:

```text id="crawl_plan_questions"
Which sources will be checked?
Which sources will be skipped?
Which method will be used?
Which priority applies?
Which timeout applies?
Which artifacts are expected?
Which source policy decision was made?
```

---

## 7.2 Crawl Plan Item

```json id="crawl_plan_item_spec"
{
  "run_id": "",
  "competitor_id": "",
  "source_id": "",
  "source_url": "",
  "source_type": "product_page",
  "priority": "priority_1",
  "frequency": "daily",
  "collection_method": "browser_rendered_crawler",
  "crawl_mode": "browser",
  "automation_allowed": true,
  "source_compliance_status": "compliant",
  "policy_decision": "allow",
  "skip_reason": "",
  "expected_artifacts": [
    "raw_html",
    "clean_text",
    "screenshot"
  ],
  "timeout_ms": 45000,
  "retry_policy": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 5000
  }
}
```

---

# 8. Collection Cadence Rules

## 8.1 Priority-Based Cadence

Use source priority to determine default cadence.

```text id="priority_cadence"
Priority 1 -> daily
Priority 2 -> weekly
Priority 3 -> monthly
Priority 4 -> archive only / manual
```

---

## 8.2 Competitor Tier Adjustment

Use competitor tier to adjust cadence.

```text id="competitor_tier_cadence"
Tier 1:
  Priority 1 daily
  Priority 2 weekly
  Priority 3 monthly

Tier 2:
  Priority 1 weekly
  Priority 2 weekly
  Priority 3 monthly

Tier 3:
  All sources monthly
  Full deep crawl only on trigger
```

---

## 8.3 Triggered Collection

Trigger extra collection when:

```text id="triggered_collection_events"
Severity 4/5 finding appears
competitor has 3+ Severity 3 findings in 30 days
new source is approved
source failed and is re-enabled
Sherry manually triggers refresh
new competitor is added
source is marked priority_1
```

---

# 9. Static Crawler Specification

## 9.1 Purpose

The static crawler should fetch simple public pages quickly.

Use for:

```text id="static_crawler_use_cases"
RSS pages
simple HTML pages
press release pages
blog pages
resource center listing pages
simple case study pages
sitemap URLs
```

---

## 9.2 Static Crawler Requirements

```text id="static_crawler_requirements"
HTTP GET
timeout support
redirect support
status code capture
content-type capture
final URL capture
HTML size limit
user-agent configuration
retry on 5xx or timeout
do not retry blocked policy failures
```

---

## 9.3 Static Crawl Output

```json id="static_crawl_output"
{
  "source_id": "",
  "requested_url": "",
  "final_url": "",
  "http_status": 200,
  "content_type": "text/html",
  "raw_html": "",
  "headers": {},
  "fetched_at": "",
  "duration_ms": 0,
  "error": null
}
```

---

# 10. Browser Crawler Specification

## 10.1 Purpose

The browser crawler should render pages that require JavaScript.

Use for:

```text id="browser_crawler_use_cases"
homepages
product pages
solution pages
pricing pages
modern marketing pages
SPA pages
interactive case study pages
partner/integration pages
```

---

## 10.2 Browser Crawler Requirements

Use Playwright.

Requirements:

```text id="browser_crawler_requirements"
headless browser
configurable viewport
wait until network idle or main content selector
capture final URL
capture DOM HTML
capture visible text
capture screenshot
capture page title
capture meta description
block unnecessary heavy assets if safe
timeout support
graceful error capture
```

---

## 10.3 Browser Crawl Output

```json id="browser_crawl_output"
{
  "source_id": "",
  "requested_url": "",
  "final_url": "",
  "page_title": "",
  "meta_description": "",
  "raw_html": "",
  "visible_text": "",
  "screenshot_path": "",
  "captured_at": "",
  "duration_ms": 0,
  "browser_console_errors": [],
  "error": null
}
```

---

# 11. Sitemap Discovery Specification

## 11.1 Purpose

Sitemaps help discover new public pages without deep crawling the entire site.

Use sitemap discovery for:

```text id="sitemap_discovery_use_cases"
newsroom pages
blog pages
resources
case studies
docs/help centers
release notes
partner pages
integration pages
```

---

## 11.2 Sitemap Sources

Check:

```text id="sitemap_sources"
/sitemap.xml
/sitemap_index.xml
/robots.txt sitemap references
known CMS sitemap patterns
source-provided sitemap URL
```

---

## 11.3 Sitemap Discovery Output

```json id="sitemap_discovery_output"
{
  "source_id": "",
  "sitemap_url": "",
  "urls_discovered": 0,
  "new_urls": [],
  "changed_urls": [],
  "skipped_urls": [],
  "errors": []
}
```

---

## 11.4 Discovery Rules

Do not automatically activate every discovered URL.

Instead:

```text id="sitemap_discovery_rules"
auto-collect URLs matching approved source patterns
queue unknown URL patterns for review
deduplicate canonical URLs
exclude obvious tag/category/archive pages unless useful
exclude non-business assets
exclude login or gated paths
```

---

# 12. RSS Feed Specification

## 12.1 Purpose

RSS feeds are preferred for blogs, newsrooms, and press releases when available.

RSS is more stable and less noisy than visual page crawling.

---

## 12.2 RSS Requirements

```text id="rss_requirements"
fetch feed
parse items
capture title
capture URL
capture published date
capture summary
deduplicate by canonical URL and GUID
fetch full article page if new
create evidence for new relevant items
```

---

## 12.3 RSS Output

```json id="rss_output"
{
  "feed_url": "",
  "items_seen": 0,
  "new_items": [],
  "duplicate_items": [],
  "errors": []
}
```

---

# 13. News Search Ingestion Specification

## 13.1 Purpose

News search catches external articles and announcements that competitor-owned sources may not surface quickly.

Use for:

```text id="news_search_use_cases"
press coverage
funding news
acquisition news
third-party commentary
partnership coverage
public-company coverage
syndicated press releases
```

---

## 13.2 News Search Query Pattern

For each competitor:

```text id="news_query_pattern"
"[Competitor Name]" AND ("launch" OR "partnership" OR "acquisition" OR "funding" OR "healthcare" OR "pharma" OR "EHR" OR "AI" OR "patient access")
date range: last 24 hours
```

---

## 13.3 News Ingestion Rules

```text id="news_ingestion_rules"
deduplicate syndicated articles
prefer official source as canonical if available
store publisher
store published date
store captured date
store article URL
store excerpt
label third-party sources as medium confidence unless corroborated
do not create duplicate findings for syndicated copies
```

---

# 14. Careers and Jobs Collection Specification

## 14.1 Purpose

Jobs are directional signals about investment, hiring priorities, product focus, and market expansion.

Jobs must not be treated as proof of launch.

---

## 14.2 Careers Collector Requirements

```text id="careers_collector_requirements"
support standard careers pages
support ATS links where public
extract job title
extract department
extract location
extract job description excerpt
extract posted date if available
detect duplicate job reposts
cluster related jobs by theme
```

---

## 14.3 Jobs Signal Categories

```text id="job_signal_categories"
EHR integration
FHIR / HL7
pharmacy PMS
patient access
co-pay / affordability
AI / virtual rep
publisher monetization
programmatic media
identity graph
clinical intent
data partnerships
sales expansion
market expansion
```

---

## 14.4 Jobs Evidence Caveat

Every jobs-derived evidence record should include:

```text id="jobs_evidence_caveat"
Job postings are directional signals, not proof of product launch.
```

---

# 15. Manual Upload Collection Specification

## 15.1 Purpose

Manual upload supports sources that should not be crawled automatically.

Examples:

```text id="manual_upload_examples"
analyst reports
gated webinar notes
conference notes
licensed reports
manual social exports
human-provided excerpts
sales-call competitor notes
```

---

## 15.2 Manual Upload Requirements

Manual upload must collect:

```text id="manual_upload_requirements"
uploaded_by_user_id
source_description
competitor_id if applicable
source_type
access_basis
usage_rights_note
contains_phi_confirmation
contains_sensitive_data_confirmation
retention_class
file_path
extracted_text if allowed
```

---

## 15.3 Manual Upload Blocking

Block or route to review if:

```text id="manual_upload_blocking"
access_basis is unknown
user indicates possible PHI
file appears to contain patient identifiers
file contains credentials or secrets
file type unsupported
```

---

# 16. Approved Social Ingestion Specification

## 16.1 Purpose

Social signals are useful for narrative tracking, executive emphasis, and product positioning, but must come from approved sources only.

Allowed inputs:

```text id="approved_social_allowed_inputs"
approved API
licensed social listening vendor
manual export
human-provided post text
approved internal upload
```

Not allowed:

```text id="approved_social_not_allowed"
unauthorized scraping
browser automation against restricted social platforms
credential sharing
private group extraction
personal profile scraping
contact harvesting
```

---

## 16.2 Social Evidence Caveat

Every social-derived evidence record should include:

```text id="social_evidence_caveat"
Social evidence reflects public narrative or executive emphasis. It should not be treated as confirmed product capability unless supported by official product, docs, or announcement evidence.
```

---

# 17. Artifact Storage Specification

## 17.1 Artifact Types

The collector should store:

```text id="artifact_types"
raw_html
clean_text
screenshot
diff_text
metadata_json
downloaded_pdf
manual_upload_file
rendered_page_pdf_optional
```

---

## 17.2 Storage Paths

Local MVP:

```text id="artifact_storage_paths"
storage/html_snapshots/
storage/clean_text/
storage/screenshots/
storage/diffs/
storage/downloaded_files/
storage/manual_uploads/
```

---

## 17.3 File Naming

Use deterministic file names.

```text id="artifact_file_naming"
{sourceId}-{YYYYMMDDHHmmss}-{artifactType}-{hashPrefix}.ext
```

Examples:

```text id="artifact_file_examples"

source_123-20260425060200-diff-a82fd1.txt
```

```json id="artifact_metadata"
  "created_at": "",

}
```

Text extraction converts raw pages into clean text for diffing and agent analysis.

## 18.2 Extraction Inputs

```text id="text_extraction_inputs"
raw HTML
visible text
page title
meta description
structured data JSON-LD
article body if available
main content selector if configured
```

```text id="text_extraction_requirements"
remove script/style/nav/footer
remove cookie banner text
remove repetitive CTAs
remove newsletter sign-up boilerplate
preserve headings
preserve product names
preserve feature claims
preserve metrics
preserve customer names
preserve dates
preserve partner names
preserve pricing terms
preserve release note entries
```

## 18.4 Clean Text Output

```json id="clean_text_output"
{

}
```

# 19. Boilerplate Removal Specification

## 19.1 Boilerplate to Suppress

Suppress:

```text id="boilerplate_suppress"
headers
footers
cookie banners
privacy banners
newsletter signups
global navigation
social share widgets
related content widgets
pagination
copyright year
tracking script changes
CSS/JS bundle changes
chatbot widget changes
generic CTA buttons repeated site-wide
```

---

## 19.2 Content to Preserve

Preserve:

```text id="boilerplate_preserve"
hero copy
product names
feature claims
use case language
buyer/persona language
customer logos
case study metrics
pricing or packaging claims
integration names
partner names
release note entries
docs API details
compliance claims
clinical workflow language
EHR/PMS/pharmacy/co-pay/AI language
```

---

# 20. Snapshot Specification

## 20.1 Snapshot Purpose

A snapshot represents the state of a source at one point in time.

Snapshots are not findings.

Snapshots are raw collection records.

---

## 20.2 Snapshot Creation Rules

Create a snapshot when:

```text id="snapshot_creation_rules"
source crawl succeeds
manual upload is accepted
RSS item is fetched
news article is fetched
public job page is fetched
docs/release page is fetched
```

Do not create a snapshot when:

```text id="snapshot_no_create_rules"
source policy blocks collection
source is skipped
source fails before any content is captured
manual upload is rejected
```

---

## 20.3 Snapshot Fields

```json id="snapshot_fields"
{
  "source_id": "",
  "run_id": "",
  "captured_at": "",
  "url": "",
  "final_url": "",
  "http_status": 200,
  "content_hash": "",
  "main_content_hash": "",
  "visual_hash": "",
  "raw_html_path": "",
  "clean_text_path": "",
  "screenshot_path": "",
  "previous_snapshot_id": "",
  "is_baseline": false,
  "change_score": 0,
  "change_summary": "",
  "metadata_json": {}
}
```

---

# 21. First-Day Baseline Rule

## 21.1 Purpose

The first crawl creates the baseline.

It should not trigger false “changed” findings.

---

## 21.2 Behavior

On first crawl of a source:

```text id="first_day_baseline_behavior"
create snapshot
mark is_baseline = true
store raw HTML
store clean text
store screenshot where applicable
create baseline evidence only for high-priority product/source pages if configured
do not create website_change finding
do not trigger alert
do not trigger battlecard task
show source as baseline established
```

---

## 21.3 Optional Baseline Summary

For Priority 1 sources, the system may create a baseline summary evidence record:

```text id="baseline_summary_behavior"
evidence_type = website_snapshot
purpose = baseline context
agent_queue = optional
finding_creation = disabled unless Sherry manually requests baseline analysis
```

---

# 22. Diff Engine Specification

## 22.1 Purpose

The diff engine compares current snapshot against previous snapshot and identifies meaningful content change.

---

## 22.2 Diff Inputs

```text id="diff_inputs"
previous clean text
current clean text
previous main content hash
current main content hash
previous screenshot hash
current screenshot hash
source type
source priority
known boilerplate patterns
source-specific ignored selectors
```

---

## 22.3 Diff Outputs

```json id="diff_outputs"
{
  "has_change": true,
  "change_score": 82,
  "added_text": [],
  "removed_text": [],
  "changed_sections": [],
  "boilerplate_suppressed": [],
  "change_summary": "",
  "recommended_change_type": "feature_change",
  "is_trivial": false,
  "requires_agent_analysis": true
}
```

---

## 22.4 Change Score

Change score should combine:

```text id="change_score_components"
text difference magnitude
business keyword match
source type importance
source priority
competitor tier
new named product/feature
new partner/customer
new metric/proof point
pricing/commercial language
clinical/EHR/pharmacy/co-pay/AI terminology
removed important claim
```

Suggested range:

```text id="change_score_range"
0–20 = trivial/noise
21–40 = minor
41–60 = moderate
61–80 = meaningful
81–100 = high-impact
```

---

# 23. Change Classification

## 23.1 Required Change Categories

```text id="change_categories"
trivial_change
positioning_change
messaging_change
product_launch
feature_change
new_use_case
new_persona
new_category_language
new_case_study
new_customer_logo
new_proof_point
pricing_packaging_signal
new_partnership
new_integration
docs_capability_change
release_note_change
job_posting_signal
event_webinar_signal
compliance_claim
acquisition_funding_signal
executive_change
source_structure_change
unknown
```

---

## 23.2 Category Rules

### `trivial_change`

Examples:

```text id="trivial_change_examples"
copyright year
footer link
cookie banner
nav label
CSS class
tracking script
newsletter module
minor punctuation
```

Default:

```text id="trivial_change_default"
do not create candidate finding
archive or log only
```

---

### `product_launch`

Requires strong evidence such as:

```text id="product_launch_evidence"
new product page
official press release
explicit launch language
release note stating availability
pricing/package page with product SKU
```

Do not classify job/social-only evidence as launch.

---

### `feature_change`

Signals:

```text id="feature_change_signals"
new feature claim
new workflow
new capability
new module
new API
new targeting method
new reporting feature
```

---

### `new_partnership`

Signals:

```text id="partnership_signals"
official partnership announcement
partner page added
integration listing added
press release naming partner
docs showing technical integration
```

---

### `new_proof_point`

Signals:

```text id="proof_point_signals"
case study metric
customer outcome
NRx / TRx lift
engagement lift
ROI claim
named customer logo
methodology note
```

---

### `job_posting_signal`

Signals:

```text id="job_posting_signal_examples"
new role mentioning EHR integration
new role mentioning FHIR/HL7
new role mentioning pharmacy PMS
new role mentioning AI rep
new role mentioning patient access
```

Required caveat:

```text id="job_posting_change_caveat"
Directional hiring signal, not proof of launch.
```

---

# 24. Business Relevance Classifier

## 24.1 Purpose

Not every change should reach agents.

The Business Relevance Classifier decides whether evidence should enter the agent queue.

---

## 24.2 Relevance Inputs

```text id="business_relevance_inputs"
change category
change score
source type
source priority
competitor tier
Doceree product keyword matches
negative keyword matches
product signal rules
competitor product overlap
business terms
new named entities
historical duplicate status
```

---

## 24.3 Relevance Output

```json id="business_relevance_output"
{
  "business_relevant": true,
  "relevance_score": 87,
  "matched_doceree_products": [
    "Point-of-Care",
    "NEXT"
  ],
  "matched_signal_rules": [
    "real_time_clinical_trigger",
    "EHR_integration"
  ],
  "negative_keyword_hit": false,
  "recommended_agent": "Website Change Hunter",
  "reason": "New official product-page language references EHR prescribing moment and real-time triggers."
}
```

---

## 24.4 Suppression Rules

Suppress or downgrade when:

```text id="business_relevance_suppression"
negative keyword hit indicates false positive
change is boilerplate
source is low priority and generic
same change already processed
new text is generic SEO with no healthcare/product overlap
source confidence is low and no corroboration
```

---

# 25. Evidence Creation from Diff

## 25.1 When to Create Evidence

Create evidence when:

```text id="evidence_from_diff_create_conditions"
change is meaningful
change score >= threshold
change category is not trivial_change
source policy allows evidence creation
source compliance status allows use
excerpt can be generated
source URL exists
captured timestamp exists
```

---

## 25.2 Evidence Fields from Diff

```json id="evidence_from_diff_fields"
{
  "evidence_type": "website_change",
  "source_type": "product_page",
  "source_url": "",
  "captured_at": "",
  "collection_method": "",
  "excerpt": "",
  "before_text": "",
  "after_text": "",
  "diff_text": "",
  "source_reliability_score": 0.95,
  "source_compliance_status": "compliant",
  "raw_html_path": "",
  "clean_text_path": "",
  "screenshot_path": "",
  "raw_artifact_status": "available",
  "screenshot_status": "available"
}
```

---

## 25.3 Excerpt Generation Rules

The excerpt should be:

```text id="excerpt_generation_rules"
short enough for review
long enough to support the claim
include exact changed language
include surrounding context
avoid full page dump
avoid unsupported interpretation
```

Recommended length:

```text id="excerpt_length"
50–250 words
```

---

# 26. Source Health Tracking

## 26.1 Purpose

Source health tells Sherry whether coverage is reliable.

---

## 26.2 Health Statuses

```text id="source_health_statuses"
healthy
degraded
failed
blocked_by_policy
needs_review
manual_only
unknown
```

---

## 26.3 Health Update Rules

On success:

```text id="source_health_success_rules"
set health_status = healthy
set last_checked_at
set last_successful_check_at
clear transient failure state
create source_health_check success record
```

On failure:

```text id="source_health_failure_rules"
set health_status = degraded or failed
set last_checked_at
set last_failure_at
set last_failure_reason
create source_health_check failure record
create crawl_error record
```

On policy block:

```text id="source_health_policy_block_rules"
set health_status = blocked_by_policy or manual_only
create source_health_check policy record
do not retry automatically
```

---

# 27. Failure Types

## 27.1 Crawl Failure Types

```text id="crawl_failure_types"
timeout
dns_failure
connection_refused
http_403
http_404
http_429
http_500
redirect_loop
ssl_error
content_too_large
unsupported_content_type
browser_crash
screenshot_failed
text_extraction_failed
robots_or_policy_disallowed
login_wall
paywall
captcha
blocked_by_source_policy
manual_only_source
non_compliant_source
unknown_error
```

---

## 27.2 Failure Severity

```text id="crawl_failure_severity"
low = one optional source failed
medium = priority_2 source failed
high = priority_1 source failed
critical = source policy guardrail failed open or all sources failed
```

---

# 28. Retry Strategy

## 28.1 Retryable Failures

Retry:

```text id="crawler_retryable_failures"
timeout
http_429
http_500
browser_crash
temporary DNS failure
temporary connection issue
screenshot failure
text extraction failure
```

---

## 28.2 Non-Retryable Failures

Do not retry:

```text id="crawler_non_retryable_failures"
blocked_by_source_policy
manual_only_source
login_wall
paywall
captcha
non_compliant_source
unsupported_collection_method
possible PHI
invalid URL
```

---

## 28.3 Retry Defaults

```json id="crawler_retry_defaults"
{
  "static_crawl": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 3000
  },
  "browser_crawl": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 5000
  },
  "rss_feed": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 3000
  },
  "news_search": {
    "max_attempts": 2,
    "backoff_ms": 5000
  },
  "screenshot": {
    "max_attempts": 1,
    "fallback": "text_only_evidence"
  }
}
```

---

# 29. Domain and Concurrency Controls

## 29.1 Concurrency Defaults

```json id="crawler_concurrency_defaults"
{
  "max_global_concurrent_sources": 10,
  "max_concurrent_per_domain": 2,
  "delay_between_domain_requests_ms": 2500,
  "static_timeout_ms": 30000,
  "browser_timeout_ms": 45000
}
```

---

## 29.2 Domain Grouping

Group collection by:

```text id="domain_grouping"
competitor domain
source hostname
collection method
priority
```

---

## 29.3 Overload Protection

The crawler should:

```text id="crawler_overload_protection"
limit parallel requests per domain
back off on 429
stop aggressive retry on 403/blocked
avoid infinite crawling
respect configured URL limits
surface repeated failures
```

---

# 30. URL Discovery and Scope Control

## 30.1 Approved URL Scope

The crawler should stay within approved scope.

Allowed:

```text id="approved_url_scope"
approved source URL
same-domain canonical URL
approved sitemap URLs
approved child URLs matching source pattern
approved newsroom / blog / docs / case study URLs
```

Not allowed:

```text id="disallowed_url_scope"
external ad links
login pages
checkout pages
private portals
random social links
unapproved third-party pages
unbounded deep crawl
```

---

## 30.2 Auto-Discovered URL Handling

Auto-discovered URLs should be classified as:

```text id="auto_discovered_url_status"
approved_pattern
needs_review
blocked
duplicate
irrelevant
```

Unknown URLs go to:

```text id="auto_discovered_queue"
Source Discovery Queue
```

---

# 31. Canonicalization and Deduplication

## 31.1 Canonical URL Rules

Normalize:

```text id="canonical_url_normalization"
remove tracking parameters
remove trailing slash variants
lowercase host
resolve redirects
use rel=canonical if present
normalize http/https if redirect confirms
```

Remove parameters:

```text id="tracking_params_remove"
utm_source
utm_medium
utm_campaign
utm_content
utm_term
gclid
fbclid
mc_cid
mc_eid
```

---

## 31.2 Duplicate Content Rules

Detect duplicates by:

```text id="duplicate_content_rules"
canonical URL
content hash
main content hash
title + published date
press release headline
RSS GUID
news cluster similarity
job title + location + description hash
```

---

# 32. Screenshot Capture

## 32.1 When Screenshot Is Required

Capture screenshot for:

```text id="screenshot_required_sources"
homepage
product_page
solution_page
pricing_page
case_study
partner_page
integration_page
comparison_page
Severity 4/5 finding evidence
```

---

## 32.2 When Screenshot Is Optional

Optional for:

```text id="screenshot_optional_sources"
blog
news article
press release
docs page
release note
job posting
event page
```

---

## 32.3 Screenshot Failure Behavior

If screenshot fails but text extraction succeeds:

```text id="screenshot_failure_behavior"
create evidence with screenshot_status = failed_capture
add warning
allow agent analysis if text evidence is strong
lower evidence quality slightly
```

---

# 33. PDF and File Download Handling

## 33.1 Auto-Download Allowed

Auto-download public files only when:

```text id="file_download_allowed"
file is public
```

# Section X+26 — Source Registry Seed Pack, Competitor Monitoring List, and Day-1 Crawl Configuration

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the Day-1 source registry seed pack for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The purpose is to make the first autonomous run useful, controlled, safe, and measurable.

The system should not start with a vague competitor list.

It should start with a structured registry that tells the command center:

- Which competitors exist.
- Which competitors matter most.
- Which Doceree products they threaten.
- Which public sources should be monitored.
- Which sources are approved for automation.
- Which sources are manual-only.
- Which sources need URL verification.
- Which sources should run daily, weekly, or monthly.
- Which agent should analyze each signal type.
- Which sources should be included in Day-1 baseline crawling.
- Which sources should be excluded until Sherry validates them.

The core principle is:

> Day 1 should establish a trusted, controlled monitoring base — not an uncontrolled scrape of the web.

---

## 2. Source Registry Philosophy

The source registry is the operating contract between competitive intelligence strategy and automation.

Without a registry, agents will behave like generic researchers.

With a registry, agents behave like disciplined analysts who know:

```text
what to monitor
why it matters
how often to monitor it
which source types are reliable
which sources are risky
which sources are prohibited
which Doceree products are affected
which findings should route to Sherry
````

The source registry should be treated as a first-class product object.

It is not just seed data.

It powers:

```text id="seed_pack_powers"
crawler planning
daily scheduler
source health monitoring
agent routing
confidence scoring
product mapping
review queues
battlecard triggers
alerts
daily briefs
KPIs
source discovery backlog
```

---

# 3. Authoritative Seed Source

## 3.1 Primary Source

The authoritative seed source is:

```text id="authoritative_seed_source"
Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center — Competitor & Source Registry v1
```

The registry contains:

```text id="registry_contains"
competitors
tiers
websites
categories
regions
known products
Doceree product overlaps
reason for monitoring
positioning summaries
key claims
proof points
partnerships / integrations
information gaps
sources
MVP monitoring list
collection method policy
competitor signal watchlist
```

Codex should not invent missing competitors or URLs.

If a URL is not verified, the record should be seeded as:

```text id="needs_source_discovery_seed_status"
needs_source_discovery
```

or:

```text id="needs_validation_seed_status"
needs_validation
```

---

## 3.2 MVP Monitoring List

The registry defines a Day-1 MVP monitoring cohort.

Codex should seed this cohort exactly from the registry JSON.

Important rule:

```text id="mvp_monitoring_rule"
The MVP monitoring list is the first scheduler cohort. It should be loaded on Day 1. Everything outside that list is post-MVP unless Sherry manually promotes it.
```

The current registry includes a `mvp_monitoring_list` with ranked sources. Examples from the seed include OptimizeRx homepage, investor/news releases, blog, and careers; DeepIntent homepage and newsroom sources; PulsePoint homepage, press releases, and blog; IQVIA homepage/newsroom/careers; and additional sources through a 50-source MVP cohort.  The registry also shows later MVP cohort entries such as RedSail press/news sources, PatientPoint news, Vistar Media news, GoodRx investor press releases, and Demandbase newsroom. 

---

# 4. Day-1 Seed Objectives

Day 1 should achieve five outcomes.

```text id="day1_seed_objectives"
1. Load the canonical competitor registry.
2. Load the canonical source registry.
3. Load the 50-source MVP monitoring cohort.
4. Establish first baseline snapshots for approved automated sources.
5. Create source discovery and validation queues for everything not ready to crawl.
```

Day 1 should not attempt to:

```text id="day1_should_not"
crawl every possible competitor page
scrape LinkedIn
scrape gated reports
crawl login-required portals
invent missing URLs
create final findings from baseline snapshots
send CEO or Sales alerts
publish battlecard updates
```

---

## 5.1 Required Competitor Fields

```text id="required_competitor_seed_fields"
name
tier
category

research_priority

doceree_product_overlap
```

Website may be nullable only when the competitor is still in discovery.

If website is missing:

```text id="missing_website_behavior"
set source_status = needs_source_discovery
do not schedule crawling
show in Source Discovery Queue
```

---

## 5.2 Competitor Tier Definitions

### Tier 1 — Direct Competitors

Definition:

```text id="tier1_definition"
Direct competitors with strong product or category overlap with one or more Doceree products.
```

Day-1 behavior:

```text id="tier1_day1_behavior"
Monitor daily on Priority 1 sources.
Monitor weekly on Priority 2 sources.
Monitor monthly on Priority 3 sources.
Include in daily brief if meaningful movement occurs.
Route Severity 4/5 signals to Sherry review.
```

### Tier 2 — Adjacent Competitors

Definition:

```text id="tier2_definition"
Adjacent competitors with credible overlap in healthcare marketing, pharma media, HCP engagement, patient access, AI, orchestration, data, or publisher monetization.
```

Day-1 behavior:

```text id="tier2_day1_behavior"
Monitor weekly on Priority 1 and Priority 2 sources.
Monitor monthly on Priority 3 sources.
Promote temporarily if a Severity 4/5 signal appears.
```

### Tier 3 — Emerging / Indirect / Category-Shaping Competitors

Definition:

```text id="tier3_definition"
Emerging, indirect, generic, or category-shaping competitors that may become relevant but are not yet direct daily threats.
```

Day-1 behavior:

```text id="tier3_day1_behavior"
Monitor monthly by default.
Do not include in Day-1 daily crawler unless they are in the 50-source MVP cohort.
Promote only through trigger rules or Sherry action.
```

---

# 6. Product Overlap Seed Model

Product overlap tells agents which Doceree products are likely affected when a competitor moves.

Each overlap record should include:

```json id="product_overlap_seed_model"
{
  "competitor": "",
  "doceree_product": "",
  "overlap_level": "high | medium | low | none",
  "overlap_rationale": "",
  "confidence_label": "high | medium | low | needs_validation",
  "status": "confirmed | inferred | needs_validation",
  "watchlist_signal_types": []
}
```

---

## 6.1 Product Mapping Rule

When a finding is created, the system should retrieve:

```text id="product_overlap_runtime_retrieval"
competitor profile
competitor product overlap matrix
Doceree Product Spine
product keywords
negative keywords
signal rules
```

Then the system should map the finding to:

```text id="product_mapping_runtime_rules"
all High-overlap products when supported by evidence
Medium-overlap products when signal context supports it
Low-overlap products only when there is direct evidence or pattern support
```

The registry guidance says agents should retrieve the competitor’s `doceree_product_overlap` block and map findings to products with high or medium overlap when signals support it, while preserving the original signal as source-of-truth attachment.

# 8. Source Priority Rules

## 8.1 Priority 1

Priority 1 sources are the most important sources for daily competitive intelligence.

Examples:

```text id="priority1_examples"
homepage
product page
solution page
pricing page
official newsroom
official press release page
official release notes
official docs for product capability
high-value case study page
major partner / integration page
```

Default cadence:

```text id="priority1_cadence"
daily for Tier 1
weekly for Tier 2
monthly for Tier 3 unless promoted
```

---

## 8.2 Priority 2

Priority 2 sources are useful but less urgent.

Examples:

```text id="priority2_examples"
blog
careers page
resource center
webinars
events
secondary newsroom
secondary product pages
```

Default cadence:

```text id="priority2_cadence"
weekly for Tier 1 and Tier 2
monthly for Tier 3
```

---

## 8.3 Priority 3

Priority 3 sources are supporting context.

Examples:

```text id="priority3_examples"
older resource libraries
generic category pages
partner directories
non-core blogs
lower-relevance job categories
```

Default cadence:

```text id="priority3_cadence"
monthly
```

---

## 8.4 Priority 4

Priority 4 sources are archive-only or manual.

Examples:

```text id="priority4_examples"
manual-only reports
unverified URLs
low-confidence third-party pages
historical pages
sources waiting for Sherry validation
```

Default cadence:

```text id="priority4_cadence"
do not crawl automatically
surface in backlog
```

The PRD explicitly sets cadence by source priority: Priority 1 daily, Priority 2 weekly, Priority 3 monthly, and Priority 4 archive-only.

| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------: | --------------: | ------------------------------- |
| Homepage                   | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | Day-1 baseline source           |
| Product page               | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | High product signal             |
| Solution page              | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | Persona/use-case signal         |
| Pricing page               | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | High commercial signal          |
| Newsroom                   | rss_feed or website_crawler                  |         Yes |              No | Prefer RSS if available         |
| Press release              | rss_feed / website_crawler / news_search     |         Yes |              No | Official high-confidence source |
| Blog                       | rss_feed / website_crawler                   |         Yes |              No | Noisy; weekly by default        |
| Careers                    | website_crawler / ATS parser                 |         Yes |              No | Directional only                |
| Docs / Help Center         | sitemap_monitor / website_crawler            |         Yes |              No | Product truth signal            |
| Release Notes              | rss_feed / sitemap_monitor / website_crawler |         Yes |              No | Product change signal           |
| Case Study                 | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | Proof-point signal              |
| Partner Page               | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | Partnership/integration signal  |
| Integration Page           | browser_rendered_crawler                     |         Yes |              No | Technical depth signal          |
| Event / Webinar            | website_crawler                              | Conditional |           Maybe | Must avoid gated content        |
| LinkedIn Company Page      | approved_api / vendor_data / manual_export   |  No crawler |             Yes | No browser scraping             |
| Executive LinkedIn Profile | approved_api / vendor_data / manual_export   |  No crawler |             Yes | No browser scraping             |
| Analyst Report             | manual_upload                                |  No crawler |             Yes | Access basis required           |
| Gated Webinar              | manual_upload                                |  No crawler |             Yes | Access basis required           |
| Paid Ad Library            | manual_upload / approved_api                 | Conditional |             Yes | Post-MVP                        |
| Review Site                | website_crawler / manual                     | Conditional |             Yes | Low confidence                  |
| Patent / Trademark         | approved public database                     | Conditional |             Yes | Post-MVP                        |

---

## 9.3 Hard Validation Rules

Codex must implement registry validation before saving a source.

Reject:

```text id="source_registry_hard_rejects"
LinkedIn company page + website crawler
Executive LinkedIn profile + website crawler
Analyst report + automation_allowed = true
Gated webinar + automation_allowed = true
Paid/gated source with unknown access basis
Manual-only source with automation_allowed = true
Blocked source with day1_enabled = true
Source marked needs_review with day1_enabled = true
```

The PRD explicitly requires validation to prevent unsupported source types and unauthorized scraping, including rejecting LinkedIn company or executive profile sources when the user attempts website crawling, and treating analyst reports or gated webinars as manual-upload only. 

---

# 10. Source Confidence Seed Rules

Source confidence should be seeded by source type.

## 10.1 High Confidence Sources

```text id="high_confidence_sources"
official competitor product page
official homepage
official press release
official newsroom
official docs
official release notes
official case study
official investor relations release
```

Language:

```text id="high_confidence_language"
Competitor claims...
Competitor announced...
Documentation indicates...
The official page states...
```

---

## 10.2 Medium Confidence Sources

```text id="medium_confidence_sources"
news article
job posting
executive social post from approved source
event page
webinar page
SEO category page
conference speaker abstract
```

Language:

```text id="medium_confidence_language"
This suggests...
This may indicate...
A third-party source reports...
A job posting suggests investment in...
```

---

## 10.3 Low Confidence Sources

```text id="low_confidence_sources"
third-party mention
review site
partial source
unverified URL
unclear source ownership
non-official repost
```

Language:

```text id="low_confidence_language"
This should be validated...
This is a weak signal...
Do not use externally until corroborated...
```

The Product Spine / PRD guidance requires confidence to be separate from severity and says source type should influence how the agent phrases a finding; for example, official product pages and press releases support stronger language, while job postings and third-party mentions require caveats.

# 13. Day-1 Baseline Crawl Configuration

## 13.1 Purpose

Day-1 crawl establishes source baselines.

It should create:

```text id="day1_baseline_creates"
source snapshots
raw HTML artifacts
clean text artifacts
screenshots where required
content hashes
source health records
baseline status
```

It should not create:

```text id="day1_baseline_does_not_create"
website change findings
alerts
battlecard tasks
CEO alert candidates
Sales alert candidates
daily brief claims based only on baseline
```

---

## 13.2 Day-1 Baseline Rules

For each Day-1 enabled source:

```text id="day1_baseline_rules"
1. Run SourcePolicyResolver.
2. If allowed, collect source.
3. Store raw artifacts.
4. Extract clean text.
5. Capture screenshot if required.
6. Create SourceSnapshot.
7. Mark snapshot as baseline.
8. Update source health.
9. Do not create change evidence.
10. Do not queue agents unless baseline analysis is manually requested.
```

---

## 13.3 Baseline Summary Option

For Priority 1 sources, Codex may optionally create baseline context records.

```text id="baseline_context_option"
evidence_type = website_snapshot
purpose = baseline_reference
agent_queue = disabled by default
```

Use this only for:

```text id="baseline_context_allowed_sources"
homepage
product page
press release index
official newsroom
official docs / release notes
official case study index
```

---

# 14. Day-2 Change Detection Configuration

Day 2 is when meaningful change detection begins.

For each Day-1 source:

```text id="day2_change_detection_flow"
1. Crawl source again.
2. Create new snapshot.
3. Compare against Day-1 baseline.
4. Suppress boilerplate changes.
5. Classify business-relevant change.
6. Create evidence if meaningful.
7. Queue evidence for agents.
8. Let Orchestrator decide final finding route.
```

---

# 19. Seed Loader Rules

## 19.1 Upsert Behavior

Seed scripts should be idempotent.

Use stable keys:

```text id="source_seed_stable_keys"
competitors: slug or normalized name
competitor_sources: competitor_id + canonical_url
mvp_monitoring_list: rank + competitor + url
collection_method_policy: source_type
watchlist: competitor + signal family
source_discovery_backlog: competitor + suspected_source_type + source_description
```

---

## 19.2 Do Not Duplicate

Seed should not duplicate if rerun.

If record exists:

```text id="seed_upsert_existing_behavior"
update non-sensitive metadata
preserve human edits unless seed_force_update = true
preserve approval changes made by Sherry
preserve disabled/manual-only/blocked states
```

---

## 19.3 Preserve Sherry Overrides

If Sherry changes a source manually, future seed runs should not overwrite it.

Fields to preserve:

```text id="preserve_sherry_overrides"
approval_status
automation_allowed
collection_method
priority
frequency
notes
source_confidence
source_risk_level
is_active
disabled_at
```

unless:

```text id="force_seed_override"
SEED_FORCE_UPDATE=true
```

---

# 36. Day-1 Run Modes

The first system run should support three modes.

## 36.1 Validate Only

```text id="day1_validate_only_mode"
Validate competitor and source registry.
Do not crawl.
Do not create snapshots.
Return validation report.
```

## 36.2 Baseline Only

```text id="day1_baseline_only_mode"
Crawl approved Day-1 sources.
Create snapshots.
Mark them as baseline.
Do not create change findings.
Generate Source Baseline Report.
```

## 36.3 Baseline + Optional Product Summary

```text id="day1_baseline_summary_mode"
Crawl approved Day-1 sources.
Create baseline snapshots.
Optionally summarize official product pages for competitor profile context.
Do not create final findings.
Do not create alerts.
```

Recommended default:

```text id="recommended_day1_mode"
Baseline Only
```

---

# 37. Day-1 Safety Gates

Before Day-1 baseline crawl starts, the system should verify:

```text id="day1_safety_gates"
seed validation passed
no LinkedIn/social crawler sources enabled
no manual-only sources enabled
no blocked sources enabled
all Day-1 URLs are valid
all Day-1 collection methods are supported
storage folders exist
database is reachable
OpenAI API is not required for baseline crawl
email is not required for baseline crawl
Sherry/Admin triggered or scheduled baseline is allowed
```

If any gate fails:

```text id="day1_safety_gate_failure"
block baseline crawl
show blockers
write run warning
do not proceed silently
```

---

# 38. Day-1 Output Artifacts

```text id="day1_output_artifacts"
source_baseline_report
source_health_records
source_snapshots
raw_html_artifacts
clean_text_artifacts
screenshots where required
crawl_errors for failed sources
source_discovery_backlog
day1_readiness_score
```

It should not produce:

```text id="day1_forbidden_outputs"

urgent alerts
```

# Section X+27 — Deployment, Local Operations, Backups, and Production Migration Plan

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines how the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center should be run locally, operated day-to-day, backed up, monitored, recovered, and eventually migrated to production.

The system should not be treated as a disposable prototype.

Even if the MVP starts locally on Sherry’s machine, it is still a business-critical competitive intelligence system that will store:

- Product Spine data
- Competitor registry data
- Source registry data
- Source snapshots
- Evidence
- Agent outputs
- Findings
- Human review decisions
- Daily briefs
- PDFs
- Email delivery records
- Eval results
- KPI snapshots
- Audit logs

The core principle is:

> Start locally, but design like production from Day 1.

This means the local MVP should already have:

- Dockerized services
- Environment separation
- Backup routines
- Health checks
- Restore procedures
- Runbooks
- Logs
- Worker supervision
- Safe secret handling
- Migration path to cloud deployment

---

## 2. Deployment Philosophy

The command center should be built in three deployment stages.

```text
Stage 1: Local MVP
Stage 2: Private hosted staging
Stage 3: Production deployment
````

The product should not jump directly to production before local reliability is proven.

The recommended path is:

```text id="deployment_path"
1. Build locally.
2. Run Day-1 baseline locally.
3. Run at least 7 successful scheduled daily runs locally.
4. Validate source health and report delivery.
5. Run golden evals.
6. Prove restore from backup.
7. Move to private hosted staging.
8. Run parallel local + hosted validation.
9. Move to production.
```

---

# 3. Deployment Stages

## 3.1 Stage 1 — Local MVP

Purpose:

```text id="stage_1_purpose"
Allow Sherry to run the command center locally while Codex builds the product step by step.
```

Local MVP should support:

```text id="stage_1_supports"
local PostgreSQL
local Next.js app
local worker process
local file storage
local Playwright browser rendering
local PDF generation
SMTP email delivery
OpenAI API calls
manual Day-1 baseline run
scheduled daily run
local backup and restore
```

Stage 1 should not require:

```text id="stage_1_should_not_require"
Kubernetes
multi-region deployment
complex cloud networking
enterprise SSO
managed object storage
managed queue infrastructure
large-scale observability platform
```

---

## 3.2 Stage 2 — Private Hosted Staging

Purpose:

```text id="stage_2_purpose"
Validate the command center in a hosted environment before production.
```

Staging should support:

```text id="stage_2_supports"
managed Postgres or hosted Postgres
server deployment
worker deployment
private authentication
persistent storage
cloud backup
scheduled jobs
email sending
OpenAI API calls
production-like source crawling
PDF generation
```

Staging should be used for:

```text id="stage_2_use_cases"
deployment validation
backup validation
restore validation
scheduler validation
source policy validation
agent eval validation
PDF/email validation
performance testing
access testing
```

---

## 3.3 Stage 3 — Production Deployment

Purpose:

```text id="stage_3_purpose"
Run the command center as Doceree's operating competitive intelligence system.
```

Production should support:

```text id="stage_3_supports"
reliable scheduled daily runs
persistent database
persistent object storage
backup automation
restore procedure
worker health monitoring
email delivery monitoring
OpenAI usage monitoring
audit logs
access control
error alerting
staging-to-production promotion
```

Production should not be launched until:

```text id="stage_3_launch_conditions"
Day-1 source registry is stable
daily scheduler is reliable
source failures are visible
PDF/email delivery is stable
evidence/finding guardrails pass
golden evals pass
backup restore is proven
Sherry can operate review workflow
runbooks exist
```

---

# 4. Recommended Technical Stack by Stage

## 4.1 Local MVP Stack

```text id="local_mvp_stack"
Frontend / Backend: Next.js
Language: TypeScript
Database: PostgreSQL in Docker
ORM: Prisma
Worker runtime: Node.js worker process
Crawler: Playwright + fetch
PDF: Playwright HTML-to-PDF
Storage: local filesystem
Email: SMTP
AI: OpenAI APIs + Agents SDK
Scheduler: node-cron or worker scheduler
Auth: local credential auth or NextAuth-compatible local auth
```

---

## 4.2 Hosted Staging Stack

Recommended options:

```text id="hosted_staging_stack_options"
App hosting: Render, Railway, Fly.io, DigitalOcean App Platform, AWS, GCP, or Azure
Database: managed Postgres
Storage: managed disk or S3-compatible object storage
Worker: separate background service
Scheduler: platform cron or app worker scheduler
Email: SMTP, Postmark, SendGrid, AWS SES, or Google Workspace SMTP
```

Preferred simple staging path:

```text id="preferred_staging_path"
Render or Railway for app + worker + managed Postgres
S3-compatible storage for artifacts
SMTP provider for email
```

---

## 4.3 Production Stack

Recommended production options:

```text id="production_stack_options"
Option A: Render/Railway production deployment for fastest reliable MVP
Option B: AWS ECS/Fargate + RDS + S3 + EventBridge for enterprise-grade production
Option C: GCP Cloud Run + Cloud SQL + Cloud Storage + Cloud Scheduler
Option D: Azure Container Apps + Azure Database for PostgreSQL + Blob Storage
```

Recommended production choice:

```text id="recommended_production_choice"
Start with Render/Railway production if speed matters.
Move to AWS/GCP/Azure if Doceree IT requires enterprise cloud governance.
```

# 6. Docker Compose Specification

## 6.1 Required Local Compose Services

```yaml id="docker_compose_local_spec"
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: doceree_ci
      POSTGRES_USER: doceree_ci
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: doceree_ci_local_password
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  web:
    build: .
    command: npm run dev
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    env_file:
      - .env.local
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    volumes:
      - .:/app
      - ./storage:/app/storage
      - ./logs:/app/logs

  worker:
    build: .
    command: npm run worker:daily
    env_file:
      - .env.local
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    volumes:
      - .:/app
      - ./storage:/app/storage
      - ./logs:/app/logs

  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog
    ports:
      - "8025:8025"
      - "1025:1025"

volumes:
  postgres_data:
```

---

## 6.2 Local Docker Rules

Codex should ensure:

```text id="local_docker_rules"
Postgres data persists across restarts.
Storage folder is mounted.
Logs folder is mounted.
Web and worker share the same storage path.
Worker does not run inside Next.js request lifecycle.
Mailhog is optional.
Secrets are read from .env.local.
```

```text id="env_example"
# Scheduler
DAILY_RUN_TIME=06:00
DAILY_RUN_TIMEZONE=America/New_York
DAILY_REPORT_RECIPIENT=sherry.george@doceree.com
WEEKEND_RUNS_ENABLED=true

# Crawler
CRAWLER_USER_AGENT=DocereeCICommandCenter/1.0
CRAWLER_MAX_GLOBAL_CONCURRENCY=10
CRAWLER_MAX_DOMAIN_CONCURRENCY=2
CRAWLER_STATIC_TIMEOUT_MS=30000
CRAWLER_BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MS=45000
SCREENSHOT_ENABLED=true

# Email
SMTP_HOST=localhost
SMTP_PORT=1025
SMTP_USER=
SMTP_PASS=

EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=local

# Backups
BACKUP_ENABLED=true
```

# 10. Worker Operations

## 10.1 Worker Requirement

The daily scheduler must run in a worker process.

It should not rely on a browser tab, local page load, or a single HTTP request.

---

## 10.2 Worker Commands

```json id="worker_commands"
{
  "worker:daily": "tsx src/workers/daily-run-worker.ts",
  "worker:retention": "tsx src/workers/retention-worker.ts",
  "worker:eval": "tsx src/workers/eval-worker.ts",
  "worker:all": "concurrently \"npm run worker:daily\" \"npm run worker:retention\" \"npm run worker:eval\""
}
```

---

```text id="worker_health_checks"
last heartbeat timestamp is recent
next scheduled run exists
last run status is visible
retention worker is available
eval worker is available
```

# 13. Backup Strategy

## 13.1 What Must Be Backed Up

Back up:

```text id="backup_must_include"
Postgres database
Product Spine seed data
competitor registry seed data
source registry data
findings
evidence metadata
human review decisions
daily briefs
PDF exports metadata
agent runs
eval results
KPI snapshots
audit logs
configuration settings
storage artifacts that are still within retention window
```

---

## 13.2 What May Be Excluded From Long-Term Backup

Depending on retention policy, long-term backup may exclude:

```text id="backup_may_exclude"
expired raw HTML
expired screenshots
temporary Playwright files
temporary PDFs
debug logs older than retention window
test fixture outputs
node_modules
build artifacts
```

---

## 13.3 Local Backup Types

Use three backup types.

```text id="local_backup_types"
database_dump
storage_archive
config_manifest
```

### Database Dump

```text id="database_dump_description"
Postgres dump of all business data.
```

### Storage Archive

```text id="storage_archive_description"
Compressed archive of storage artifacts that have not expired.
```

### Config Manifest

```text id="config_manifest_description"
Non-secret environment and app configuration summary.
```

---

## 13.4 Backup Schedule

Local MVP defaults:

```text id="backup_schedule_defaults"
daily database backup after daily run
daily storage manifest after daily run
weekly full storage archive
backup retention: 14 days local
```

Production defaults:

```text id="production_backup_defaults"
daily managed Postgres backup
point-in-time recovery if supported
daily object storage lifecycle snapshot or versioning
30-day backup retention minimum
weekly restore drill in staging during early production
monthly restore drill after stabilization
```

---

# 17. Restore Strategy

## 17.1 Restore Principles

Restore must be tested before production.

The system should support:

```text id="restore_supports"
restore database
restore storage artifacts
restore config manifest
restore into local environment
restore into staging environment
validate restored data
```

---

## 17.2 Restore Safety Rules

```text id="restore_safety_rules"
Never restore over production without explicit confirmation.
Never restore without creating pre-restore backup.
Never restore if migration versions are incompatible without migration plan.
Never restore secrets from backup into UI.
Never overwrite current storage unless target directory is specified.
```

---

## 17.3 Restore Validation

After restore, verify:

```text id="restore_validation_checks"
database connects
migrations are valid
Sherry user exists
Product Spine data exists
competitors exist
sources exist
evidence records exist
findings exist
daily briefs exist
PDF records exist
storage files referenced by database exist
worker can start
health check passes
```

---

## 17.4 Restore Drill

Before production migration, perform:

```text id="pre_prod_restore_drill"
1. Create local full backup.
2. Create fresh local database.
3. Restore backup.
4. Restore storage.
5. Run health check.
6. Open dashboard.
7. Verify latest daily brief.
8. Verify evidence links.
9. Verify PDF availability.
10. Run one manual dry run.
```

---

# 18. Data Retention and Backup Interaction

## 18.1 Retention Rules

The system already defines:

```text id="retention_rules_for_deployment"
raw website snapshots: 7 days
screenshots: 7 days
social data: 7 days
business records: retained
evidence metadata: retained
audit logs: retained long-term
```

---

## 18.2 Backup Must Respect Retention

Backup should not preserve expired raw artifacts indefinitely.

Rules:

```text id="backup_retention_rules"
Do not include artifacts already marked expired.
Do not restore artifacts that retention policy says should be deleted unless restoring historical backup for audit.
Preserve evidence metadata even when raw artifacts are expired.
Preserve finding and daily brief records.
Preserve audit logs.
```

---

# 19. Storage Operations

## 19.1 Local Storage Health

Check:

```text id="storage_health_checks"
storage directory exists
storage directory is writable
html_snapshots folder exists
clean_text folder exists
screenshots folder exists
pdf_reports folder exists
backups folder exists
available disk space above threshold
```

---

## 19.2 Disk Space Thresholds

Local defaults:

```text id="disk_space_thresholds"
warning when free disk space < 10 GB
critical when free disk space < 3 GB
pause screenshot capture if critical
pause full crawl if critical
always notify Sherry when critical
```

---

## 19.3 Storage Cleanup

Cleanup should be handled by retention jobs.

Do not manually delete files unless:

```text id="manual_delete_allowed"
artifact contains sensitive data
artifact contains possible PHI
artifact was captured by mistake
Sherry/Admin explicitly deletes through UI
```

# 20. Production Migration Plan

## 20.1 Migration Readiness Checklist

The product is ready to migrate from local MVP to hosted staging when:

```text id="migration_readiness_checklist"
local app runs successfully
database migrations are stable
seed scripts are idempotent
Day-1 baseline run works
at least 7 daily runs completed
daily brief PDF generates reliably
email delivery works
source failures are visible
manual review workflow works
critical backend guardrails pass
golden evals pass
backup and restore tested
health checks pass
runbooks exist
```

---

## 20.2 Migration Phases

```text id="production_migration_phases"
Phase 1: Prepare hosted infrastructure
Phase 2: Export local database and storage
Phase 3: Import into staging
Phase 4: Run staging validation
Phase 5: Run parallel validation
Phase 6: Promote to production
Phase 7: Decommission local scheduler or keep local read-only
```

---

## 20.3 Phase 1 — Prepare Hosted Infrastructure

Tasks:

```text id="prepare_hosted_infrastructure_tasks"
create hosted app service
create hosted worker service
create managed Postgres database
create object storage bucket
configure environment variables
configure SMTP provider
configure OpenAI API key
configure domain / URL
configure private auth
configure backups
```

---

## 20.4 Phase 2 — Export Local Data

Run:

```bash id="export_local_data_commands"
npm run backup:all
npm run backup:verify
```

Confirm:

```text id="export_local_data_confirm"
database dump exists
storage archive exists
backup manifest exists
checksums pass
backup run record is stored
```

---

## 20.5 Phase 3 — Import Into Staging

Run in staging:

```bash id="import_staging_commands"
npm run restore:all -- --backupManifest=<manifest_path>
npm run db:migrate
npm run ops:health
```

Verify:

```text id="staging_import_verify"
dashboard loads
Sherry user exists
Product Spine loads
competitor registry loads
source registry loads
daily briefs load
PDF links work or gracefully show missing artifact
worker starts
scheduler is paused until validation completes
```

---

## 20.6 Phase 4 — Staging Validation

Staging validation should include:

```text id="staging_validation_checks"
manual dry run
source policy validation
crawler smoke test on 2–3 approved sources
agent smoke test on fixture evidence
PDF generation test
email test to Sherry or test inbox
golden eval run
backup creation
restore drill into second staging database
```

---

## 20.7 Phase 5 — Parallel Validation

Run local and staging in parallel for at least:

```text id="parallel_validation_duration"
3 daily runs
```

Compare:

```text id="parallel_validation_compare"
sources checked
source failures
evidence created
findings created
daily brief content
PDF generation
email delivery
agent errors
runtime cost
```

During parallel validation:

```text id="parallel_validation_rules"
Only one environment should send official daily email.
Staging should send to test recipient unless Sherry explicitly enables it.
Do not duplicate production alerts.
Do not publish battlecard tasks from staging.
```

---

## 20.8 Phase 6 — Production Cutover

Cutover steps:

```text id="production_cutover_steps"
1. Pause local scheduler.
2. Run final local backup.
3. Restore latest backup to production.
4. Run production health check.
5. Run production dry run.
6. Enable production scheduler.
7. Send first production daily brief to Sherry only.
8. Monitor first production run.
9. Keep local environment read-only for 7 days.
```

---

## 20.9 Phase 7 — Post-Cutover Monitoring

For the first 14 days:

```text id="post_cutover_monitoring"
check daily run status every morning
check source failure rate
check PDF/email delivery
check OpenAI usage
check crawler errors
check worker heartbeat
check backup completion
run golden evals twice weekly
run restore drill weekly
```

---

# 29. Disaster Recovery

## 29.1 Recovery Objectives

Local MVP targets:

```text id="local_recovery_objectives"
RPO: 24 hours
RTO: 4 hours
```

Production targets:

```text id="production_recovery_objectives"
RPO: 24 hours or better
RTO: 2 hours or better
```

Definitions:

```text id="rpo_rto_definitions"
RPO = maximum acceptable data loss window.
RTO = maximum acceptable time to restore service.
```

---

## 29.2 Disaster Scenarios

Prepare for:

```text id="disaster_scenarios"
local laptop failure
database corruption
storage artifact loss
bad migration
duplicate email send bug
scheduler stuck
worker crash loop
```

# Section X+28 — Security, Compliance, Access Control, and Data Governance Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the security, compliance, access control, source governance, evidence governance, data handling, audit logging, approval gates, secret management, and safe-use rules for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The command center will collect, store, analyze, summarize, and distribute competitive intelligence. Because it will operate autonomously, it must be governed from the beginning.

The system should not rely on agents, prompts, or frontend buttons alone to enforce safety.

The backend must enforce security and governance rules at the service layer.

The core principle is:

> Competitive intelligence is useful only if it is accurate, lawful, traceable, permissioned, and safe to distribute.

This section exists to make sure the command center does not become:

- an uncontrolled scraper
- an unsupported claims generator
- a private-data collector
- a source-policy bypass tool
- a report sender without approval gates
- an AI system that hides evidence, low confidence, or source failures
- an internal system that exposes secrets, raw prompts, or sensitive data

---

## 2. Governance Philosophy

The command center should operate under seven security and governance principles.

```text
1. Evidence-first intelligence
2. Permissioned access
3. Source-policy enforcement
4. Human approval for high-risk distribution
5. Data minimization
6. Traceability and auditability
7. Fail-closed behavior
````

---

## 2.1 Evidence-First Intelligence

Every competitor finding must be tied to evidence.

The system must enforce:

```text id="evidence_first_rules"
No evidence, no finding.
No source URL, no claim.
No captured timestamp, no claim.
No source type, no claim.
No excerpt, no claim.
No compliant source, no final finding.
No final finding without Orchestrator validation.
```

Agents may propose interpretations, but the system must distinguish:

```text id="evidence_interpretation_levels"
source text
agent interpretation
competitor claim
Doceree product truth
human-approved conclusion
```

---

## 2.2 Permissioned Access

All users should be authenticated.

All write actions should be permission-gated.

Reader users may view permitted intelligence, but they should not be able to:

```text id="reader_forbidden_security"
approve findings
send alerts
send reports
edit sources
edit competitors
edit products
edit prompts
trigger crawlers
trigger agents
change settings
change source policy
change retention policy
view secrets
```

---

## 2.3 Source-Policy Enforcement

The system must not collect from a source simply because a URL exists.

Every source must have:

```text id="source_policy_required_fields"
source type
collection method
approval status
automation allowed flag
access basis
source risk level
compliance status
requires login flag
```

The system must block collection when policy says collection is not allowed.

---

## 2.4 Human Approval for High-Risk Distribution

The system may generate alert candidates automatically.

The system must not automatically send high-risk findings to CEO, Sales, or broader audiences.

Sherry approval is required before:

```text id="approval_required_distribution"
CEO alert send
Sales alert send
Severity 4/5 broad distribution
battlecard publication
external forwarding
report recipient expansion
high-risk source exception approval
non-standard retention exception
```

Daily brief auto-send to Sherry remains allowed.

---

## 2.5 Data Minimization

The system should collect only what is needed for competitive intelligence.

It should prefer:

```text id="data_minimization_prefer"
source URL
captured timestamp
source type
short excerpt
before/after diff
screenshot when needed
metadata required for traceability
```

It should avoid unnecessary storage of:

```text id="data_minimization_avoid"
full raw HTML beyond retention window
unnecessary personal data
private profile data
contact harvesting
restricted login content
paywalled content without approved access basis
files unrelated to competitive intelligence
```

---

## 2.6 Traceability and Auditability

Every sensitive action must answer:

```text id="auditability_questions"
Who did it?
What did they do?
When did they do it?
Which object did it affect?
What changed?
Was it user, system, scheduler, or agent initiated?
What evidence supported it?
Was approval required?
Was approval granted?
```

---

## 2.7 Fail-Closed Behavior

When the system is uncertain, it should fail closed.

Examples:

```text id="fail_closed_examples"
Unknown source policy -> do not crawl.
Unknown access basis -> do not use for final finding.
Possible PHI -> block from agent queue.
Missing evidence excerpt -> do not create final finding.
Invalid agent output -> do not save finding.
Approval missing -> do not send alert.
Source compliance guardrail failure -> stop finalization.
```

---

# 3. Security Scope

This section governs:

```text id="security_scope"
users
roles
permissions
authentication
authorization
source collection
manual uploads
evidence storage
agent tool access
report generation
PDF exports
email delivery
alerts
battlecards
audit logs
retention
backups
settings
secrets
safe mode

```

| Executive Reader        | Can view reports, findings, and high-level dashboards.                           |

Even though MVP begins with Sherry as primary user, the system should be ready for controlled multi-user access.

The role system should be permission-based, not hardcoded by role name only.

Role labels help the UI.

Permission flags control actual access.
