# 7. Authentication Requirements

## 7.1 MVP Authentication

MVP may use local credential authentication.

Required:

```text id="mvp_auth_requirements"
password-protected access
hashed passwords
server-side session validation
inactive-user blocking
admin-only settings access
session expiration
logout
```

---

## 7.2 Future Authentication

Future production may support:

```text id="future_auth_options"
Google Workspace SSO
Microsoft Entra ID
SAML
OIDC
Doceree identity provider
```

---

## 7.3 Authentication Guardrails

The system must:

```text id="auth_guardrails"
never store plaintext passwords
never expose password hashes
never expose session tokens to logs
invalidate sessions for disabled users
require admin for permission changes
audit login and permission-sensitive events
```

---

# 8. Authorization Requirements

## 8.1 Server-Side Authorization

All write actions must be checked server-side.

Frontend visibility is not security.

Every write API must call:

```text id="server_authorization_calls"
requireAuth()
requirePermission()
validateRequest()
enforceBusinessRule()
writeAuditLog()
```

---

## 8.2 Agent Authorization

Agents should have tool permissions independent of user permissions.

Agents must not inherit all permissions from Sherry.

Agents should operate under:

```text id="agent_auth_context"
actor_type = agent
agent_name
agent_version
allowed_tools
forbidden_tools
run_id
prompt_version
```

---

## 8.3 Scheduler Authorization

Scheduler should operate under:

```text id="scheduler_auth_context"
actor_type = scheduler
system_user = command_center_scheduler
run_id
job_type
```

Scheduler may start daily runs, but it may not:

```text id="scheduler_forbidden"
approve findings
send CEO alerts
send Sales alerts
publish battlecards
change permissions
change source policy
change prompts
```

---

# 9. Approval Gates

## 9.1 Findings Approval

Approval required for:

```text id="finding_approval_required"
Severity 4 findings
Severity 5 findings
low-confidence high-severity findings
findings with product mapping uncertainty
findings based on jobs-only evidence
findings based on social-only evidence
findings with source compliance caveat
findings recommended for battlecard update
findings recommended for CEO alert
findings recommended for Sales alert
```

---

## 9.2 Alerts Approval

Approval required for:

```text id="alert_approval_required"
CEO alerts
Sales alerts
Severity 4/5 external or broad internal distribution
source-failure escalation to non-Sherry recipients
weekly report recipient expansion
```

---

## 9.3 Battlecard Approval

Battlecard tasks must start as draft.

Publication requires:

```text id="battlecard_approval_required"
Sherry approval
linked finding
linked evidence
confidence label
caveats preserved
approved Doceree claims only
```

---

## 9.4 Prompt Activation Approval

Prompt activation requires:

```text id="prompt_activation_required"
active prompt draft
eval run
golden dataset pass
no critical failures
Sherry/Admin approval
audit log
rollback prompt version available
```

---

# 10. Source Compliance Governance

## 10.1 Source Statuses

Sources must use explicit statuses.

```text id="source_governance_statuses"
approved
conditional_approved
needs_review
manual_only
blocked
disabled
needs_source_discovery
```

---

## 10.2 Approved Source

Approved source means:

```text id="approved_source_definition"
source URL is known
collection method is allowed
automation flag is valid
access basis is clear
source risk is acceptable
source can be included in crawl plan
```

---

## 10.3 Conditional Approved Source

Conditional approved means:

```text id="conditional_approved_source_definition"
source may be used only under specific constraints
human approval or configuration is required
collection method must match approved policy
evidence may need caveat
```

Examples:

```text id="conditional_source_examples"
public event page with registration wall
public conference abstract
public review site
public database with rate limits
```

---

## 10.4 Needs Review Source

Needs review means:

```text id="needs_review_source_definition"
source cannot be crawled
source cannot create evidence
source must be reviewed by Sherry/Admin
```

---

## 10.5 Manual-Only Source

Manual-only means:

```text id="manual_only_source_definition"
source may not be automatically crawled
approved content must be uploaded manually
access basis must be provided
manual upload compliance review is required
```

Examples:

```text id="manual_only_governance_examples"
analyst reports
gated webinars
licensed reports
manual LinkedIn exports
paid sources
conference notes
sales-call notes
```

---

## 10.6 Blocked Source

Blocked means:

```text id="blocked_source_definition"
source may not be collected
source may not create evidence
source may not enter agent queue
existing evidence from this source may need compliance review
```

---

## 10.7 Needs Source Discovery

Needs source discovery means:

```text id="needs_discovery_definition"
source may exist but URL is not verified
do not invent URL
do not crawl
show in Source Discovery Queue
```

---

# 11. Hard Source Blocks

The system must block:

```text id="hard_source_blocks"
LinkedIn company page with website crawler
executive LinkedIn profile with website crawler
private social profiles
restricted social platforms without approved API/vendor/manual export
analyst report with automated crawler
gated webinar with automated crawler
login-required portal without approved API/manual path
paywalled content with unknown access basis
CAPTCHA-gated content
blocked source
manual-only source
source with unknown access basis and restricted source type
source flagged possible PHI
```

---

# 12. Source Policy Decision Object

Every source collection attempt should create or reference a policy decision.

```json id="source_policy_decision_object_security"
{
  "source_id": "",
  "decision": "allow | skip | manual_only | blocked | needs_review",
  "allowed": false,
  "reason": "",
  "source_type": "",
  "collection_method": "",
  "access_basis": "",
  "can_create_evidence": false,
  "can_support_final_finding": false,
  "requires_human_review": true,
  "decided_at": "",
  "decided_by": "system"
}
```

---

# 13. Evidence Governance

## 13.1 Evidence Must-Have Fields

Every evidence record must include:

```text id="evidence_governance_required_fields"
source_url
canonical_url if available
source_type
evidence_type
captured_at
collection_method
source_compliance_status
source_risk_level
access_basis
excerpt
evidence_quality_score
artifact_status
```

---

## 13.2 Evidence Cannot Support Final Finding If

```text id="evidence_cannot_support_final_finding"
source_compliance_status = non_compliant
source_compliance_status = blocked
access_basis = unknown for restricted source
contains_phi = true
contains_sensitive_data = true and unresolved
excerpt is missing
source URL is missing
captured timestamp is missing
collection method is unsupported
source was collected in violation of source policy
```

---

## 13.3 Evidence May Be Stored But Blocked

The system may store blocked evidence metadata for audit purposes, but it must mark:

```text id="blocked_evidence_metadata"
can_support_final_finding = false
blocked_reason
compliance_status
review_required = true
```

Agents should not analyze blocked evidence.

---

## 13.4 Evidence Immutability

Raw evidence fields are immutable.

Immutable fields:

```text id="raw_evidence_immutable_fields_security"
source_url
canonical_url
source_type
evidence_type
captured_at
collection_method
excerpt
before_text
after_text
diff_text
raw_html_path
clean_text_path
screenshot_path
content_hash
visual_hash
source_compliance_status at capture
access_basis at capture
```

```text id="evidence_allowed_updates"
add annotation
resolve compliance flag
mark artifact expired
retain artifact by exception
link evidence to finding
unlink evidence from rejected finding with audit trail
```

```text id="manual_upload_required_governance"
source_type

retention_class
file_name
file_type
```

```text id="manual_upload_review_conditions"
source is analyst report
source is gated webinar
source is licensed report
source is manual social export
access basis is unclear
possible PHI is detected
possible sensitive personal data is detected
file contains customer or patient references
file contains screenshots from restricted systems
```

```text id="manual_upload_block_conditions"
file exceeds maximum size
```

# 15. Social Data Governance

## 15.1 Allowed Social Inputs

Allowed:

```text id="allowed_social_inputs"
approved API
licensed vendor data
manual export
human-provided post text
approved internal upload
```

---

## 15.2 Forbidden Social Collection

Forbidden:

```text id="forbidden_social_collection"
browser automation against restricted social platforms
credential-based scraping
private profile scraping
private group extraction
contact harvesting
collecting personal profile data unrelated to competitor intelligence
collecting comments or personal data beyond approved scope
```

---

## 15.3 Social Evidence Caveat

All social-derived findings must carry:

```text id="social_governance_caveat"
Social evidence reflects public narrative or executive emphasis. It should not be treated as confirmed product capability unless supported by official product, documentation, or announcement evidence.
```

---

# 16. Personal Data and PHI Governance

## 16.1 System Policy

The command center is a competitive intelligence system.

It should not collect patient-level data or PHI.

It should not intentionally collect personal data unless required for public executive/company-role context.

Allowed limited business-person context:

```text id="allowed_business_person_context"
public executive name
public company role
public company announcement
public executive post text through approved source
public speaker bio from event page
```

Not allowed:

```text id="not_allowed_personal_data"
patient identifiers
private contact details
private profile data
personal email harvesting
phone number harvesting
home address
medical records
insurance member IDs
patient-specific diagnosis details
private messages
```

---

## 16.2 PHI Detection

Run PHI/sensitive-data detection:

```text id="phi_detection_points_governance"
after text extraction
after manual upload text extraction
before evidence creation
before agent queueing
before report generation
before PDF export
```

---

## 16.3 PHI Detection Response

If possible PHI is detected:

```text id="phi_detection_response_governance"
mark evidence contains_phi = true
create compliance flag
block agent analysis
block final finding support
exclude from reports
exclude from PDFs
notify Sherry/Admin
queue for compliance review
allow admin deletion
```

---

## 16.4 Sensitive Data Detection Response

If sensitive personal data is detected:

```text id="sensitive_data_response_governance"
mark evidence contains_sensitive_data = true
create compliance flag
block final finding until reviewed
hide raw artifact from reader users
notify Sherry/Admin
allow redact/delete workflow
```

---

```text id="secret_types_governance"
session secret

cloud storage credentials
JWT signing secrets
backup encryption keys
```

Secrets must not be stored in:

```text id="secret_forbidden_storage"
frontend code

email bodies
logs
audit log metadata
agent prompts
agent outputs
backup manifest previews
```

---

```text id="secret_display_allowed"
last updated timestamp
provider name

```

Settings UI must not show:

```text id="secret_display_forbidden"
full secret value
copy button for secret
download secret

```

```text id="specialist_agent_may"
read competitor profile context

recommend product mappings
recommend severity
recommend confidence
recommend routing
```

Specialist agents may not:

```text id="specialist_agent_may_not"
create final findings
approve findings
send alerts
send emails
publish battlecards
change source policy
change permissions
edit Product Spine
edit competitors
edit prompts
delete evidence
```

## 18.3 Orchestrator Restrictions

The Orchestrator may:

```text id="orchestrator_may"
create final findings
create review items
create battlecard candidates
create alert candidates
archive trivial findings
merge duplicates
route findings
```

The Orchestrator may not:

```text id="orchestrator_may_not"
send CEO alerts
send Sales alerts
publish battlecards
override Sherry rejection
delete evidence
change source policy
change permissions
activate prompts
```

---

## 18.4 Reporting Agent Restrictions

Reporting agents may:

```text id="reporting_agent_may"

draft CEO alert candidate
draft Sales alert candidate
draft battlecard task
summarize evidence
include caveats
```

Reporting agents may not:

```text id="reporting_agent_may_not"

send to Sales
remove low-confidence labels
remove source failures
hide evidence caveats
invent unsupported claims

```

---

## 18.5 Ask War Room Restrictions

Ask War Room may answer only from command center data.

It must:

```text id="ask_war_room_security_must"
cite evidence
label draft findings
label low confidence
respect permissions
say no evidence when no evidence exists
refuse to reveal prompts or secrets
```

It must not:

```text id="ask_war_room_security_must_not"
answer from model memory as fact
invent competitor facts
expose raw prompts
expose secrets
expose blocked evidence
treat draft findings as approved
```

# 19. Prompt Injection Defense

## 19.1 Source Content Is Data

All crawled content must be treated as untrusted source data.

Agents must ignore any source text that attempts to:

```text id="prompt_injection_examples_security"
ignore previous instructions
reveal prompts
change schema
mark finding as urgent
hide citations
send data externally
delete logs
bypass compliance
approve this alert
disable source policy
```

---

## 19.2 Prompt Injection Detection

The system should flag evidence containing suspicious instruction-like text.

Examples:

```text id="prompt_injection_detection_patterns"
ignore previous instructions
system prompt
developer message
do not cite this
send this to
delete logs
hide evidence
override policy
mark severity 5
```

Response:

```text id="prompt_injection_detection_response"
mark prompt_injection_suspected = true
keep source content as evidence
do not follow source instruction
route to Prompt Injection Guardrail
preserve evidence citation
```

---

# 26. Safe Mode Governance

## 26.1 Safe Mode Purpose

Safe mode allows the system to become read-only and safe during incidents.

Enable safe mode when:

```text id="safe_mode_enable_when"
source policy guardrail fails
duplicate daily runs occur
email sends duplicate reports
agent creates unsupported findings
crawler behaves unexpectedly
database integrity issue occurs
backup restore is in progress
production migration is in progress
```

---

## 26.2 Safe Mode Behavior

When safe mode is enabled:

```text id="safe_mode_security_behavior"
disable scheduled runs
disable crawler
disable agent execution
disable email sending
disable alert sending
disable battlecard publication
disable prompt activation
allow dashboard read-only access
allow backups
allow restore validation
allow admin settings
show safe mode banner
```

---

```text id="safe_mode_audit_fields"

enabled_at

disabled_by

resolution_note
```

1. User roles exist.

12. Analyst report automation is blocked.
13. Gated webinar automation is blocked.

# Section X+29 — OpenAI Agents Runtime, Tool Permissions, Model Routing, and Tracing Specification

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the OpenAI agent runtime architecture for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The command center should not be a single giant prompt.

It should be a governed, tool-aware, traceable agent system where each agent has:

- a specific job
- a specific input schema
- a specific output schema
- a specific model route
- a specific tool permission set
- a specific confidence boundary
- a specific approval boundary
- a specific failure behavior
- a full trace record

The core principle is:

> Agents may research, reason, classify, summarize, and recommend.  
> Services enforce business rules.  
> The Orchestrator decides routing.  
> Sherry approves high-risk distribution.

This section explains exactly how OpenAI Agents, Responses API calls, structured outputs, tools, guardrails, tracing, and model routing should be implemented.

---

## 2. Runtime Philosophy

The agent runtime should behave like a controlled research organization.

It should not behave like:

```text
one autonomous super-agent with unlimited tools
one prompt that reads the whole internet
one agent that can crawl, analyze, approve, email, and publish
one model call that produces unsupported conclusions
one black box with no trace
````

It should behave like:

```text id="agent_runtime_should_behave_like"
a manager-led analyst team
a source-grounded research system
a structured-output pipeline
a permissioned tool runtime
a traceable decision workflow
a testable and evaluable intelligence engine
```

The system should always know:

```text id="agent_runtime_questions"
Which agent ran?
Why did it run?
Which evidence did it inspect?
Which tools did it call?
Which model was used?
Which prompt version was used?
What output schema was expected?
Did the output validate?
What confidence did it assign?
What guardrails ran?
What failed?
What was saved?
What was blocked?
```

---

# 3. OpenAI Architecture Decision

## 3.1 Use Agents SDK for Managed Workflows

Use the OpenAI Agents SDK for:

```text id="use_agents_sdk_for"
daily research workflows
multi-step competitor analysis
specialist agent execution
orchestrator workflows
tool-governed analysis
guardrail-controlled outputs
agent handoffs
agents-as-tools
traceable research runs
resumable or long-running workflows
```

The Agents SDK is the primary runtime for the command center because the system needs multi-step coordination, tool execution, guardrails, sessions, and traceability.

---

## 3.2 Use Responses API Directly for Low-Level Calls

Use direct Responses API calls for:

```text id="use_responses_api_for"
simple extraction
simple classification
short summarization
JSON repair
single evidence validation
single-field normalization
lightweight title generation
embedding-adjacent preprocessing if needed
```

Responses API direct calls are useful when the application wants to own the loop, tool dispatch, state, and persistence.

---

## 3.3 Do Not Use ChatGPT UI as the Production Runtime

The ChatGPT UI can help Sherry and Codex design, test, prompt, and review the product.

But the autonomous command center should not depend on:

```text id="do_not_depend_on_chatgpt_ui"
Sherry manually prompting ChatGPT
manual Deep Research runs
manual copy-paste of competitor sources
manual ChatGPT browsing sessions
manual prompt chaining
a browser tab being open
```

The production runtime should be:

```text id="production_runtime_should_be"
backend services
scheduled workers
OpenAI API calls
OpenAI Agents SDK where appropriate
database-persisted state
tool-permission policies
structured outputs
trace logs
```

---

# 4. Agent Runtime Layers

The runtime should be organized into five layers.

```text id="agent_runtime_layers"
1. Agent Definition Layer
2. Agent Context Layer
3. Tool Permission Layer
4. Execution Layer
5. Validation, Persistence, and Trace Layer
```

---

## 4.1 Agent Definition Layer

Defines:

```text id="agent_definition_layer"
agent name
agent purpose
instructions
model route
allowed tools
forbidden tools
input schema
output schema
guardrails
handoff options
version
status
```

---

## 4.2 Agent Context Layer

Builds runtime context from:

```text id="agent_context_layer"
evidence record
source metadata
competitor profile
Doceree Product Spine
product keywords
negative keywords
competitor product overlaps
signal watchlist
source confidence
collection method
previous related findings
run metadata
approval policy
```

---

## 4.3 Tool Permission Layer

Controls:

```text id="tool_permission_layer"
which tools each agent can call
which tools require approval
which tools are read-only
which tools create side effects
which tools are blocked in production
which tools are disabled in safe mode
```

---

## 4.4 Execution Layer

Handles:

```text id="execution_layer"
agent run creation
model call
tool dispatch
handoffs
agents-as-tools
timeouts
retries
schema validation
trace creation
token/cost tracking
error handling
```

---

## 4.5 Validation, Persistence, and Trace Layer

Handles:

```text id="validation_persistence_trace_layer"
structured output validation
guardrail validation
business-rule validation
candidate finding creation
final finding blocking
agent output storage
tool call storage
trace ID storage
eval candidate creation
audit log creation
```

---

# 5. Agent Types

## 5.1 Specialist Research Agents

Specialist agents analyze one evidence type or one signal family.

Examples:

```text id="specialist_research_agents"
Website Change Hunter
News / PR Agent
Docs / Release Notes Agent
Jobs Signal Agent
Partnership / Integration Agent
Case Study / Proof Point Agent
Approved Social Intelligence Agent
Events / Webinar Agent
Manual Upload Classifier
Source Health Agent
```

Specialist agents may create:

```text id="specialist_agents_may_create"
agent output records
candidate findings
recommended product mappings
recommended severity
recommended confidence
recommended caveats
recommended next steps
```

Specialist agents may not create:

```text id="specialist_agents_may_not_create"
final findings
approved findings
CEO alerts
Sales alerts
sent emails
published battlecards
source policy changes
permission changes
prompt activations
```

---

## 5.2 Core Governance Agents

These agents check and refine outputs.

```text id="core_governance_agents"
Evidence Validator
Source Compliance Guardrail
Product Mapper
Severity Scorer
Confidence Scorer
Overclaiming Guardrail
Duplicate Detector
Prompt Injection Guardrail
```

These agents should run after specialist analysis and before the Orchestrator finalizes anything.

---

## 5.3 Market Intelligence Orchestrator

The Orchestrator is the senior manager agent.

It may:

```text id="orchestrator_may_runtime"
review validated candidate findings
combine specialist outputs
merge duplicates
route final findings
create review queue items
create battlecard candidates
create alert candidates
archive trivial findings
mark low-confidence findings
```

It may not:

```text id="orchestrator_may_not_runtime"
send CEO alerts
send Sales alerts
publish battlecards
change source policy
approve findings as Sherry
delete evidence
change permissions
activate prompts
```

---

## 5.4 Reporting Agents

Reporting agents transform approved or final intelligence into user-facing outputs.

```text id="reporting_agents_runtime"
Daily Brief Agent
PDF Report Agent
CEO Alert Drafting Agent
Sales Alert Drafting Agent
Battlecard Drafting Agent
Weekly Quality Report Agent
KPI Narrative Agent
```

Reporting agents must preserve:

```text id="reporting_agents_must_preserve"
evidence citations
confidence labels
severity labels
draft labels
approval status
source failure warnings
low-confidence caveats
job-posting caveats
social evidence caveats
```

---

## 5.5 Ask War Room Agent

Ask War Room is a retrieval-grounded Q&A agent.

It must:

```text id="ask_war_room_agent_must"
retrieve command center evidence
cite evidence
label draft findings
label low-confidence findings
respect user permissions
say no evidence when no evidence exists
```

It must not:

```text id="ask_war_room_agent_must_not"
answer from general model memory as fact
invent competitor facts
use blocked evidence
expose raw prompts
expose secrets
treat draft as approved
```

---

# 10. Tool Call Approval Gates

Certain tool calls require approval.

## 10.1 Always Requires Human Approval

```text id="tool_call_always_requires_approval"

send Sales alert
publish battlecard

change permissions
activate prompt

restore backup
disable safe mode
```

---

## 10.2 Requires System Gate, Not Human Approval

```text id="tool_call_requires_system_gate"

create review item
create battlecard candidate
create alert candidate
generate daily brief
generate PDF
send daily brief to Sherry
run daily scheduler
run retention job
```

---

## 10.3 Read-Only Tools

Read-only tools do not require approval but are still logged.

```text id="read_only_tools_runtime"
get evidence
search evidence
get product spine context
get competitor profile
get source metadata
get prior findings
get daily run context
```

---

# 11. Structured Output Requirements

All agent outputs must be structured.

The system should use strict JSON Schema / Zod / Pydantic-compatible schemas for agent outputs wherever possible.

Structured outputs are required because:

```text id="structured_output_required_because"
agent output must be machine-validated
candidate findings must be safely persisted
severity and confidence must be typed
product mappings must be inspectable
report generation needs predictable fields
evals need deterministic comparison
```

---

## 11.1 Standard Agent Output Envelope

```json id="standard_agent_output_envelope"
{
  "agent_name": "",
  "agent_version": "",
  "prompt_version": "",
  "model": "",
  "run_id": "",
  "evidence_ids": [],
  "output_type": "",
  "status": "valid",
  "confidence_label": "medium",
  "summary": "",
  "structured_payload": {},
  "caveats": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "requires_review": false,
  "created_at": ""
}
```

---

## 11.2 Invalid Output Behavior

If agent output does not match schema:

```text id="invalid_output_behavior_runtime"
1. Attempt one JSON/schema repair using a repair model route.
2. Validate repaired output.
3. If still invalid, mark agent task failed.
4. Do not create candidate finding.
5. Create run warning.
6. Create eval candidate if failure is recurring or critical.
```

---

## 11.3 Strict Schema Rule

Agents must not return freeform output for core workflows.

Freeform text may exist only inside typed fields such as:

```text id="freeform_allowed_fields"
summary
why_it_matters
rationale
recommended_action
caveat
```

---

# 13. Model Routing Strategy

## 13.1 Model Route Names

Use named routes rather than hardcoding model names in every agent.

```text id="model_route_names"
fast_classification
standard_analysis
deep_analysis
strategic_synthesis
json_repair
report_writing
eval_grading
ask_war_room
```

## 13.2 Model Route Object

```json id="model_route_object"
{
  "route_name": "deep_analysis",
  "primary_model": "configured_in_env",
  "fallback_model": "configured_in_env",

  "temperature": 0.1,
  "max_output_tokens": 4000,

  "use_cases": [
    "strategic product mapping",
    "orchestrator routing",
    "severity scoring"
  ]
}
```

---

## 13.3 Recommended Route Use

| Route               | Use For                                     | Temperature |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------: |
| fast_classification | trivial change, source type, relevance gate |         0.0 |
| standard_analysis   | specialist evidence analysis                |         0.1 |
| deep_analysis       | complex competitive interpretation          |         0.1 |
| strategic_synthesis | daily brief strategic read, CEO draft       |         0.2 |
| json_repair         | schema repair only                          |         0.0 |
| report_writing      | daily brief, battlecard drafts              |         0.2 |
| eval_grading        | subjective quality grading                  |         0.0 |
| ask_war_room        | evidence-grounded Q&A                       |         0.1 |

---

## 13.4 Model Routing Rules

```text id="model_routing_rules"
Use fast_classification before expensive analysis.
Use standard_analysis for most specialist agents.
Use deep_analysis for Orchestrator, Product Mapper, Severity Scorer, and complex findings.
Use strategic_synthesis for Daily Brief Agent and CEO Alert Drafting Agent.
Use json_repair only after schema validation failure.
Use eval_grading only for eval workflows.
Do not use high-reasoning routes for trivial changes.
Do not run agents on evidence that fails compliance.
```

---

# 14. Context Builder

## 14.1 Purpose

The Context Builder prepares the minimum necessary context for each agent.

It should avoid dumping the entire database into every prompt.

---

## 14.2 Context Builder Inputs

```text id="context_builder_inputs_runtime"
evidence_id
competitor_id
source_id
run_id
agent_name
requested_context_profile
```

## 14.3 Context Profiles

```text id="context_profiles"
news_pr_context

case_study_context
```

```json id="standard_context_packet"
{

    "run_id": "",
```

---

## 14.5 Context Minimization Rule

The agent should receive only:

```text id="context_minimization_rule_runtime"
the evidence being analyzed
the competitor profile
the relevant Doceree products
the relevant product keywords and negative keywords
relevant prior findings
the output schema
the specific task instructions
```

Do not include:

```text id="context_do_not_include"
all products unnecessarily
all competitors unnecessarily
raw HTML unless required
secrets
credentials
irrelevant internal documents
unapproved Doceree claims
```

---

# 15. Agent Execution Flow

## 15.1 Specialist Agent Flow

```text id="specialist_agent_execution_flow"
1. Evidence enters evidence_analysis_queue.
2. AgentBatchService selects recommended agent.
3. AgentRunnerService loads agent registry.
4. AgentRunnerService loads prompt version.
5. ContextBuilder builds context packet.
6. AgentToolPolicyService loads allowed tools.
7. Input guardrails run.
8. Agent executes through Agents SDK or Responses API route.
9. Tool calls are validated and logged.
10. Output guardrails run.
11. Structured output is validated.
12. Agent output is stored.
13. Candidate finding is created if valid.
14. Governance agents run.
15. Orchestrator routes.
```

---

## 15.2 Orchestrator Flow

```text id="orchestrator_execution_flow"
1. Load candidate findings.
2. Load evidence validation result.
3. Load source compliance result.
4. Load product mapping result.
5. Load severity and confidence results.
6. Load overclaiming result.
7. Load duplicate detection result.
8. Decide route.
9. Finalize finding only if allowed.
10. Create review item if needed.
11. Create battlecard candidate if needed.
12. Create alert candidate if needed.
13. Store Orchestrator output.
14. Log trace and audit-sensitive actions.
```

---

## 15.3 Reporting Agent Flow

```text id="reporting_agent_execution_flow"
1. Load final findings for run.
2. Load review queues.
3. Load source failures.
4. Load low-confidence findings.
5. Load evidence appendix.
6. Draft structured daily brief.
7. Validate report governance.
8. Generate PDF through report service.
9. Email through email service if allowed.
10. Store notification event.
```

---

# 16. Guardrails

OpenAI guardrails should be used together with service-layer guardrails. Agent-level guardrails help validate inputs and final outputs, while tool guardrails are required around every function-tool invocation that can create side effects.

---

## 16.1 Input Guardrails

Input guardrails should check:

```text id="input_guardrails_runtime"
evidence exists
evidence has excerpt
evidence source is compliant
evidence has no unresolved PHI flag
source content includes no active prompt injection instruction
agent is allowed to analyze evidence type
context packet does not contain secrets
```

---

## 16.2 Output Guardrails

Output guardrails should check:

```text id="output_guardrails_runtime"
output matches schema
evidence_ids are present
severity is 1–5
confidence label is valid
job posting is not stated as product launch
social evidence is caveated
low confidence is labeled
no unsupported Doceree claim is used
no blocked evidence is cited
no raw prompt or secret is exposed
```

---

## 16.3 Tool Guardrails

Tool guardrails should check:

```text id="tool_guardrails_runtime"
agent is allowed to call tool
tool input schema validates
tool side-effect level is allowed
safe mode status permits tool
human approval exists if required
tool output schema validates
tool did not return secrets
```

---

## 16.4 Prompt Injection Guardrail

If source text includes instruction-like attacks, the system should:

```text id="prompt_injection_guardrail_runtime"
treat source text as data only
ignore source instructions
flag prompt_injection_suspected
preserve evidence
not lower citation requirements
not change schema
not mark Severity 5 because the page says so
```

---

# 17. Handoffs and Agents-as-Tools

## 17.1 Manager Pattern

The Orchestrator should use manager-style orchestration for daily runs.

Pattern:

```text id="manager_pattern_runtime"
Orchestrator calls specialist outputs as tools or reads their stored outputs.
Specialists do not directly hand off to each other for finalization.
Orchestrator owns final routing.
```

---

## 17.2 Handoff Pattern

Use handoffs only when:

```text id="handoff_pattern_use"
interactive Ask War Room needs to transfer to a specialist
manual review assistant needs a specialist clarification
complex evidence analysis needs a nested specialist
```

---

## 17.3 Agents-as-Tools

Use agents-as-tools for:

```text id="agents_as_tools_use"
Product Mapper
Severity Scorer
Confidence Scorer
Overclaiming Guardrail
Duplicate Detector
Source Compliance Guardrail
```

These tool-agents should return structured outputs only.

---

# 18. Session and Memory Strategy

## 18.1 Daily Runs Are Mostly Stateless

Daily run agents should not rely on conversational memory.

They should rely on:

```text id="daily_run_state_source"
database records
evidence
source snapshots
product spine
competitor registry
prior findings
run context
```

---

## 18.2 Ask War Room May Use Sessions

Ask War Room may use session memory for:

```text id="ask_war_room_session_memory"
conversation continuity
follow-up question resolution
active filters
previous evidence references
```

But it must always ground answers in retrieved command center data.

---

## 18.3 No Hidden Long-Term Agent Memory

Agents should not create unreviewed hidden long-term memory.

Long-term knowledge belongs in:

```text id="long_term_knowledge_locations"
Product Spine tables
Competitor Registry
Source Registry
Evidence Vault
Findings
Human Reviews
Prompt Registry
Eval Dataset
```

---

# 19. Tracing Specification

## 19.1 Purpose

Every agent run should be traceable.

Tracing is required for:

```text id="tracing_required_for"
debugging
quality review
eval creation
prompt regression
cost tracking
tool-call review
source compliance review
human review explanation
production incident response
```

---

## 19.2 Trace Fields to Store

```json id="trace_fields_to_store"
{
  "trace_id": "",
  "workflow_name": "",
  "agent_run_id": "",
  "agent_name": "",
  "prompt_version": "",
  "model": "",
  "run_id": "",
  "started_at": "",
  "ended_at": "",
  "duration_ms": 0,
  "status": "",
  "tool_calls_count": 0,
  "tokens_used": 0,
  "estimated_cost": 0,
  "errors": [],
  "warnings": []
}
```

---

## 19.3 Trace Redaction

Do not send or store:

```text id="trace_redaction_do_not_store"
API keys
SMTP credentials
database URLs
passwords
session tokens
raw PHI
raw secrets
full internal prompts in user-visible UI
```

Prompt versions may be stored by ID and file path.

Raw prompt content should be visible only to Sherry/Admin in prompt-management context.

---

## 19.4 Trace UI

Agent Run Detail should show:

```text id="trace_ui_fields"
trace ID
agent name
model
prompt version
tool calls
guardrails
input evidence
output status
schema validation
tokens used
cost estimate
errors
warnings
linked findings
```

# 20. Token and Cost Tracking

## 20.1 Track Usage By

```text id="token_cost_tracking_by"
run
agent
tool call
model
prompt version
evidence item
daily brief
Ask War Room question
eval run
```

---

## 20.2 Cost Fields

```json id="cost_tracking_fields"
{
  "input_tokens": 0,
  "cached_input_tokens": 0,
  "output_tokens": 0,
  "reasoning_tokens": 0,
  "total_tokens": 0,
  "estimated_cost": 0,
  "model": "",
  "route_name": ""
}
```

---

## 20.3 Cost Guardrails

Even if token usage is not a concern, the system should prevent waste.

```text id="cost_guardrails_runtime"
do not analyze trivial changes
deduplicate news before deep analysis
use fast model for simple classification
batch low-priority evidence
limit retries
flag unusually expensive runs
track cost per valid finding
```

---

# 21. Error Handling

## 21.1 Retryable Agent Errors

Retry once for:

```text id="retryable_agent_errors_runtime"
temporary OpenAI API error
timeout
rate limit
invalid JSON
schema repairable output
temporary tool error
```

---

## 21.2 Non-Retryable Agent Errors

Do not retry:

```text id="non_retryable_agent_errors_runtime"
evidence compliance blocked
possible PHI
tool permission denied
human approval missing
source policy blocked
invalid agent registration
missing prompt version
unsupported output schema
safe mode blocking execution
```

---

## 21.3 Agent Failure Behavior

```text id="agent_failure_behavior_runtime"
mark agent task failed
store error
create run warning or error
do not create final finding
do not hide failure from daily brief if relevant
create eval candidate for recurring failure
```

---

# 22. Long-Running Runs and Background Work

Daily runs may involve many sources and many evidence items.

The system should run these through:

```text id="long_running_runtime"
worker process
agent batch queue
run state machine
background model responses where appropriate
stored run status
stored trace IDs
cancel support where safe
```

Do not depend on:

```text id="long_running_do_not_depend"
browser tab
single HTTP request
manual ChatGPT session
unpersisted memory
```

---

# 32. Critical Runtime Guardrails

The agent runtime must enforce:

```text id="critical_runtime_guardrails"
No agent runs on non-compliant evidence.
No agent runs on possible PHI.
No specialist agent creates final finding.
No agent sends email.
No agent sends CEO or Sales alert.
No agent publishes battlecard.
No agent changes source policy.
No agent changes permissions.
No agent activates prompt without eval pass and approval.
No output persists without schema validation.
No final finding persists without evidence validation.
No report removes low-confidence caveats.
No tool call bypasses AgentToolPolicyService.
No secrets enter context packets.
No source prompt injection instruction is followed.
```

This section is complete when the product supports the following:

1. Agent registry exists.
2. Tool registry exists.
3. Agent tool permissions exist.
4. Model routes exist.
5. Prompt registry is connected to agents.
6. OpenAIClientFactory exists.
7. AgentContextBuilder exists.
8. AgentToolPolicyService exists.
9. AgentRunnerService exists.
10. AgentOutputValidator exists.
11. Structured outputs are required for core agents.
12. Invalid output does not create candidate findings.
13. One JSON/schema repair attempt exists.
14. Input guardrails exist.
15. Output guardrails exist.
16. Tool guardrails exist.
17. Prompt injection guardrail exists.
18. Specialist agents cannot create final findings.
19. Agents cannot send emails.
20. Agents cannot send CEO alerts.
21. Agents cannot send Sales alerts.
22. Agents cannot publish battlecards.
23. Agents cannot change source policy.
24. Agents cannot change permissions.
25. Agents cannot activate prompts.
26. Agents cannot delete artifacts.
27. Orchestrator can finalize only through service-layer validation.
28. Daily Brief Agent preserves warnings and caveats.
29. Ask War Room cites evidence and says no evidence when appropriate.
30. Model routing works by task type.
31. Fast route handles trivial classification.
32. Deep route handles Orchestrator and complex reasoning.
33. JSON repair route handles repair only.
34. Agent traces are stored.
35. Tool calls are stored.
36. Guardrail results are stored.
37. Token and cost records are stored.
38. Trace UI exists.
39. Agent settings UI exists.
40. Prompt activation requires eval pass and Sherry/Admin approval.
41. Tests cover tool permissions, model routing, output validation, prompt injection, tracing, and Orchestrator finalization.


# Section X+30 — Testing, QA, CI/CD, and Release Gates

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the full testing, QA, CI/CD, release-gate, regression, eval, and production-readiness strategy for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

The system will run autonomous crawlers, OpenAI agents, source-policy checks, evidence validation, product mapping, severity scoring, report generation, PDF creation, email delivery, review queues, alerts, battlecards, backups, and retention jobs.

Because the product is autonomous, the test system must be strict.

The command center must not ship with weak guardrails.

The core principle is:

> If a failure can damage trust, create unsupported intelligence, crawl the wrong source, send the wrong alert, hide low confidence, lose evidence, or break Sherry’s daily brief — it must be tested before release.

---

## 2. QA Philosophy

The command center should be tested like a business-critical intelligence system, not like a casual dashboard.

Testing must prove that the system is:

```text
accurate
evidence-backed
source-compliant
permission-safe
agent-safe
report-safe
scheduler-safe
recoverable
observable
auditable
````

The QA goal is not merely:

```text
Does the app run?
```

The QA goal is:

```text id="qa_goal"
Can Sherry trust this system to independently monitor competitors, create evidence-backed findings, route high-risk intelligence for review, generate the daily brief, and avoid unsafe actions?
```

---

# 3. Testing Principles

## 3.1 Evidence Integrity Over UI Polish

The most important tests are not visual tests.

The most important tests prove:

```text id="evidence_integrity_tests"
no final finding without evidence
no unsupported competitor claim
no non-compliant evidence in final findings
no missing source URL
no missing captured timestamp
no hidden low-confidence caveat
no source failure suppressed
```

---

## 3.2 Source Policy Must Fail Closed

If source policy is uncertain, the system should block automation.

Tests must prove:

```text id="source_policy_fail_closed_tests"
manual-only sources are not crawled
blocked sources are not crawled
LinkedIn/social sources are not browser-crawled
analyst reports are manual-upload only
gated webinars are manual-upload only
unknown access basis blocks restricted collection
needs_source_discovery rows do not enter scheduler
```

---

## 3.3 Agents Must Be Boxed In

Agents must not be able to bypass services.

Tests must prove:

```text id="agent_box_tests"
specialist agents cannot create final findings
agents cannot send email
agents cannot send CEO/Sales alerts
agents cannot change source policy
agents cannot change permissions
agents cannot publish battlecards
agents cannot activate prompts
invalid outputs do not persist
```

---

## 3.4 Reports Must Preserve Caveats

Reports are decision documents.

Tests must prove:

```text id="report_caveat_tests"
daily brief includes source failures
daily brief includes low-confidence findings
daily brief includes evidence appendix
daily brief does not include blocked evidence
PDF does not expose secrets
email does not claim success when delivery fails
```

---

## 3.5 Release Gates Must Be Automated

Codex should not rely on manual confidence.

Every build milestone should have automated checks.

```text id="automated_release_gates"
lint
typecheck
schema validation
unit tests
integration tests
E2E tests
agent evals
source policy tests
security tests
migration tests
backup tests
release readiness checks
```

---

# 4. Test Pyramid

The system should use a layered test strategy.

```text id="test_pyramid"
1. Static checks
2. Unit tests
3. Contract tests
4. Integration tests
5. E2E tests
6. Agent evals
7. Golden dataset regression
8. Release-gate checks
9. Production smoke tests
10. Restore and disaster-recovery drills
```

---

## 4.1 Static Checks

Static checks should run on every commit.

```text id="static_checks"
TypeScript typecheck
ESLint
Prettier / formatter check
Prisma schema validation
Zod schema compilation
environment variable validation
dependency vulnerability scan
dead route scan if possible
```

---

## 4.2 Unit Tests

Unit tests validate isolated business logic.

Examples:

```text id="unit_test_examples"
SourcePolicyResolver
EvidenceValidationService
FindingService guardrails
AgentToolPolicyService
ModelRouteService
ReportValidationService
RetentionPolicyService
PermissionService
```

---

## 4.3 Contract Tests

Contract tests validate schema boundaries.

Examples:

```text id="contract_test_examples"
API request schema
API response schema
agent output schema
tool input schema
tool output schema
crawler output contract
PDF export object contract
notification event contract
```

---

## 4.4 Integration Tests

Integration tests validate multiple services working together.

Examples:

```text id="integration_test_examples"
crawler creates snapshot and evidence
evidence enters agent queue
agent creates candidate finding
orchestrator finalizes finding
daily run generates PDF and email event
retention expires artifacts but preserves metadata
```

---

## 4.5 E2E Tests

E2E tests validate user journeys.

Examples:

```text id="e2e_test_examples"
Sherry runs Day-1 baseline
Sherry sees source snapshots
Sherry reviews Severity 4 finding
Sherry approves battlecard task
Sherry opens daily brief PDF
Reader cannot approve finding
```

---

## 4.6 Agent Evals

Agent evals validate AI reasoning quality.

They are not replacements for software tests.

They measure:

```text id="agent_eval_measures"
product mapping accuracy
severity accuracy
confidence calibration
overclaiming control
source interpretation quality
battlecard recommendation quality
daily brief usefulness
Ask War Room grounding
```

---

# 5. Testing Tools

## 5.1 Recommended Test Stack

```text id="recommended_test_stack"
Unit / integration tests: Vitest
React component tests: Testing Library
E2E tests: Playwright
API contract validation: Zod
Database testing: Prisma + isolated test database
Mocking: MSW or custom service mocks
Email testing: Mailhog / mocked SMTP provider
PDF testing: Playwright PDF smoke tests
Agent evals: custom eval runner + golden examples
CI: GitHub Actions
```

---

## 5.2 Test Database

Use a dedicated test database.

```text id="test_database"
DATABASE_URL_TEST=postgresql://doceree_ci_test:password@localhost:5432/doceree_ci_test
```

Rules:

```text id="test_db_rules"
never run tests against production database
reset test database before integration suite
seed only minimal deterministic data
use fixtures for crawled pages
mock external APIs by default
```

# 6. Test Environments

## 6.1 Environment Matrix

| Environment | Purpose                    | Database   | Email          | Crawler         | OpenAI         | Scheduler |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | -------------- | --------------- | -------------- | --------- |
| local_dev   | Build locally              | local      | Mailhog/test   | real or fixture | real or mocked | optional  |
| test        | Automated tests            | test DB    | mocked         | fixtures        | mocked         | disabled  |
| dry_run     | Safe workflow testing      | sandbox    | disabled       | real limited    | real           | manual    |
| staging     | Production-like validation | staging    | test recipient | real            | real           | optional  |
| production  | Live operation             | production | Sherry         | real            | real           | enabled   |

# 7. Critical Guardrail Test Suite

This is the most important test suite.

It must run in every CI build.

## 7.1 Evidence Guardrails

```text id="critical_evidence_guardrail_tests"
FindingService blocks final finding without evidence.
FindingService blocks final finding with non-compliant evidence.
FindingService blocks final finding if evidence has no excerpt.
FindingService blocks final finding if evidence has no source URL.
FindingService blocks final finding if evidence has no captured timestamp.
EvidenceService blocks raw evidence field updates.
EvidenceGovernanceService blocks possible PHI from agent queue.
ReportGovernanceService excludes blocked evidence from reports.
```

---

## 7.2 Source Policy Guardrails

```text id="critical_source_policy_guardrail_tests"
SourcePolicyResolver blocks manual-only source.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks blocked source.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks needs-review source.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks LinkedIn company page crawler.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks executive LinkedIn profile crawler.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks analyst report automation.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks gated webinar automation.
SourcePolicyResolver blocks unknown-access restricted source.
CrawlerService refuses blocked policy decision.
Day-1 scheduler excludes needs_source_discovery rows.
```

---

## 7.3 Agent Tool Guardrails

```text id="critical_agent_tool_guardrail_tests"
Specialist agent cannot call finalize_finding.
Specialist agent cannot call send_email.
Specialist agent cannot call send_alert.
Specialist agent cannot call publish_battlecard.
Specialist agent cannot call change_source_policy.
Specialist agent cannot call manage_permissions.
Orchestrator cannot send CEO alert.
Orchestrator cannot publish battlecard.
Invalid agent output does not create candidate finding.
Prompt injection text is treated as source data only.
```

---

## 7.4 Approval Gate Guardrails

```text id="critical_approval_gate_tests"
CEO alert cannot send without Sherry approval.
Sales alert cannot send without Sherry approval.
Battlecard task cannot publish without Sherry approval.
Severity 5 alert candidate routes to review.
Prompt version cannot activate without eval pass.
Reader cannot approve finding through API.
Reader cannot send alert through API.
Reader cannot edit source through API.
```

---

## 7.5 Report Guardrails

```text id="critical_report_guardrail_tests"
Daily brief includes source failures.
Daily brief includes low-confidence findings.
Daily brief includes evidence appendix.
Daily brief includes run metadata.
PDF excludes secrets.
PDF excludes raw prompts.
PDF excludes possible PHI.

PDF failure is visible in dashboard.
```

# 9. Agent Eval Framework

## 9.1 Purpose

Software tests prove the system behaves safely.

Agent evals prove the AI behaves intelligently.

Both are required.

Agent evals should test:

```text id="agent_eval_targets"
Website Change Hunter
News / PR Agent
Jobs Signal Agent
Product Mapper
Severity Scorer
Confidence Scorer
Overclaiming Guardrail
Duplicate Detector
Orchestrator
Daily Brief Agent
Ask War Room
```

---

## 9.2 Eval Types

```text id="agent_eval_types"
golden_exact
rubric_scored
classification_accuracy
severity_accuracy
confidence_calibration
product_mapping_accuracy
overclaiming_detection
grounding_quality
citation_quality
routing_quality
daily_brief_quality
```

---

## 9.3 Golden Dataset Minimum

Before MVP release, create at least:

```text id="golden_dataset_minimum"
10 website-change examples
10 news / PR examples
10 jobs-signal examples
10 product-mapping examples
10 severity-scoring examples
10 confidence-scoring examples
10 overclaiming examples
10 duplicate-detection examples
10 daily-brief examples
10 Ask War Room examples
```

Minimum total:

```text id="golden_dataset_min_total"
100 golden examples
```

---

## 9.4 Eval Pass Thresholds

MVP minimum thresholds:

```text id="eval_pass_thresholds"
Product mapping accuracy >= 80%
Severity accuracy >= 75%
Confidence calibration >= 75%
Overclaiming detection >= 90%
Evidence citation presence = 100%
No unsupported final claims = 100%
No blocked evidence used = 100%
No PHI included in report = 100%
```

---

## 9.5 Critical Eval Failures

A single critical eval failure blocks release.

Critical failures:

```text id="critical_eval_failures"
uses blocked evidence
creates finding with no evidence
states job posting as product launch
states social post as confirmed capability
uses needs-confirmation Doceree claim as approved claim
sends or recommends sending CEO/Sales alert without approval
omits source URL or captured date
hides low confidence
removes source failure warning from report
```

## 13.1 Local MVP Release Gate

Local MVP cannot be considered complete unless:

```text id="local_mvp_release_gate"
repo starts locally
database migrates
seed runs
Sherry admin exists
Product Spine seed exists
source registry seed exists
MVP 50-source cohort seed exists
Day-1 baseline fixture run works
crawler fixtures pass
evidence guardrails pass
source policy guardrails pass
agent tool guardrails pass
daily brief fixture generation works
PDF smoke test passes
email mock test passes
backup and restore test passes
```

---

## 13.2 Internal Alpha Gate

Internal alpha begins when:

```text id="internal_alpha_gate"
Local MVP gate passes
UI shell exists
Source Registry UI exists
Evidence Vault UI exists
Findings UI exists
Agent Runs UI exists
Daily Brief UI exists
manual Day-1 baseline run works
manual daily run works on fixtures
no critical guardrail failures
```

---

## 13.3 Beta Gate

Beta begins when:

```text id="beta_gate"
7 successful local daily runs
daily brief email success >= 95%
PDF generation success >= 95%
Priority 1 source failures are visible
Sherry can approve/reject findings
battlecard candidates route correctly
CEO/Sales alerts require approval
golden evals pass
source policy tests pass
backup restore drill passes
```

---

## 13.4 Production Gate

Production cannot launch unless:

```text id="production_release_gate"
all CI checks pass
all critical guardrail tests pass
all golden evals pass
database migration validated in staging
backup verified
restore drill passed
safe mode works
worker heartbeat works
daily run lock works
staging daily run succeeds
staging PDF/email succeeds
Sherry approves production readiness
rollback plan exists
```

```text id="release_blockers"
final finding can be created without evidence
non-compliant evidence can support final finding
manual-only source can be crawled
LinkedIn/social crawler source is allowed
agent can send email
agent can send CEO/Sales alert
reader can approve finding
Severity 5 alert can send without approval
daily brief hides source failures
PDF exposes secrets
backup verification fails
restore fails
golden eval critical failure
database migration fails
typecheck fails
unit tests fail
security tests fail
```

# Section X+31 — MVP Scope Lock, V1 Scope, V2 Scope, and Explicit Non-Goals

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section freezes the build scope for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center before Codex implementation begins.

The product is intentionally ambitious. Without a scope lock, Codex may try to build everything at once, which would create risk across architecture, testing, agent quality, source compliance, UI completeness, and delivery speed.

The core principle is:

> Build the smallest complete autonomous command center that can run daily, collect approved evidence, analyze meaningful competitor signals, route findings through guardrails, generate a PDF brief, email Sherry, and make every claim traceable.

The MVP is not a demo.

The MVP is a functioning local-first competitive intelligence system.

However, the MVP should not attempt every possible channel, every possible source, every advanced integration, or every enterprise deployment option on Day 1.

---

## 2. Scope Philosophy

The product should be built in four controlled layers.

```text
MVP: Local autonomous command center with approved sources, evidence, agents, daily brief, PDF, email, review queues, and core governance.

V1: Hardened production-ready system with broader source coverage, stronger UI workflows, more evals, deeper analytics, and hosted deployment.

V2: Expanded intelligence platform with approved social/vendor integrations, paid media, analyst/manual intelligence, advanced trend detection, and broader stakeholder distribution.

V3 / Future: Enterprise-grade strategic intelligence suite with advanced predictive analytics, integrations into CRM/Sales Enablement systems, multi-region deployment, advanced workflows, and expanded automation.
````

The MVP should prove:

```text id="mvp_should_prove"
The system can run independently.
The system can collect evidence safely.
The system can detect meaningful competitor change.
The system can analyze evidence with agents.
The system can create source-backed findings.
The system can keep low-confidence and high-risk findings reviewable.
The system can generate and email a useful daily brief.
The system can expose failures instead of hiding them.
The system can be backed up and restored.
The system can be tested and trusted.
```

---

# 3. MVP Definition

## 3.1 MVP Statement

The MVP is:

```text id="mvp_definition"
A local-first autonomous competitive intelligence command center for Sherry that monitors the approved Day-1 competitor source cohort, creates evidence-backed findings, routes high-risk findings to review, generates a daily PDF brief, emails it to Sherry, and displays all activity in a dashboard-first UI.
```

The MVP is not:

```text id="mvp_is_not"
a fully enterprise-hosted product
a broad social listening platform
a generalized web scraping system
a replacement for every manual PMM task
a sales content management system
a BI warehouse
a CRM integration layer
a public-facing intelligence portal
```

---

## 3.2 MVP Success Criteria

The MVP succeeds when Sherry can say:

```text id="mvp_success_statement"
Every morning, I get a reliable, evidence-backed competitive intelligence brief. I can see what changed, why it matters, what evidence supports it, which Doceree products are affected, what needs review, and what failed.
```

---

# 5. MVP Product Scope

## 5.1 MVP User Scope

MVP users:

```text id="mvp_users"
Sherry George — Owner/Admin
Reader user — optional test user for permission validation
```

MVP does not need full organizational rollout.

MVP does need permission architecture so that future users can be added safely.

---

## 5.2 MVP Primary User Journey

The MVP must support this daily journey:

```text id="mvp_primary_user_journey"
1. System runs daily at 6:00 AM America/New_York.
2. System checks approved Day-1 sources.
3. System creates snapshots and diffs.
4. System creates evidence for meaningful changes.
5. System routes evidence to specialist agents.
6. Governance agents validate interpretation.
7. Orchestrator creates final findings or review items.
8. Daily Brief Agent creates report data.
9. PDF is generated.
10. Email is sent to Sherry.
11. Sherry opens dashboard.
12. Sherry reviews findings, warnings, and source failures.
13. Sherry approves, rejects, edits, or requests more evidence.
```

---

# 6. MVP Source Scope

## 6.1 Included Source Scope

MVP includes only:

```text id="mvp_included_sources"
approved Day-1 source registry rows
approved public competitor websites

approved product pages
approved solution pages
approved newsroom pages
approved press release pages
approved blogs
approved careers pages

approved public partner / integration pages if included in Day-1 registry
manual uploads with access basis
```

---

## 6.2 Day-1 MVP Cohort

The MVP must load the 50-source cohort from the Competitor & Source Registry into the scheduler on Day 1.

Rule:

```text id="mvp_50_source_rule"
Only the 50-source MVP cohort is scheduled by default. All post-MVP sources remain inactive unless Sherry manually promotes them.
```

The source registry explicitly says the 50-URL MVP cohort should be loaded into the scheduler on Day 1 and that everything else is post-MVP. 

---

## 6.3 MVP Excluded Source Scope

MVP excludes automated collection from:

```text id="mvp_excluded_sources"
LinkedIn company pages
executive LinkedIn profiles
private social platforms
restricted social platforms without approved API/vendor/manual export
analyst reports through automation
gated webinars through automation
paid reports through automation
login-required portals
paywalled sources with unknown access basis
CAPTCHA-gated sources
private groups
contact databases
review sites unless specifically approved
patent databases
trademark databases
podcast/video sources
ad libraries
```

The Source Registry requires validation to prevent unsupported source types and unauthorized scraping, including blocking LinkedIn/social crawler attempts and treating analyst reports or gated webinars as manual-upload only.

# Section X+32 — Final Build Sequence, Milestones, and Codex Execution Plan

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section defines the exact build sequence for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

This is the transition point from product specification to engineering execution.

The purpose is to tell Codex:

```text
what to build first
what to build second
what not to build yet
what must be real
what may be scaffolded
what must be tested before moving forward
what counts as done
where to stop
````

The core principle is:

> Codex should build in controlled milestones, not one giant uncontrolled repo generation.

The product is too important and too large to build all at once.

Codex should build the system like this:

```text
Foundation first.
Database second.
Seed data third.
Backend services fourth.
UI shell fifth.
Crawler sixth.
Evidence seventh.
Agents eighth.
Daily run ninth.
Reports tenth.
Security and QA throughout.
```

---

## 2. Build Philosophy

Codex should follow five build principles.

```text id="build_philosophy"
1. Build vertically usable slices.
2. Commit after each milestone.
3. Run tests after each milestone.
4. Keep post-MVP features scaffolded but inactive.
5. Never bypass guardrails to make a demo work.
```

The goal is not to make the UI look impressive first.

The goal is to build the trust engine first:

```text id="trust_engine_order"
source registry
source policy
crawler
snapshots
evidence
agent validation
findings
review
reports
email
```

The UI should expose truth. It should not hide missing backend capability.

---

# 3. Codex Operating Rules

## 3.1 Codex Must Work Stepwise

Codex must not attempt to build the entire system in one prompt.

Each Codex task should:

```text id="codex_task_rules"
touch a bounded set of files
produce a working checkpoint
include tests or test scaffolds
explain files changed
explain how to verify
not silently skip core requirements
not activate post-MVP features
```

---

## 3.2 Codex Must Preserve Scope Lock

Codex must obey the MVP Scope Lock.

Codex must not build:

```text id="codex_scope_do_not_build"
LinkedIn scraping
social profile scraping
gated webinar scraping
paywall bypassing
CEO auto-send
Sales auto-send
external battlecard publishing
CRM integration
Slack / Teams distribution
full cloud production deployment before local MVP
advanced analytics before evidence loop works
```

---

## 3.3 Codex Must Prefer Working Milestones Over Perfect Abstractions

Each milestone should leave the product runnable.

Bad pattern:

```text id="bad_codex_pattern"
generate 300 files with no working path
```

Good pattern:

```text id="good_codex_pattern"
generate core files
run typecheck
run tests
verify app boots
then proceed
```

---

## 3.4 Codex Must Not Fake Core Functionality

Codex may scaffold post-MVP integrations, but it must not fake MVP functionality.

Real in MVP:

```text id="codex_must_make_real"
database
seed data
source policy validation
crawler baseline
snapshot creation
diff engine
evidence vault
agent runtime framework
finding guardrails
daily brief
PDF generation
email to Sherry
safe mode
backup / restore
critical tests
```

Scaffold only:

```text id="codex_may_scaffold"
approved social ingestion
analyst report agent
paid media agent
podcast/video agent
patent/trademark agent
CRM export
Slack/Teams integration
production cloud deployment
SSO
```

---

# 4. Repository Build Strategy

## 4.1 Recommended Repo Type

Codex should create a single monorepo-style Next.js application for MVP.

Recommended structure:

```text id="repo_strategy"
Next.js app
TypeScript
Prisma
PostgreSQL
Node worker scripts
Playwright crawler and PDF renderer
OpenAI agent runtime services
Local filesystem storage
Vitest and Playwright tests
```

Do not split into multiple repos during MVP.

Reason:

```text id="single_repo_reason"
The MVP needs speed, coherence, local-first operation, and fewer integration points.
```

---

## 4.2 Branch Strategy

Recommended branches:

```text id="branch_strategy"
main
develop
feature/milestone-XX-name
fix/bug-name
release/mvp
```

Rules:

```text id="branch_rules"
main should always be stable
develop can contain integrated milestone work
each milestone gets one feature branch
merge only after tests pass
tag major milestone completions
```

---

## 4.3 Commit Strategy

Every milestone should end with a commit.

Commit message format:

```text id="commit_message_format"
milestone-XX: short description
```

Examples:

```text id="commit_message_examples"
milestone-01: scaffold local app and docker setup
milestone-04: add source registry seed and validation
milestone-08: implement crawler baseline and snapshots
milestone-12: add agent runtime and candidate findings
```

---

# 5. Milestone Overview

The MVP should be built in **18 milestones**.

```text id="milestone_overview"
Milestone 0 — Repo and build plan initialization
Milestone 1 — Local app scaffold and environment
Milestone 2 — Database, Prisma, migrations, and base schema
Milestone 3 — Product Spine seed
Milestone 4 — Competitor and Source Registry seed
Milestone 5 — Identity, permissions, security, and audit foundation
Milestone 6 — App shell and dashboard navigation
Milestone 7 — Product, competitor, and source registry UI
Milestone 8 — Crawler, baseline snapshots, and source health
Milestone 9 — Diff engine and evidence creation
Milestone 10 — Evidence Vault and evidence governance
Milestone 11 — Findings, product mapping, and review workflow
Milestone 12 — OpenAI agent runtime foundation
Milestone 13 — Specialist agents, governance agents, and Orchestrator
Milestone 14 — Daily run state machine and scheduler
Milestone 15 — Daily brief, PDF generation, and email delivery
Milestone 16 — Evals, QA, release gates, and critical tests
Milestone 17 — Backups, restore, safe mode, and local operations
Milestone 18 — MVP hardening, smoke test, and Sherry acceptance
```

---

# Section X+33 — Codex Prompt Pack: Step-by-Step Build Prompts

## 1. Purpose of This Section

This section contains the exact prompt pack Sherry should give to Codex to build the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center step by step.

This is the final pre-build section.

After this section is added, the next action is no longer more specification writing.

The next action is:

```text
Start Codex build with Prompt 0.
````

The purpose of this prompt pack is to prevent Codex from trying to build the entire product in one uncontrolled pass.

Each prompt should produce:

```text
a bounded milestone
working files
verification commands
tests where relevant
a clear implementation summary
known limitations
the next recommended prompt
```

The core principle is:

> Codex should build the MVP in controlled, testable, reviewable increments.

---

# 2. How to Use This Prompt Pack

## 2.1 Execution Rule

Give Codex **one prompt at a time**.

Do not paste all prompts at once.

The correct workflow is:

```text
1. Give Codex Prompt 0.
2. Review output.
3. Run verification commands.
4. Fix issues.
5. Commit.
6. Give Codex Prompt 1.
7. Repeat.
```

---

## 2.2 Codex Must Stop After Each Prompt

At the end of each prompt, Codex must stop and report:

```text
what it built
files created
files changed
database changes
tests added
commands run
test results
known limitations
next recommended step
```

Codex should not continue into the next milestone unless Sherry explicitly says:

```text
Continue to next milestone.
```

---

## 2.3 Codex Must Not Overbuild

Codex must obey MVP scope.

Codex must not build:

```text
LinkedIn scraping
executive social profile scraping
paywall bypassing
login-wall bypassing
gated webinar scraping
CEO auto-send
Sales auto-send
external battlecard publishing
CRM integration
Slack integration
Teams integration
full cloud production deployment
SSO
advanced paid media monitoring
patent/trademark monitoring
podcast/video ingestion
```

These may be scaffolded only where explicitly requested.

---

## 2.4 Codex Must Preserve Guardrails

Codex must never weaken these rules to make a test pass:

```text
No final finding without evidence.
No non-compliant evidence in final findings.
No manual-only source crawling.
No LinkedIn/social browser crawling.
No analyst report automation.
No gated webinar automation.
No agent email sending.
No agent CEO/Sales alert sending.
No reader write access.
No hidden low-confidence labels.
No hidden source failures.
No PDF/email secrets.
No Sherry approval bypass.
```

# 3. Universal Header to Add to Every Codex Prompt

Before every milestone prompt, paste this universal header.

```text id="universal_codex_header"
You are building the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

This is a local-first autonomous competitive intelligence product for Doceree.

Primary owner:
- Sherry George
- Email: sherry.george@doceree.com
- Role: Owner/Admin

Core requirements:
1. Build stepwise.
2. Do not build the whole product at once.
3. Obey the MVP Scope Lock.
4. Use Product Spine as the source of truth for Doceree products.
5. Keep Confirmed / Inferred / Needs-confirmation claims separated.
6. Use the Competitor & Source Registry as the source of truth for competitors and sources.
7. Load the 50-source MVP monitoring cohort as Day-1 scope.
8. Keep post-MVP sources inactive unless manually promoted.
9. Enforce source policy before crawling.
10. Never crawl manual-only, blocked, needs-review, login-wall, paywall, CAPTCHA, LinkedIn/social, analyst-report, or gated-webinar sources through automation.
11. Every final finding must have compliant evidence.
12. Evidence must include source URL, captured timestamp, source type, collection method, and excerpt.
13. Agents cannot bypass backend services.
14. Specialist agents cannot create final findings.
15. Agents cannot send email, send alerts, publish battlecards, change permissions, change source policy, activate prompts, or delete artifacts.
16. CEO/Sales alerts require Sherry approval.
17. Battlecard publication requires Sherry approval.
18. Daily brief auto-sends only to Sherry.
19. Source failures and low confidence must never be hidden.
20. Add tests wherever possible.

After implementation, report:
- Summary
- Files created
- Files changed
- Migrations added
- API routes added
- UI pages added
```

# 23. Emergency Fix Prompt Template

Use this when a milestone fails.

```text id="codex_emergency_fix_prompt"
Use the universal Codex header.

Emergency Fix Request.

The previous milestone failed.

Failure summary:
[paste exact error, failing test, log output, or screenshot description]

Requirements:
1. Diagnose the root cause.
2. Do not weaken guardrails.
3. Do not delete tests to make the build pass.
4. Do not bypass source policy.
5. Do not loosen evidence requirements.
6. Do not give agents forbidden permissions.
7. Make the smallest safe fix.
8. Add or update tests if needed.
9. Rerun the relevant verification command.

After implementation:
- Explain root cause.
- List files changed.
- Show test command run.
- Show result.
- State whether the milestone can continue.
Stop.
```

# 24. Code Review Prompt Template

Use this after Codex completes each milestone.

```text id="codex_code_review_prompt"
Review the milestone implementation for the Doceree Competitive Intelligence Command Center.

Focus on:
1. MVP scope compliance.
2. Source policy guardrails.
3. Evidence integrity.
4. Product Spine claim separation.
5. Agent tool permissions.
6. Permission enforcement.
7. Audit logging.
8. Test coverage.
9. Security risks.
10. Overbuilt V1/V2 features.

Check specifically:
- Did Codex accidentally activate post-MVP sources?
- Can any final finding exist without evidence?
- Can any manual-only source be crawled?
- Can agents send emails or alerts?
- Can reader users perform writes?
- Are low-confidence labels preserved?
- Are source failures visible?
- Are secrets hidden?

Return:
1. Pass/fail.
2. Critical issues.
3. High-priority issues.
4. Medium-priority issues.
5. Suggested fixes.
6. Whether to proceed to next milestone.
```
